Andreas von Löwis of Menar was born on 4 January 1778 (at the end of 1877 according to the old calendar) at Vanamõisa in Kirbla Parish, Läänemaa, the son of a retired general. In 1794–97 he was in military service in St. Petersburg, serving as a warrant officer in the cavalry. In 1801 he went to study at Jena and in 1803 at the University of Heidelberg, and in 1806–1808 studied at the Schwetzingen Forestry Institute.

In 1811 von Löwis of Menar was elected secretary of the Livonian Public Benefit and Economic Society based in Riga. He organised its activities and was the editor of the society's publications. He subsequently moved to Tartu and probably studied art under C. A. Senff.

In 1816–39 he took part in the trigonometric survey of Livonia and the compiling of maps carried out under the direction of Friedrich Georg Wilhelm Struve.

His most important work is his own illustrated survey of the knightly castles of Livonia: Denkmäler aus der Vorzeit Liv- und Estlands I-II (1821, 1827). He died at Kaipen (Keipene) manor in Latvia/Livonia.
dd36ab042fa2f31cb9268ddb15e7dc31585b453a: Born 30.07.1947. Estonian actor and pedagogue. Father a dairyman, mother a dairy laboratory assistant. Graduated from Rakvere 1st Secondary School in 1965, studied at Tallinn Polytechnic Institute in 1965–68, and graduated from the acting department of the Tallinn State Conservatory in 1972. Worked as an actor at the Drama Theatre in 1972–75 and 1978–95, was a lecturer in theatre studies at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute in 1975–80 and at the Estonian Institute of Humanities in 1988–2004; from 1995 a teacher at the Old Town Educational Collegium and from 1997 also at its Theatre School (stage speech etc.). Wrote the play "Olevused" (1980) together with Juhan Viiding, compiled and directed as a group work "Lavakavu" (I 1982, II 1984) and the programme "Kallis õhtu" (I 1992, II 2014). Sang (together with J. Viiding and Lembit Ulfsak) in the ensemble Amor Trio, performed at the Viru Variety, played in TV productions ("Mõmmi ja aabits", 1973–77 and 1998–99) and in film ("Aeg maha!", 1975, Eesti Telefilm), took part in the concert series "Tornikell minu külas" (1979).
c4596295aa5a230ef3e2f0c6b101080b3e5917c6: Ksenia Verbeštšuk is a visual and applied artist living in Tallinn, specialising in photography, film, scenography and visual art. Her work encompasses theatre, cinema and various audiovisual projects, in which she seeks to create connections between poetry, philosophy and the realm of reality and dreams. Ksenia is passionately devoted to exploring the complexity of life and cultural narratives, often raising questions about subjective and objective perceptions. Her work has been exhibited in several galleries in Estonia and Austria, and she is actively working as a freelance artist in various projects, theatre and film sets. In 2026 she graduated from EKA (Estonian Academy of Arts) with a bachelor's degree in scenography. In addition, she has completed an exchange programme at AKBILD (Akademie der bildenden Künste Wien) in the department of scenography and performing arts, and has taken part in several international projects.
2290b3d6e1db5e3993bd9f8149edefd8bf072229: VÕERAHANSU, Johannes (1902, Keo, Raikküla Parish – 1980, Tallinn). Johannes Võerahansu is considered one of the most outstanding Estonian landscape and genre painters. His paintings from the second half of the 1930s, with their light-filled, silvery colouring poeticising Estonian life and nature, are among the top works of this genre. The artist also expressively depicted nature as the background of paintings on the theme of fieldwork made during World War II. From the beginning of his creative path, Võerahansu also cultivated portrait painting, several of which belong to the classics of Estonian portraiture. In the 1960s–1970s he moved away from painting and focused more on drawings. Võerahansu received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school and under Ado Vabbe at the Pallas Art School. He later worked as a teacher at the Higher Courses of Visual Art, at the Tartu State Art Institute, at the Tartu Art School, and as a professor at the Estonian State Art Institute. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
183825f469da2c4c525bcfa1400d7d8722c5753f: He was born in 1799 in Viljandi, the son of the tailor Friedrich Burchard Dörbeck and his mother Helena (Rakosnik), who was of Polish descent. He studied graphic art in St. Petersburg under Friedrich Neyer, and was an engraver of texts for state securities. Dörbeck's first marriage lasted from August to October 1819. In 1820–23 he lived in Riga, where he engraved visiting cards and portraits. In 1822 he made an aquatint of the Estonian K. J. Peterson. In 1823 he remarried in Riga and moved to Berlin, where he worked as a successful caricaturist (publisher Gropius). Lithograph series: Berliner Witze, Berliner Redensarten (1830), Album Academicum (1832), etc. In Berlin Dörbeck engraved portraits of Luther, Calvin and others. In 1823 his daughter Olga Helene was born, and in 1827 his son Roman Anastasius. In 1830 his second wife Jakobine died. In 1831 the artist married for the third time. In 1832 his son Franz was born. Suffering from tuberculosis, Dörbeck returned with Olga and Roman to Viljandi in 1835. He died in Viljandi. A memorial stone was unveiled to him at the Riia maantee cemetery.
5332b5aa6fb73363b70fc1b472ede91ef8a3e3ec: He finished Tallinna 22. Keskkool in 1964 and entered the University of Tartu. In autumn 1964 he was conscripted into the Soviet Army, where he served in the air force. He graduated from the university in 1971. From 1971 to 1977 he was a correspondent for the newspaper Sirp ja Vasar, and until 1980 the editor of its art and architecture pages. From 1980 to 1983 he worked at the Tallinn port customs as an expert on art and precious metals, where he helped to take abroad works and exhibitions of Estonian progressive artists who were out of favour at the time. From 1983 to 1987 he worked as artistic director of the monumental art studio at the combine ARS. From 1981 to 1985 he was compiler of the magazine Kunst ja Kodu. From 1990 to 1991 he worked as editor-in-chief of the magazine Poliitika and later at several Tallinn newspapers, at the same time writing a number of articles on contemporary art for the magazine Vikerkaar and the newspaper Eesti Aeg (under the pseudonyms Adam Krikk, Gustav Pähkel, Jürgen Rupski).
2c2d82cc6f2c24fb6895615d437c7bc7d4a7eee4: Riin Pallon (b. 1978) has studied painting (BA) and art teacher education (MA) at the Estonian Academy of Arts, and studied in Germany at the Karlsruhe Academy of Arts as an exchange student in Gustav Kluge's painting class. She currently lives and works in Rapla. She has participated in exhibitions since 2004, and after a break in exhibiting (2014-2019) for family reasons, she took part again in a large exhibition at the end of 2019. In 2010, together with another artist, she founded the Rapla County Contemporary Art Centre, where she organises exhibitions and children's art projects. She is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association. Her paintings are visually meaningful and multifaceted in content; universal human themes are connected with a personal viewpoint and experience, and a certain dose of (self-)irony can also be found in them. In many of the paintings apocalyptic freeze-frames shine through, brimming with energy and leading the viewer on a walk through poetic landscapes.
036b567daa6eb74221e8a935ebd94fc961010516: Cultural journalist, theatre critic, librettist and writer; graduated in 1926 from the Viljandi Boys' Gymnasium, studied law briefly at the University of Tartu, graduated from the Tallinn Higher Military School. Began his journalistic work in 1926 at Sakala, was editor-in-chief there (with interruptions) from 1931 to 1944 (writing mainly about Ugala productions) and administrator of Ugala in 1940-41. Promoted sport in Viljandi (swimming, tennis, aviation). Wrote the librettos for Priit Ardna's operettas "Ly", "Tütarlaps kodumaata" and "Igavene legend", plays ("Maja sadamas", 1939, "Väike rumal süda", 1940, "Kummaline võõras tuli orgu", 1948, "Rindejoonel", 1949) and memoirs ("Mu meelen...", 1963). Fled to Germany in 1944, was active in the Geislingen Estonian National Committee Theatre (a dramatisation of A. H. Tammsaare's "Põrgupõhja uue Vanapagana"), moved to the USA in 1949, worked as a deep-sea diver and fisherman. His father was a constable, later a railway official.
94fe89e692114d6b31f9743b92d19da1e5fc197c: Katrin Kabun (b. 1966) is a textile designer who lives and works in Tallinn. She graduated from Tallinn University Haapsalu College with a BA (2013, cum laude) and from the Estonian Academy of Arts with an MA (2017, cum laude), and continues her studies as a doctoral student at the Estonian Academy of Arts. For her master's thesis Katrin received the EKA Young Applied Artist Award and the award of the EKA competition for applied research and development works in the category of works improving societal well-being and/or the living environment. In her design research Katrin deals with questions of applying sheep's wool, as a valuable renewable resource, in contemporary product design. Her research is based on a certain apparent opposition — transferring the properties of sheep's wool, as an archaic material, into the language of contemporary design, and seeking, through design, means of applying the emotional and aesthetic values of wool and keeping them relevant in the context of today's sustainable design and living environment.
3e80af5f116f872df4a57186eca66d1a363faf5e: Siim Hanikat has studied at the Estonian Academy of Arts' Open Academy and at Tallinn University's Baltic Film, Media and Arts Institute. His works, which mostly depict female figures, are the artist's experiments, at various stages of the creative process, with a variety of materials and means, ranging from pencil drawing to graffiti. His works are interesting, colourful and lively. The viewer can sense how he searches for beautiful motifs and angles to turn into physical objects. Strong colours dominate his drawings, which, in addition to the charcoal-black tones used, often create a poster-like effect. It can be assumed that the colourful female figures do not wish to state a final truth — they are neither happy nor sad. Simply, on the day the work was born, they inspired the artist. The author has hidden concealed messages in the works; such hidden little messages seem to give the works a new personal dimension.
bbe84f0fa86937cbc941625aee1b78d11d856fb4: Johannes Barbarus (Johannes Vares), physician, poet and man of letters. Thanks to a successful medical practice in Pärnu he was not dependent on the support given to writers and could allow himself sharp socially critical statements. He entered literature with neo-romantic poems in the magazine "Noor-Eesti" (1910). He belonged to the "Siuru" circle; his first collections of verse are "Fata-Morgana" (1918), "Inimene ja sfinks" (1919) and "Katastroofid" (1920). Barbarus actively took part in the activities of the oppositional group "Tarapita" (1921-1922). The collection of topical poems "Vahekorrad" (1922) is influenced by Expressionism. He made an attempt to reform Estonian poetry on the French model, seeking to bring into Estonian literature fast rhythms corresponding to the advances of science and technology: the collection "Geomeetriline inimene" (1924). The collection "Multiplitseerit inimene" (1927) continues the dismantling of received truths. He is the same person as the later Soviet statesman Johannes Vares.
0fc5dd3ae9ab362f815d9540a34aee77373b5cb4: Self-taught portrait photographer from Ida-Viru. EU Commission photo competition "Mina ja Euroopa" prize place 2013 Nikon photo competition "Sõbralik Eesti" 2013 1st place Pentax portrait photo competition of the year 2015 3rd place Louvre Museum's 2015 group exhibition "Exposure awards" Sony World Photography Awards December 2015 winner Global Encounters Snapshot competition 2015 personal photo exhibition at the gallery of the University of Tartu Narva College 2016 Pentax portrait photo competition of the year 2016 2nd place Sony World Photography Awards National Awards 2nd place 2017 Sony World Photography Awards group exhibition Somerset House, London 2017 Nikon 2018 competition "Kuupilt" winner October 'What Lies Beneath' 500px group exhibition Toronto 2019 Bridgeman studio award, January 2020, 2019 shortlist Group exhibition ZE+F, Object Multimedia Future Hub, Narva 2020
cd46383a6a9a07efc9dd6c45aa7a826d32ed5ad0: In 1928 Halliste moved to Tallinn, where he worked for a year in Jaan Koort's studio, studying ceramics and bronze casting there. After leaving Koort he began earning his living by making furniture parts and engraving ornaments for a piano factory. He was a board member of the Estonian Museum Society, of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists, a member of the Board of the Fine Arts Foundation, and a member of the building committee and board of the Tallinn Art Hall. In the 1930s the artist had the opportunity to further his training through trips to Russia, Finland, Italy, France and Germany. During World War II the artist lived withdrawn from society; in the summers he stayed with his wife in Pupastvere. After the war ended the sculptor worked for some time as a restorer at the State Art Museum. The post-war years were the most productive in the artist's oeuvre; his main workplace was a studio on Lauristini Street in Tallinn.
40ab0ba0547487434b652642dacc044f9f9deb6f: He was born on 3 October 1962 in Tartu. His mother Laine Pukk (b. 1935-2023) was a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School for over 30 years. His father, Aleksander Suuman (1927-2003), was a painter and poet. The Tartu Children's Art School was followed by the Estonian State Art Institute (Estonian Academy of Arts) 1980-1986, where he studied in the graphic art speciality. Aapo has been a member of the Portrait Society of America (PSOA) since 1999 and a Signature Member since 2017. Aapo Pukk has brought home dozens of awards from international portrait competitions. A member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2011. Aapo Pukk has worked as a contracted lecturer at the Estonian Academy of Arts since 2012. Aapo is deeply engaged in teaching art and developing methodologies at his eponymous art school. Over the past 15 years Aapo has taught more than 200 courses. He himself says that he loves painting flowers and landscapes just as much as portraiture.
3e03d3ce61797d1ecf5f4eeb7f58c7bbe2825116: Gerth Kuusk is a self-taught painter who works daily as a designer. His first attempts at classical painting were made in 2012, after which the artist's ambition and artistic depth have continued to grow. In 2015 he completed the classical painting continuing-education course at the EKA Open Academy, and in 2019 the handicraft technology and design speciality at Tallinn University Haapsalu College. In his work Kuusk places at the centre states reflecting the human being and his relationship with an abstract and at times metaphysical inner world environment. Kuusk has taken part in several young art auctions and in painters' annual exhibitions in Pärnu and Tallinn. In April 2024 his first solo exhibition took place at ArtDepoo. For the latter, Kuusk involved his small children in the creative process, who, as co-authors of the works, helped bring a carefree treatment of colour and form into the paintings.
0c8c6693dfe92cbef5dec21b017caed44ef3cdea: Juhan Paberit (1917) created restless, dynamic and emotionally powerful monuments and gravestones during the 1960s–1970s. His monuments, mostly executed as reliefs, are recognisable by their beautiful painterly surface treatment. Paberit is one of the most outstanding relief sculptors in Estonia. He was predominantly a Tartu-centred artist, and thus Paberit's gravestone sculptures are largely found in Tartu's cemeteries; the monuments to those fallen in the Second World War are located in South Estonia (in Elva, Õisu, Kanepi), but also in Paide. In his portrait work he gladly used ceramics – portraits indeed form a significant part of his oeuvre – the artist's relationship to the model is usually warm and lyrical. Paberit was mobilised into the Red Army during the Second World War, began his sculpture studies in 1946 at the Tartu State Art Institute, and graduated as a sculptor from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1952.
2fa8b6a70e6723fff59af84d40225d66e75c0459: Taavi Oolberg came to painting relatively late in life, after graduating from the Tartu Art College Pallas. Before that he worked mainly as a graphic designer, illustrator and caricaturist. The greatest influence on the development of his painting has been exerted by the teachers of the Pallas era, whose work he has often referenced in his own. Particularly noticeable are his bows to Peeter Allik and Imat Suuman. Oolberg likes to organise his work into series. He also creates editioned painting prints, where each subsequent work differs slightly from the previous one, together forming what seems like an animated narrative flow. The artist considers collaboration important. He is happy to take part in joint projects and exhibitions with other creators, and he also tries to involve artist friends in his solo exhibitions. For him, sharing creative experiences and a jointly created environment makes life much more joyful and inspiring.
c5da304a1956e3d19dbeb2c2cfe0d015cfc397ad: Grigori (Georg) Tõnisson was born in Pärnu as the son of a grammar school caretaker. In 1911 his landscape vignettes and stories were printed in the Postimees supplement Sädemed, and soon his caricatures appeared in the newspapers Kilk and Meie Tallinna Ajaleht. In 1913 he moved to Tallinn and began working for the magazine Leek. In 1915 he was mobilised into the Tsarist army, and in 1915 he was taken prisoner of war by the Germans. In 1918 he returned to Tallinn and, together with Hendrik Saar (Kivilombi Ints), founded the satirical art magazine "Sipelgas" (15 issues were published), for which Gori was both a prose and picture author (in woodcut). From 1920 he was a member of the editorial board of the newspaper Vaba Maa, and in 1938 a member of the editorial board of Rahvaleht. In 1941 Gori was arrested; after his release he worked at the newspapers Rahva Hääl and Sirp ja Vasar. During the German occupation he was imprisoned twice; the artist's date of death is 7.10.1944, the cause of which (suicide?) remains unresolved. He is buried at the Tallinn Siselinna cemetery.
581fc8ad8d3f33913602c3880b6a162ad6ea4cbd: Eve Ermann (b. 1972) graduated from the EKA Department of Glass Art (1999) with a BA, followed by the EKA teacher training programme (2001). She has worked as a wall painting conservator-restorer. She completed the EKA Open Academy continuing education programme in Architectural Conservation and Restoration (2014). From 2016 she has been a member of the Estonian Watercolour Society. She has taken part in joint exhibitions, the pan-European ECWS (European Confederation of Watercolour Societies) exhibitions in Avignon, Salamanca, Kraków, Ulm, Bilbao. Also international watercolour exhibitions in Italy, in Fabriano, and in Finland, in Helsinki. She has had five solo exhibitions. She has taken part in percent-for-art competitions, among them in 2021 one of seven winning works at the art competition of the Estonian Embassy in Washington, and in 2023 third place at the art competition for the building of the Estonian Knighthood. The nature and aesthetics of her paintings have been influenced by her work on historical sites.
affb5e89d4101110357c7f8146b155a51e0a0487: She was born as the daughter of Ferdinand Zeidler, who later ran a private school in Valga. She was educated in Viipuri and at the Valga private grammar school, and passed her final examinations in Tartu in 1887. From 1889–94 she studied at A. Stieglitz's School of Technical Drawing in St Petersburg, and as the school's scholarship holder studied porcelain painting in Paris and drawing at the Académie Colarossi. In 1908 she furthered her studies in metalwork in London, Stuttgart and Vienna. She worked as a teacher at art schools in Petrograd from 1897–1918. In 1918 she settled in Tallinn. From 1919–40 she was a teacher of metal, porcelain, watercolour and drawing at the State School of Applied Art. From 1924–35 she was head of the metal workshop and particularly developed filigree technique. From 1919–31 she was also a drawing teacher at the Tallinn German private grammar school for boys. She founded her own studio. In the 1920s she belonged to ARS, from 1928–35 to EKKKÜ, from 1938–39 to EAKKK, and took part in the founding of RaKü in 1932. In 1940 she moved to Finland, in 1941 to Germany, and in 1948 to Sweden.
d8be103b38b7e38f20d994e01402fc2be231a3f0: Mart Trummal was born in 1953 in Tartu. He graduated from the University of Tartu in theoretical physics in 1976. He began painting in 2017, and since that year has taken part in five annual exhibitions of Tartu artists and fourteen group exhibitions of the Konrad Mägi Studio. The exhibition "Kaks vaadet" ["Two Views"] together with Külli Trummal at the Betti Alver Museum in Jõgeva in 2018. Solo exhibition "Alasti portreed" ["Naked Portraits"] at Promenaadiviis Gallery in Tartu in 2019. Since 2019 he has also worked with charcoal and pencil drawings. Portraits of thirteen figures of Estonian culture were used as illustrations for Hando Runnel's poetry collection "Aadamal oli seitse poega", Ilmamaa 2020. Two commissioned portraits in public space, Estonian University of Life Sciences 2021, Estonian Academy of Sciences 2022. Self-taught. As a child he received a year's worth of guidance from Silvia Jõgever and Laine Pukk, and from 2017 onward from the Konrad Mägi Studio, from Aapo Pukk and Tiit Pääsuke.
7fa56a1a8d6e23b9527dfdbcb5f0a055141da788: Alina Orav (b. 1989 in Tallinn) is a painting and painting-installation artist from Estonia who lives and works in Estonia and Canada. She is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association. She obtained a master's degree in painting from the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2017, and Alina has also furthered her studies on exchange programmes in Florence (2011–2012 at ABAF University, IT) and Vancouver (2015 at ECUAD University, CA) as well as in art practices in London (UK), Amsterdam (NL) and Volda (NO). The artist has held over 20 solo exhibitions in total: in Estonia, Vancouver (CA), Helsinki (FI), Ísafjörður (IS), and has taken part in group exhibitions in Brande (DK), Berlin (DE), Florence (IT), Helsinki (FI), Moscow (RU), Stockholm (SE), Vancouver (CA), Watford (UK), Venice (USA), Japan and Estonia. She has curated group exhibitions in Vancouver (CA, 2015) and Helsinki (FI, 2018).
687ea4f45166085a045278f20e6f1a2c0688bed1: Katariin Mudist (b. 1994) is an interdisciplinary artist who has graduated from the Department of Contemporary Art of the Estonian Academy of Arts. In 2020/21 she studied at KASK in Ghent, in 2018 she graduated from the Tartu Art College's media and advertising design programme, and furthered her studies at the Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design in Budapest. Katariin mostly works with sculpture, installation, graphic art and ceramics. An important place is held by a layer that abstracts society and its relation to the individual, which is often presented through a robust style, humour and easily relatable situations. For example, most recently at the exhibition "Nähtamatud Kohalolijad" ["Invisible Presences"], held at the EKA Gallery in July 2021, Katariin uncovered the nature of cleaning work and society's attitudes towards it. Currently the artist is working on a forthcoming exhibition at the Tartu Art House, which will take place in spring 2022.
2ab9b3edf291f916c5745af508e98804a220a500: Mari Haavel (b. 1970) is a textile artist and textile designer who lives and works in Tallinn. She has graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts' textile programme with a BA (1996). Mari Haavel has worked as a gallerist and also as a home textile designer at various Estonian companies dealing with textiles, and she continues to work in this field today. Alongside this, Mari has continuously pursued her own work as well – she has taken part and continues to take part in various textile exhibitions, including international ones, and in solo exhibitions. Her favourite techniques are silk-screen printing and tapestry. She has also been drawn to designing and making various textile products, which have today become Semimari Tekstiilid – a small studio where interior textiles and accessories are made in small editions, mostly by hand, using silk-screen printing technique, and largely from materials that are production leftovers from Estonian manufacturers.
2f120ded8ce458b7a064accf5354c31666914ada: Sten Saarits (b. 1987 in Tallinn) is an installation artist whose creative work primarily investigates the individual's relationship with materiality and self-positioning in space and in the chain of events. Sten uses various media to convey the effect of his works to the viewer. The artist mainly presents works in which he uses sound as a material to create various forms that can only be perceived acoustically. Sten Saarits has studied at the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts and at the Estonian Academy of Arts. The artist has also furthered his education through numerous international workshops and practical training. Sten Saarits has won second place (2012) and the grand prix (2013) at the Young Sculptor Award exhibition. He has also received the Eduard Wiiralt scholarship. Sten has taken part in exhibitions and group projects in Estonia, Austria, Sweden, Denmark, France and Lithuania.
c772da9318d2ab9af264fff4221183370a3bd0db: Kuno Veeber was born as the second of six sons of the Adila manor manager. He studied medicine at the University of Tartu and served as a medical orderly in the Estonian War of Independence. His art studies began in Ants Laikmaa's studio, and continued with Nikolai Triik and Jaan Koort. In 1922-1924 Veeber studied at the art school Pallas and graduated in its first class in 1924. In 1923 he stayed in Germany, in Dresden, living with the artist Magnus Zeller. In 1924-1926 he continued his studies in Paris with André Lhote, serving as the senior member of his studio. It was in Paris that Kuno Veeber's style as an artist took shape. In 1926 he married Agathe Kanto (Veeber). In 1927 Veeber spent half a year in Italy on a Cultural Endowment scholarship, copying, for example, Tintoretto in the Doge's Palace in Venice. Kuno Veeber took his own life on 1 January 1929, and is buried at Rahumäe Cemetery in Tallinn. The gravestone monument, made by Jaan Koort, has been vandalised.
3c2df8f7edc9528f734b354d3d7e83964f77001c: Timo Kähara (b. 1981) is an Estonian artist. Although he liked to draw and paint already at an early age, his life path took him away from art for a while. After finishing upper secondary school (in 2000) he wanted to enrol in an art school, but narrowly failed to get in. Instead he studied at the Estonian Maritime Academy and, after graduating (in 2006), worked for two years as a 3rd mate on cargo ships sailing the world's seas. Eventually he realised that this was not for him after all, his eyes did not light up, art still drew him. He ended his career as a seaman and tried again to get into art school, and this time he succeeded. In 2012 he graduated from the Tartu Art College (now the Pallas University of Applied Sciences) with a degree in media and advertising design. He has been engaged in creative work since then. He has participated in several solo and group exhibitions. Since 2019 he has been a member of the Tartu Artists' Union.
e4463fefbdbd0f5e74e3f116f0d85dc3e273dc88: Pille Tael was born in Estonia in 1979. In 2001 she graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in interior architecture and furniture design. In 2000 she won first place in the Riigikogu furniture design competition. In 2002, after graduating, she founded the company SAS Loft OÜ. In 2003-2005 she worked as curator of the Tallinn Botanical Garden. In 2005 she was a guest lecturer for the preparatory course in interior architecture and furniture design at the Estonian Academy of Arts. In 2006 she began building the SAS Loft studio, combining painting, graphic design, photography, animation and restoration. In 2008 she enrolled in the Master's programme in animation at the Estonian Academy of Arts. In the spring of 2009 she founded SA Jaama. The aim of SA Jaama is to restore the building of the Risti Railway Station, which was built in 1900. In 2009 she organised a memorial exhibition for Richard Sööt.
edd42b7fd1694000f43ec184b1aa7d885f8c05a0: Kaia Otstak (b. 1987 Tallinn, Estonia) is a freelance painter, an illustrator, a performance-artist and a Master of philosophy. She holds a B.A. and M.A. in Philosophy from Tallinn University. Otstak has participated in solo and group exhibitions since 2006, she has performed on an international scale, her articles have published in different special magazines and newspapers. Her main interests in her artwork are to find representation for the mysticism and to be in a dialogue with ethics. She currently lives and works in Estonia. Over the years, Kaia's paintings and drawings have changed from the more minimalistic and slightly monochrome style to more detailed and colourful style. But throughout the times her figurative paintings and graphics represent other realms or this realm with a philosophical or a spiritual touch.
9ac64c7e8814b19c055be17fb60267d5594ccde2: He entered the art world in the early 1970s, when a new aesthetic that touched all fields of art began to characterise the developing field of sculpture as well. The hyperrealism and pop art that influenced his early years of creative work merged early on with a grotesque depiction of the human figure that had already taken shape. To this day the author builds his compositions as humorous stagings. In the 1970s Mikoff's over-life-size portraits astonished the Estonian art public. He has mostly portrayed great men who reached the top of the social hierarchy; his recognisable and classically clear-lined portrait solutions always also contain something ironic. He has also created well-known public sculptures. He has contributed to a perfect play of form and the interaction of surprising materials. At present his arsenal includes dry humour, deliberately temporary materials and a constant readiness to experiment.
e1d3d308e777791a92bf75f5d2a8b126bfa8c577: ballerina, ballet master, ballet pedagogue; ENL 1940; ETL 1959; graduated from the Tallinn Russian Gymnasium; studied dance in 1921-25 at E. Litvinova's studio; in 1928-29 in Berlin with V. Gsovsky; in 1932 in Paris with O. Preobrazhenskaya and in 1934-36 in Riga and in 1943-44 at the Moscow choreography school; performed in Riga and Stockholm, was in 1925-30 a ballet soloist at the Flemish Royal Opera Theatre in Antwerp, then in Central Europe; was in 1933-35 ballet master and soloist of the Liepāja Opera Theatre; in 1937 a dance teacher at the Paris cabaret Folies Bergère and performed in 1938 with H. Fleming's troupe in Italy; was in 1940-41 ballet pedagogue and director at "Estonia" and there also in 1944-51 ballet director and ballet master, was a member of ERKA; initiated the founding of TKK, was its director in 1946-48 and 1951-65, and until 1966 a teacher of classical dance; Honoured Cultural Worker of the ESSR 1959; Soviet Estonian Prize 1948.
fa9c25edac37cc89514c3f2bf59334a180316c46: Katrin Pere (b. 1952) studied textile art at what was then ERKI (now EKA). After graduating (1977, cum laude), she has taken part in curated group exhibitions in Estonia, Finland, Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Hungary, Germany, the USA, the UK, Japan, Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, France and Italy. She works mainly with fibre materials in original technique, and has also used glass, metal, paper, water, earth, and materials derived from living nature. The artist's works can be found in the Estonian Museum of Applied Art and Design, the National Library, in public interiors and in private collections around the world. Pere has also had several solo exhibitions at the Tallinn Art Hall Gallery, in the Winter Garden of the National Opera Estonia, and at the National Library. She has been awarded the City of Stuttgart Prize (1988), the Textile Artist of the Year Award (1996, 1998, 2004, 2013) and the Kristjan Raud Art Prize of the Year (1999).
e1da43d18f40d682945f7976c992916affb6d50e: Laura Liventaal (b. 1988) is an artist and director who works mainly in the fields of sculpture, installation, performance, photography, video and documentary film. In 2007-2016 she studied philosophy at Tallinn University at Bachelor's and Master's level, and in 2020 she graduated from the Baltic Film and Media School with the experimental short documentary "Kuidas olla alasti" ("How to Be Naked"), which premiered at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival. Since 2021 she has been studying in the Master's programme in contemporary art at the Estonian Academy of Arts, and in 2022-2023 she furthered her studies in the art-espace department of ENSAD in Paris. Liventaal has taken part in exhibitions and festivals in Estonia, Finland, Sweden and France. Her central themes are body awareness, tactility, intimacy and the role of women in contemporary complexity, and she also deals with issues related to mental health through a psychoanalytic prism.
0ddf3c50bd9d8c8ad114c6126ee6e54c6931603e: Keiu Koppel (b. 1988) has graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in Jewellery and Blacksmithing (BA) and has also furthered her studies at the Escola Massana design school in Barcelona. Keiu Koppel's medium of expression is metal, but in her jewellery she also uses a whole range of other materials, from classic facet-cut precious stones to computer motherboards. Koppel's works express utopias of the future, the nodal points of physical, spiritual and virtual reality, and the place of the human being within them. In 2017 her largest solo exhibition to date, 'Lost in Details', took place at the Trofeja gallery in Berlin, and in 2018 the same exhibition was shown at the HOP gallery in Tallinn. 'Lost in Details' looks at both small and large objects, and even entire worlds, as analogies and patterns that form an orderly and logical whole out of chaos.
4c5e88a1a74348bbddb1b6ca0f8268b69cd292f8: Maryliis Teinfeldt-Grins (b. 1993) is mainly known as a textile artist and poet. In her creative work the artist focuses on the village landscape, storytelling and the Kadrina dialect, mainly practising embroidery and tapestry, and writing poetry in dialect. In her later works the artist deals with the ability to read landscape. Teinfeldt-Grins has studied at the Pallas University of Applied Sciences, at the Department of Textile Art of the Art Academy of Latvia, and is currently studying in the Master's programme in Contemporary Art at the Estonian Academy of Arts. Teinfeldt-Grins is a laureate of the Eduard Wiiralt Scholarship awarded by the Estonian Ministry of Culture, a laureate of the Adamson-Eric Scholarship, and the Estonian Textile Artists' Union's Young Textile Artist of 2019. The literary festival Prima Vista recognised the artist with an award for her literary texts "Esimene samm" ("The First Step").
0ec06f8eeceb67b9f4c3237b758fab0720bb943e: Jane Muts (b. 1984) graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting within the Fine Arts department. Jane Muts depicts primarily space within space in her works. Muts treats colour as a building material and creates an illusion of space through composition. Thick layers of pigment gradually applied to the canvas create richly textured surfaces, as a result of which the interior scenes call spatial perception into question. Her technique helps to connect areas of detail and emptiness. She has taken part in the Estonian Artists' Association's 22nd annual exhibition "Kevadnäitus 2022" (2022), the TASE'22 graduation exhibition (2022), a group exhibition of EKA painting students at the premises of the Chancellor of Justice of the Republic of Estonia (2021), the Buy Young Art exhibition in the green hall of the Telliskivi Creative City (2021), and the EKA Painting Course A,B,C…Z group exhibition on the walls of the restaurant Kärbes (2019).
fbd16f3c5c5a0314ceb269abc7437841d7d726ea: Denisa Štefanigová (b. 1995) is fresh graduates of the Estonian Academy of Arts in the Contemporary Art Department. With her last project, the Master thesis titled “Violet, show me how tender you can be? (Shades of Love & Desire & Infidelity & Truth)” she reflected on the topic of the sexual life of colors, of brushstrokes, through paintings, videos, puppets – a topic she keeps researching and working on. She previously graduated with a Bachelor degree from the University of Technology, Faculty of Fine Arts (FaVU) in Brno Czechia in 2019. Denisa has also studied in Facultad de Bellas Artes in Bilbao in 2017, and has been on artistic residency in Stuttgart in GEDOK Gallery on 2018. She is currently attending the Artist Residency Programme at Easttopics in Budapest, Hungary.
e37827d7bdf236e6d3b07dd2dc59378b56b7dcae: Maret Suurmets Kuura (b. 1982) is a painter and esteemed art teacher who lives and works in Tartu. Colours and their mutual interaction are important to the artist. Since childhood, the artist has been actively engaged in drawing and painting as well as in mimetic exploration of her surroundings. The artist graduated from the University of Tartu with a BA in painting (2004) and an MA in art teaching from the University of Tartu (2011). She began participating in exhibitions in 2000. She has organised over 30 solo exhibitions. Since 2006 she has belonged to the Tartu Artists' Association, and since 2009 she has been a member of the Estonian Painters' Association. In 2009 she received a scholarship from the Tartu Artists' Association to be an exchange artist in Tampere, Finland, and upon her return, in 2010, an exhibition titled "Made in Takahuhti" was held at the Tartu Art House. The artist's works belong to the collection of the Museum of New Art.
e28192a467af155f823e38ea21efa92238a19a67: Laivi (Laivi Suurväli, b. 1988) obtained a bachelor's degree from the fashion department of the Estonian Academy of Arts and a master's degree in fashion design from Aalto University in Helsinki. She has additionally studied fashion magazine design and advertising in London, completed a sustainable fashion summer school in Copenhagen, and interned at the fashion house of Boris Bidjan Saberi in Barcelona. In addition to group exhibitions, she has had 6 solo exhibitions over the past 2 years, the most notable of which are "Unista Edasi/Liiga Hea" at the Tartu Art Museum and "Maine igatsus: leida ja kaotada" together with Mihkel Maripuu at Hobusepea Gallery. She has recently started a new series of performative fashion installations, the first two exhibition evenings of which took place at the ARS Project Room in Tallinn. Her work is characterised by an experimental approach to textiles and clothing.
f2b4c469a31066edd56a4e24a51c3c5880c1672a: Estonian painter and graphic artist Endel KÕKS (1912, Tartu – 1983, Örebro) was, at the beginning of his artistic career, interested mainly in French painting, especially the Fauves; later he was influenced by many different artistic movements, including German Expressionism, Cubism, and Abstractionism. Since Kõks left Estonia during World War II, moods of exile are also reflected in his figurative paintings. In 1967 Kõks stayed in the USA, after which his style became clearer and grander, influences of pop art were added, and Native American subject matter became important to him. While in exile, Kõks was also intensively engaged in popularising and introducing Estonian art, publishing numerous exhibition reviews in the press. Kõks received his art education at the Pallas Art School under Ado Vabbe. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
047e57ee9ed45d18dce83de80c1409fddaa8404b: Adele Ulm-Augustas (1908–2000) graduated from the State School of Arts and Crafts in Tallinn in 1930. She studied sculpture at the Tallinn School of Applied Art from 1942 to 1944 and emigrated from Estonia to Sweden in 1944, moving on to the USA in 1949. In 1952 she graduated from the art school of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts, and in 1952, having moved to New York, she continued her studies at a design school there. She managed to fruitfully realise herself in exile, creating both figurative compositions and portraits, as well as abstract forms with a flowing formal language, following the example of Barbara Hepworth (1903–1975) and Henry Moore (1898–1986). She favoured rocks in various tones, whose finishing and surface treatment are of a high standard. She has belonged to artists' organisations, participated actively in exhibition life in the USA and elsewhere, and received awards.
e24294cd86f331d1e3cb2d0c79687b162e275b78: Paavo Käämbre (b. 1984) is a painter who lives and works in Tallinn. He graduated from the Tartu Art College in painting and the restoration of murals (2010) and defended his master's degree in painting at the University of Tartu (2012). Since 2012 Käämbre has worked at Eesti Päevaleht. He has had solo exhibitions at Draakoni Gallery ("Jäänud", 2014), the Pärnu Town Gallery ("Sõnad on tuhk mu suus", 2013), the Tartu Science Park ("Tähtvere", 2012), and the Aatrium Gallery ("Mustamäe", 2012). Käämbre has also participated in numerous group exhibitions, such as "Noor Eesti Kunst" "Estnische Kunst zu Gast in Fürtsnewalde" in Fürstenwalde, Germany (2015), and the exhibition of Young Painter Price finalists at the Contemporary Art Centre in Vilnius (2013). Käämbre mainly cultivates an expressive abstract painting style.
f838f6330881653b83f71f0308b5d4b0d34f96ff: Kristina Viin (born 22 November 1985 in Võru) is an Estonian artist, illustrator and poet. She belongs to the Tartu-affiliated women artists' group Delegatsioon K. Viin graduated from the Tartu Art College as a sculptor and has studied theology at the University of Tartu (since 2015). She has published the poetry collections "Nõtkel elevandisammul" (2014) and "Isepüüdleja" (2018), as well as poems in Looming, Vikerkaar, Müürileht, Värske Rõhk and elsewhere in anthologies, as well as art reviews and articles. Kristina Viin has illustrated poetry collections, children's books and publications, and has exhibited in Estonia and Finland. She has designed the stage set for the Tartu Student Theatre's production "Daniil Harms ehk Geeniuse elu". Viin is a member of the Estonian Academic Oriental Society and the Estonian Writers' Union.
20172daa5b073e59407e06748b844b61c9686fff: Kaija Kesa (b. 1978) studied graphic art and interdisciplinary arts at the Estonian Academy of Arts, graduating with a master's degree. Her work is mostly inspired by nature and an ecological-ethical way of thinking. Printmaking, as an art form with rich technical possibilities, is the artist's main means of expression. She has worked (since 2009) at the graafika.ee studio, and participates in both local and international exhibitions and projects (since 2000). She conducts workshops and courses in both printmaking and drawing. She was awarded the title of Network Baltic Young Printmaker laureate (2003). Kaija Kesa is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Association of Independent Graphic Artists. The year 2018 ended with the print exhibition "Tondi lood" at Vabaduse Gallery in Tallinn, and 2019 began with a solo exhibition at the Estonian Drama Theatre.
f0edd534e1bb84cfcabf42e893806f806366d8b3: Kristi Kangilaski (b. 1982) is an Estonian illustrator, artist and designer, whose work is characterised by poetic narrativity and a sensitive visual language. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in 2013 and has worked as a freelance artist since 2012. Since 2020 Kangilaski has worked as the town artist of Viljandi. Kangilaski has created and illustrated several popular children's books, both as author and as illustrator. Her works have been widely exhibited in Estonia and internationally, including at the Tallinn Illustration Triennial, the Bologna Children's Book Fair, the Bratislava Illustration Biennial, and several European touring exhibitions. Her solo exhibitions have taken place in galleries in Tartu and Tallinn. Kristi Kangilaski belongs to the Estonian Association of Graphic Designers.
5d296a44edaf8d1f76bd16afb46fc5b14579da3f: Viktor Gurov (b. 1989) graduated from the graphic design department of the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in 2014 and from the Faculty of Fine Arts (photography) with a master's degree (cum laude) in 2018. He studied as an exchange student at Aalto University in Helsinki. Since 2012 Gurov has worked as a freelance graphic designer. He designs exhibitions and exhibition catalogues. Viktor Gurov occasionally teaches as a guest lecturer at the Academy of Arts. In 2018 he began working as a graphic designer in the exhibitions department of the National Library of Estonia. Gurov has participated in group exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad; he is a member of the artists' group Neandertali Koobaskool, on the board of the NGO Uus Materjal (an art project-magazine), and a founder of the graffiti group and streetwear brand Multistab.
3677c6b314007b109c0ad56a1e05fd7f5b039b9b: Artist Albert Gulk was born in 1969 in Antsla. In 1996 he graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu. He has worked as a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School, currently a freelance artist. He has taken part in exhibitions since 1988. In the same year, together with Ilmar Kruusamäe, Peeter Allik and Priit Pangsepp, he founded the Kursi school in Tartu. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1995. Albert Gulk's works are characterised by a distinctive drawing style, in which he follows the rules of monumental art and the panel-like manner of presentation. Art historian Eha Komissarov has said that the certainty and conviction of Gulk's working manner immediately raised him into the front ranks of Estonian drawing. Albert Gulk's original artistry is underlined by the fact that the artist uses neither a model nor the help of a photograph in his drawings, relying solely on the images of his visual memory.
aa634542e1b020b4112064d1333ede77f172eb79: Cristelll (artist's pseudonym) was born and educated in Tallinn. She has graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts and is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association. Acrylic painting on canvas has become Cristelll's main means of expression. Her work is characterised by an intuitive journey and constant searching. Her inspiration comes from emotions, meaning, some rational or irrational object, organic forms, an event, a thought. The artist values reuse and experiments in her work with very different materials, from cinnamon bark to 3D-printed or ready-made objects. Her works can be found in the collection of the Estonian Academy of Arts, in the Mandalianpaillard gallery in Paris, as well as in private collections. Cristelll has shown her painterly work both in group and solo exhibitions, for example at MONA and at Haus Gallery.
83348766ac521f59b820dbf49737728b917c3b82: Erna Viitol (1920–2001) began her art studies in 1939 upon moving to Sweden, studying alongside work at the Viggbyholm Örjansgården free school. After returning to her homeland she began studies at the Tallinn School of Applied Art and in 1950 graduated from the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art. In the 1960s–1970s she devoted herself to portraiture and created decorative sculptures with stylised form. Her legacy includes over 60 portraits, the best of which successfully use formal generalisation without losing the psychological individuality of the sitter. Viitol portrayed many members of her family as well as cultural figures close to her, from Estonia, Finland and elsewhere. As materials she used ceramics, epoxy resin, Indonesian wood, sheet copper, glass-reinforced plastic. Some of the works remained as plaster casts, without being executed in the final material.
a8079db91115e79c9031daf4ab6fc5922a8a127a: Sandra Sirp (b 1988) expresses herself through a minimalist geometric visual language, through emptiness and space. Since 2015, Sirp has focused in her work, both in content and execution, on slowness, process and balance, which draws a connecting line between her painting series and forms a unified, coherent approach. Sirp graduated from Tallinn University with a bachelor's degree in art education (2012), from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in media graphics (2017), furthered her studies in painting at the Department of Fine Arts of the University of Porto (2015/2016), and studied in the joint master's programme in art teaching of the Estonian Academy of Arts and Tallinn University (2019–2022). Since 2023 Sirp has been a member of the Estonian Painters' Association. Sirp's works can be found in private collections and in the collection of EMMA, the Espoo Museum of Modern Art.
90965db2de4f0a29e1781a21571f6c99ac044c65: Jane Tiidelepp (b. 1971) is a painter, performance artist and poet residing in Tartu and Hiiumaa. She is currently in her 5th year studying eurythmy in the Performing Arts curriculum at the Viljandi Culture Academy. She has completed a BA in painting at the University of Tartu and an MA in art history at the University of Tartu, having previously studied in the free arts speciality at the EKA Open Academy. Tiidelepp is actively engaged both in painting and in eurythmy. In her painterly work she is intuitive and deals with both content and form, focusing rather on an abstract style of painting. Tiidelepp's works are carried out in both monochrome and blazing colour schemes, where the main aim is to find both deep meaning and total freedom in full abstraction. Jane Tiidelepp is a member of both the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association.
ac42657fb975d7a8751cdf7d784f41775abf7796: In 1915 she graduated with a silver medal from the Tallinn Girls' Crown Gymnasium, then studied in 1915–1916 at J. Bagayev's architecture courses in Petersburg and in 1916–1918 architecture at the Petrograd Women's Polytechnic Institute. In 1918–1919 she worked as an assistant architect at the Tallinn City Government. In 1919 she first appeared at an art exhibition of the Pallas art society in Tartu and furthered her training in painting under Nikolai Triik. In 1920–1921 she worked as a drawing teacher at the Tartu Teachers' Seminary. In 1922–1923 she stayed repeatedly in sanatoriums in Germany. From 1925 she took part in exhibitions in Estonia, as well as in Helsinki, Riga, Berlin, Amsterdam and elsewhere. From 1925 she was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists, in 1931–1935 a member of the Estonian Artists' Group, in 1936 a member of the Applied Artists' Union, and from 1946 a member of the ESSR Artists' Union.
5c2dc0d0db9d4ba86affe6dfb82553345226a12d: Eve Luik (1949) has worked in painting and printmaking since 1965, working at the time as an advertising artist. Since 1992 Eve Luik has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association. Since the same year she has been a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School. Eve Luik's works have been exhibited at exhibitions in Estonia, Finland, Italy, France, Switzerland, China, Japan, as well as reproduced on postcards, posters, in magazines and as illustrations in books. Her work, with its magical density and meditative depth, has found its way into many private collections. Eve has also fulfilled herself as an interior designer, as well as a fashion designer and make-up artist in Tartu beauty salons. For a long time the artist has also practised Chi-Jog-Kata, which imitates Eastern martial arts, and has passed on her skills as a trainer at the Tartu University Sports Hall.
f6e61cbd621a39b8573ec1d8b95f35c68b077d44: Liisa Kruusmägi was born in Tallinn in 1988. She studied painting at the bachelor's level at the Estonian Academy of Arts and completed her master's degree in drawing in 2013. Kruusmägi has furthered her studies at the Rhode Island School of Design, and has taken part in residency programmes in Vancouver at James Black Gallery, at AIRY, and at Yosuga in Japan, as well as at the Kitokia Grafika risograph printing studio in Lithuania. She has held solo exhibitions in Portugal, Sweden, Canada, Japan, the USA, Lithuania, Latvia, Germany and Estonia. In addition to those mentioned, she has also taken part in group exhibitions in London, Berlin, Slovakia, Italy, Finland and Russia. Liisa Kruusmägi is a freelance artist who mainly works with the media of painting and drawing and works as an illustrator. She has been a member of the Artists' Union since 2013.
32e2665d371d98406b5536fe6b14199cca363a52: She studied until 1933 at the Hugo Treffner Gymnasium in Tartu (drawing teacher Eduard Ole), graduated in 1934 from the Tallinn Boys' Real Gymnasium, studied in 1934–38 decorative painting at the State School of Applied Art. From 1936 she worked at the Tallinn Workers' Theatre. From 1937 she designed puppet productions at the Drama Theatre, working at the same theatre (with a break) until 1950 (as chief artist 1948–50); in 1946–48 she was also the stage designer of the Youth Theatre. In 1950–61 she worked at the Industrial Combine of the Estonian SSR Theatre Union, later working as an applied graphic artist (1968–86 at the experimental combine Bit). She designed books, for example Perrault's "Little Red Riding Hood" (1942), Kreutzwald's "Puulane ja tohtlane" (1945); as a fiction-book designer she made cover designs for the Estonian SSR Theatre Union's publication "Eesti NSV Teatrid" (1957–60). Estonian Encyclopaedia
6e50e60eb29fecfb0767d635aaaf9199688cca9f: Eve Valper was born in 1969 in Võru. She studied at the painting department of the University of Tartu in the years 1993–1998; she works as a freelance painter; she is also an art teacher at a hobby school and gives further-training courses in painting at the Tartu Art College Pallas. Member of the Tartu Artists' Association since 2024. In her work she is interested in space and light and the problems of perceiving the visible world, as well as matters related to history and cultural heritage; in her paintings she has recently examined the relationship of the surrounding urban space, or more broadly the environment, with the subjectivity of vision and perception. She approaches her subject matter primarily through colour, aiming to create on the two-dimensional surface of the work space, light and the environments that live their own life within it, and striving to synthesise a colour-centred painting tradition with a world of meanings and stories.
82ae92593b5eab60a2c63360c45495aa9f5cceae: Rait Prääts (1952) began his artistic career by creating large stained-glass windows for public spaces, including for St. Nicholas' Church and the National Library. In glass he developed his own authorial technique, which allowed him to paint, so to speak, three-dimensionally. Moving in the direction of sculpture, he uses cement mixtures for modelling, to which he adds painted glass details, achieving a kind of synthesis between painting and sculpture. Prääts graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in the speciality of glass art (1975), has taken part in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, and has also received a number of accolades, including the Kristjan Raud Prize (2013). His (commissioned) works have reached many places around the world and many collections. Prääts is a member of the Estonian Glass Artists' Union and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
1752a6823f3de24bdc58307167148f4836357be0: Leena Kuutma's (1974) creative style is often hybrid and mainly connected with combining the spatial experience characteristic of sculpture with the material knowledge characteristic of ceramics. She has previously used drawing techniques in ceramics and is also drawn to themes of public space and monumental art. Kuutma graduated from the sculpture department of the Estonian Academy of Arts (1996), has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, and since 1994 has taken part in more than fifty workshops, symposia and competitions, working with wood, stone, concrete, snow and ice. Her works are held in many private and museum collections and in public space in Estonia, Germany, Austria, Turkey, Denmark, Latvia and Lithuania. Kuutma is a member of the Estonian Ceramists' Union, the Estonian Sculptors' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
33765aa8dcd6210b4cc3fd27285ebeba70d3484e: Miina Vilo (b. 1995) is an Estonian artist working mainly in Tallinn and Tartu. She obtained a bachelor's degree in painting from the Pallas University of Applied Sciences (2025) and is a member of the art group MULTINEKTAR (founded 2024). Vilo's work has been described as an emotional and versatile synthesis of pop art, surrealism and symbolist elements. In 2023/24 she received the D'Albret Collection: The Reiss von Filski Trust prize. The jury highlighted her ability to tell stories through symbols that invite the viewer on a journey of dreams and reflections, noting that the artist's individuality is palpably present in every work. Vilo has actively participated in exhibitions and art auctions. More information and the full CV can be found on the artist's website: www.miinavilo.com/cv
3cfe37f37fff63b3e7aaf88677c1d0094afc844e: The cloth factory (Kalevivabrik) was founded in 1829, its product being woollen cloth - kalev. In 1858, 373 men and 430 women already worked at the Kärdla cloth factory. Although the factory's operations experienced short-term stoppages and harder times (in 1870 the factory burned down, after which a new four-storey building was completed in 1873; and at the turn of the century it faced economic difficulties), it was nevertheless the island's most important industrial enterprise until the First World War. In 1879 output was 200,000 arshins worth approximately 800,000 roubles. In 1908 the Narva Manufaktuur merged with the struggling Kärdla cloth factory. The Kärdla factory then produced 100,000 metres of cloth per year (about three times less than in 1879). In 1941 the factory was destroyed by fire.
6de4c81e725155af8546e9ed376ae08d16f52994: Singer and composer; Studied at Haapsalu Higher Elementary School and the Petrograd Polytechnic Institute, and singing privately with Armanda degli Abbati. Sang in the Estonia opera choir from 1918-44, was also an actor and music director of the miniature theatre Apollo from 1920-22, music director of Paul Pinna's Rahvateater (People's Theatre) from 1924-27, and choir and singing-game leader of the Tallinn Workers' Music Society from 1929-35. Founded the male quartet Heli 4 from Estonia singers in 1939. Fled to Germany in 1944, belonged to the association "Estonian artists in Lübeck" from 1945-46, and later to the association "Estonian artists in Blomberg". Went to the USA in 1949, lived in Chicago until 1973, then in Canada for the rest of his life, singing in the Toronto Estonian Men's Choir. Composed nearly 50 songs ("Üksainus õis", "Paula, sul on poisipea", "Vanapoisi polka" and others). His father was a merchant and maker of home organs.
373b734d5f0cb59f4e718f8e96a1dc54d7fb12da: Mara Ljutjuk was born in Tallinn in 1978. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting in 2001, and also obtained a master's degree in education sciences there. She furthered her education in fine arts in 2007 at the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia in Spain. Since 2006 she has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association. Since 2004 she has held several solo exhibitions and has participated in numerous group exhibitions since 2000. In addition to painting, Mara is engaged in curating and designing exhibitions, and is actively involved in curating and organising the programme of the Evald Okas Museum. In 2019 she received the Galerii-G art award. In 2020 she was a nominee for the Konrad Mägi Prize. Mara has three children (b. 2009/2012/2015) and lives and works in Tallinn.
be518aa1c3b824fd5acfd8cea751e0b9c460d1ea: Peeter Krosmann (b. 1971 in Pärnu) is a painter living and working in Kaunas. He studied at the Konrad Mägi Studio and graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu in 2005. Since 1999 he has taught drawing, illustration, comic design and other subjects at the Tartu Art School and the Tartu Art College. In 2015 he was awarded the Ado Vabbe Prize. Although most of his solo exhibitions have taken place in Tartu, his works have also been shown in Lithuania, Latvia, France and Norway. His style fuses the traditional painterly approach with a contemporary understanding of the world surrounding the author. He is known primarily as a painter of cityscapes and is also a highly regarded portraitist. Among other things, Krosmann is also the author of several sgraffito-technique wall paintings.
262c7d04c50395ab535d14e9aeb3e56aa206516f: Paul and Karl Burman are an interesting example in our cultural history of how representatives of the then-declining Baltic German culture adapted to and blended into a rapidly developing national art scene. He began his career as an artist in Estonia at a time when Baltic German artistic life was fading and losing significance. Paul, in his cultural convictions and use of language, firmly belonged to the Baltic German circle. His studies and childhood home also connected him with Russian culture. The artist's family had Baltic German roots and close ties with Russia. Paul Burman never learned the Estonian language until his death, although during his lifetime he associated with many Estonian artists. His work, however, developed under the influence of inner logic and impulses and had no closer connection with the general trends of Estonian art.
081d6cfbafde8d89ac502e20051da8d046d139b0: Since OÜ Visible Solutions moved to KUMU for the summer to develop new products, they donated one of last year's prototypes – Clarity: an exterior area of an interior space – to CAME. To quote the KUMU press release, "OÜ Visible Solutions is a work of art/enterprise, which operates on the edge between the economic and artistic fields, by examining them as ideologized spaces and language environments; and if one is located between them, one can interpret phenomena and concepts from one to the other. The group deals with the main principles of modern economic space, by using creative industries and processes based thereon as the primary analytical material. The group examines the new global symptoms of all-inclusive neo-liberal economic logic."
b0f5cfd88af650c86e87eedfcaad259fbfc6dac6: Esko Lepp was born the son of a blacksmith. He studied graphic art and applied graphics at the State School of Applied Art in Tallinn from 1935-1940 (supervisor G. Reindorff). He was in the service of the Estonian National Museum (ERM). He furthered his education from 1940-1941 at the Konrad Mägi State Higher Art School in Tartu. In 1941 he joined a destruction battalion. During the Second World War he worked in a kolkhoz and a factory in Russia, joined the Red Army in 1942, was called up in 1943 to the Yaroslavl collective of Estonian artists, and also worked as a front-line draughtsman. From 1943-1948 he studied graphic art at the Surikov Art Institute in Moscow, graduating as a student of P. Pavlinov in the field of woodcut. From 1948-1951 Lepp was a lecturer at the Tallinn State Art Institute (ERKI), after which he became a freelance artist. He created works on war and industrial themes, series of woodcuts, illustrations, watercolours, and ex libris.
850f47e07b24c692c7ad81722ec8844d3d262dfc:
He was born in Smolensk, Russia; the family moved to Estonia in 1914. He lived on Laeva. He studied at the Pallas Art School in Tartu from 1938-40, continuing his studies until his arrest in spring 1945 (teachers included Aleksander Vardi and others). In 1944 he attempted to flee to the West together with Valve Janov and Kaja Kärner. He was held until 1954 in a prison camp in Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia. From 1958 he lived in Tallinn, where he also died. Painter, watercolourist. From 1937-39 he was a stage designer at the Tartu Workers' Theatre. In the 1960s, like Lembit Saarts, he approached abstract painting through nature motifs.

1a48199874568c5d4a8036539d8e5de9baacd6f3: He worked in Lübeck, Tallinn, Gothenburg, Riga, Narva and Saint Petersburg, and was a citizen of Tallinn from 1701. In 1715 he again worked in Gothenburg, then in Riga and Narva, where he painted several portraits commissioned by Peter I. He arrived in Saint Petersburg in 1725 and began working at the court. He painted compositions and portraits and was known as a good copyist. In 1725 Catherine I bought four religious and allegorical paintings from him and commissioned six portraits. From 1732 he was a drawing teacher at the Cadet Corps, and from 1734-1736 a painter there as well. Commissioned by Empress Anna Ivanovna, he painted portraits of her father Ivan V, her sisters Praskovya and Yekaterina, Praskovya, daughter of Tsar Fyodor Alekseyevich, and Peter I and Catherine I. One of his earlier works, an equestrian portrait of Charles XII, was housed in the House of the Brotherhood of Blackheads in Riga.
7450d0867d27e82cd654ad0365d86fe9de90e76f: Ants Mölder (1939–2009) was active as a modernist sculptor mainly in the 1970s and 1980s. His characteristic playful approach to semi-abstract forms led him to experiment with various materials, of which aluminium and epoxy resin were especially characteristic of Estonian sculpture in the 1970s. Ants Mölder has also created decorative forms and figures from wood and marble. His mahogany sculptures have received special attention. Small-format drawings made in various techniques reveal to the viewer the sculptor's schemes of thought from the time preceding the completion of one or another sculpture. Memorial medals, awards and small forms make up a significant part of Ants Mölder's oeuvre. Second World War monuments created by him in the 1970s can be found in Estonia's public space.
69386086ea5c194f377b5f06215f24b69bdf264d:
JIM is the common denominator of three artists – Johannes Säre, Iti Kasser and Maido Juss – officially registered by the state registry key 80283354. The artwork was initially created for the three artists’ solo exhibition in the Draakon Gallery and later took an iconic role in EKKM’s bar, where it was unfortunately destroyed in the course of active partying. By now, the piece has been restored. The

consists of the three artists’ portraits printed on glass and placed one behind the other to form a strange androgyne. This is a self portrait by JIM, the person – a mix of three artists to form a single being. This method is reflective of the group’s co-creating process, a symbiosis of world-views from three different artists.
579cddd6af735f2a9b875f16a68fc674316df2c6:
Ilmar Kimm was born in Petrograd. He studied from 1927–1935 at the Estonian school in Leningrad, and from 1936–1939 at the secondary art school of the All-Russian Academy of Arts. From 1939–1941 he studied at the All-Russian Academy of Arts. In the autumn of 1941 he was mobilised into the Red Army. He was severely wounded in battle near Velikiye Luki and was demobilised. In 1944 he resumed his art studies, graduating in 1948 from the Ilya Repin Institute of Art in Leningrad.

From 1948–1951 he worked as a teacher of painting at the Tartu State Art Institute. From 1952–1988 he was a teacher at ERKI: from 1954 he was docent, from 1965 professor. From 1963–1983 he was head of the painting department, and from 1983–1988 he was consultant professor. From 1951 he was a member of the Artists' Union
277011e8c20eb055f699ada19eeef77501e0f8d2: Pille-Riin Jaik (born 1991 in Tallinn) is an interdisciplinary artist living in Vienna, who works mostly in the fields of video art and performance, but also frequently creates sculptures and installations. She has earned a Bachelor's degree in Photography at the Estonian Academy of Arts, a Master's degree in Art and Media (professor Constanze Ruhm) at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and is currently working there as a PhD in Practice candidate, researching storytelling and political landscape narratives in the Baltics. She is also a member of the video art collective Golden Pixel. In her works she is mostly interested in hypertext, strange places, weeds, textiles and fabric patterns, leftover and unused materials or ideas in a queer-feminist and class-conscious context.
9bbfc50ecb0a6d68f3d38338fc966d1a28a82ec0: Work as a sculptor: Peeter Mudist (1942–2013) is one of the greatest Estonian painters of the 20th century, whose painterly compositions are based on realism while also presenting visionary imagery. He graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1967 as a painter and began creating sculptures that same year. His first painted plaster portraits and figures were succeeded in the late 1970s by granite sculptures of stylised form. In these, the author has at times worked the natural stone only minimally. He has also created strongly generalised portrait works and large-format granite figures. Peeter Mudist has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Prize (1989), the Konrad Mägi Medal (1991), and the Order of the White Star, III Class (2001).
043f3ffedef4d53477b229b7fc920df5ebf62363: Liis Tedre (b. 1976 in Tallinn) completed her Bachelor's studies in graphic art at the Department of Fine Arts of the Estonian Academy of Arts in 2022. She has furthered her professional training at the Tartu Art College Pallas and at Dedalo Arte Contemporanea in Italy. As an artist she highly values the feeling of holding graphic paper in one's hands – its relief, structure and sensitivity. She creates both flat, more traditional prints as well as works using new author's techniques offering playfulness and unpredictability. Recently she has depicted everyday objects in her works to tell playful stories. She is interested in the universal and timeless patterns of the world, seeing similarities in how nature and the human world function, and follows paths that lead toward goodness.

5ea74f7ca842151b5dc027bcf8b7ac9fa117279b: Paco Ulman (b. 1980) is a Tallinn architect and photographic artist, who has gained recognition primarily for his metaphysical still lifes in the contemporary urban environment. Since 2008 he has held a Master's degree in Architecture from the Estonian Academy of Arts. As a photographic artist, Ulman deals mostly with the problems of urban space, which he encounters in his everyday work as an architect, dislocating the concepts of time and space as well as the categories of space and the representation of space. Currently, his most important solo exhibitions include "Tallinnas" at Hobusepea Gallery in 2009, "Tallinn-Helsinki-Stockholm" at Tallinn City Gallery in 2011, and "mememe" at Hobusepea Gallery in 2014. In 2012 Ulman received the Sadolin Contemporary Art Prize.
58163bd721ee0e7297cb9dd79f3d657a431a0432: Sergei Inkatov was born in 1971 in Baku, studied at the Baku Art School 1987–1989, at the Azim Zadeh Art School in Baku 1989–1992, and at the Venetsianov Art School in 1994. Recognitions: 2006 Diploma of Excellence, Global Art Annual, London, United Kingdom; 2010 laureate of the "Cultural Property" foundation, Russia; 2011 laureate of the Tallinn – European Capital of Culture art competition; 2017 member of the Mondial Academia, France; 2017 Mondial Academia Ambassador in Estonia; 2017 Gold Medal "Prix international des Galeries" in the category of abstract painting, France; 2019 1st place at the "Artweeks France" competition in Miramas; 2019 Gold Medal "Prix international des Galeries" in the category of abstract painting, France. 0f63d12804847d0ccfefc2e38813dce0831be41b: Tõnu Noorits, PhD (b. 1952 in Tartu) graduated from the University of Tartu in 1975 as a biologist. He defended his doctoral degree in 1984. He has worked in photographic art since 1982. In 1992, together with Silver Vahter, he founded the design and art society KYNA, where he engages in photo-staging, design and publishing. He is a versatile creator, and his works – portraits, nudes, staged photographs, abstract landscapes – often contain unexpected visions. His photographs are characterised by a high pictorial culture and perfect execution. In the final decades of the last century he was the most exhibited Estonian author in European photo salons. He has had 35 solo exhibitions in various countries – Austria, Belgium, Italy, Latvia, France, Sweden, Germany, as well as 12 group exhibitions.
82244aad9799f94cbaa930fa4c7919e497ece4b3: Tõnis Laanemaa (born 1937) studied painting at the Tartu Art School and graphic art at the Estonian State Institute. Initial leader and later member of ANK'64, the innovative Estonian art group of the 1960s. Tõnis began exhibiting with paintings, but gained recognition primarily for his free graphic art and posters, although throughout his career he has also exhibited nudes, portraits and abstract compositions. Since 1970 Laanemaa has taken part in numerous exhibitions in the Baltic states, Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Germany, Russia, and the Netherlands. Tõnis Laanemaa belongs to the generation of artists for whom proper drawing from nature is self-evident. He has also gained recognition as a figure drawer and is a highly regarded drawing teacher.
a5d7c95aa20d24285a1e714e092322727ff41137: Lembit Tolli (1927–2013) graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1953 and began exhibiting his work the same year. His creative work of the 1950s follows nature and the recommended thematics of the time. The modernist imagery of the end of the decade also drew in Lembit Tolli; he expanded his choice of materials, taking an interest in dolomite, the possibilities of wood sculpture, welded sculpture, epoxy resin and embossed metal. Alongside portrait and figure work, Tolli created masterful reliefs for Martin Saks and Endel Taniloo's monument to F. R. Kreutzwald in Kadriorg (1958) and the poetic bronze relief "Sõit maailma otsa" ["Journey to the End of the World"], based on motifs from the national epic, for the Ice Voyage obelisk (1960) at Maarjamäe in Tallinn.
e3729913450e9cd5beed568ae9b0ec5e3f850067: The artist's kinetic objects stand out for their demanding engineering-technical solutions. Starting in 1973 he built electronics-based light- and sound-kinetic objects, but only a few were exhibited during the period of their creation. The object "Kaleidoskoop" ["Kaleidoscope"] (EKM) is one of these, first shown as early as 1976 at the Tallinn Art Hall at an exhibition of experimental architecture. The public was able to become thoroughly acquainted with Jõgeva's kinetic objects only in 1993, at the exhibition "Mobile 1". Several of his objects (for example "Sinine" ["Blue"], EKM, 1973, restored 2004; "Oranž torn" ["Orange Tower"], EKM, 1978, restored 1994/2004) are based on sound and light effects. ef2e81407cfe676fd5ada298568c2999d9b1d22f: Riho Kuld (1936) is familiar to most residents of Tallinn from his white "Raadiotuvi" ["Radio Dove"] (1975) on the wall of the radio building. He appeared before the Estonian art public in the wave of modernism in the mid-1960s and was one of the renewers of Estonian sculpture. Riho Kuld's sculptures, with their baroquely playful movement, are effective through their rich structures and precise composition. His work brings to Estonian sculpture a complex movement and a perceptible dynamic force that is fairly exceptional among the Nordic countries. Among Riho Kuld's monumental works, particularly outstanding in its modernist innovativeness are the Kuressaare monument to the victims of fascism (1965) and the Tehumardi obelisk (1967; both created together with Matti Varik). He has received the Kristjan Raud Prize (1973).
8b75e9bc303f55001e1a0df04380002255b480b4: POLLI, Kaljo (1928, Raadivere village, Kuremaa parish – 2004). The Estonian painter Kaljo Polli has portrayed creative people, intellectuals, athletes and children. His works include both solutions based on local colours and tonal painting approaches. He also created large staged compositions, and his industrial-themed paintings received official recognition in their time. A separate chapter in his work is formed by the pictures with ethnographic motifs that emerged in the 1960s from impressions of a trip to Kamchatka made together with Lennart Georg Meri. Polli acquired his painting education at the Tartu State Art Institute in Johannes Võerahansu's master class; he later worked as a teacher at the Tartu Art School and at the Tartu department of ERKI. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/
3c9ddccb4b25d622237cd9ed7077e8d71c0d6039: Only a few examples of the landscape paintings of the 1930s have survived; a number of works were destroyed in the turmoil of the war.
