e952984930b30872d5dfe8d2b294c41c4ed97adb: A figural composition. In the background, autumn grain fields with sheaves of grain stacked together. The composition consists of three figures: a woman, a child, and a man. In front on the left, a strong female figure with a sheaf of grain under her right arm. Dressed in a pink dress, a bluish apron in front, and a scarf on her head. Her gaze directed down to the right, at the child and the man. In the middle, a small naked child clings to the mother's clothing and looks up at her. On the right in front sits a man dressed in a dark blue shirt and brown trousers, a hat on his head. In the background, amid hilly fields, a small round blue lake.
883fcec2f359ee4662afc591823b24f82150f310: J. Vahtra was mobilised into the army during the First World War, during the St. Petersburg period, but did not end up at the front. He took an active part in the activities of Estonian students in St. Petersburg, in 1914-1915 he helped edit the handwritten art journal "Ronk", in 1915-1916 he belonged to the union of students interested in art, music and literature "Ritsikate ring", where the writers Johannes Semper and Karl Ast-Rumor were also active. He moved from St. Petersburg to Estonia in June 1918. In 1923 he was a founding member of the Estonian Artists' Group (member of the group until 1925). In 1926 he joined the art association Pallas.
c25221f28b1c932aefb47dcd3e5f3b4bbe0ec052: A figural composition consisting of many small figures and figure groups: above the horizontal centre line a procession of people in ecstasy moves from right to left, the first ones carrying a seated figure. In the upper right corner a group of kneeling female figures, with a clergyman or a nun standing in front of them. In the left margin and below, people are engaged in everyday activities - in bed, dancing, fighting, conversing. The figures are painted sketchily, predominantly in black, brown and grey tones. Blue and pinkish-red tones dominate in the background.
a34f238a6a5733a356a31c8bfc46a227c8a577bb: Mildeberg worked as a photographer and applied artist from 1925. In 1941 he was evacuated to the rear of the Soviet Union, to Bashkiria, where he worked as a farm labourer in the Birsk district. In 1942-1945 he was a front-line artist and photographer in the Estonian Rifle Corps of the Red Army. In 1945 he became a member of the Artists' Union. After returning to Tallinn, Mildeberg worked in 1945 as a photo correspondent for Rahva Hääle, in 1945-1946 Mildeberg was the technical editor of the magazine Pikker, later a freelance artist. He preferred graphic techniques, made caricatures and cartoons, and illustrated books.
3a909804ac2351fe0727b90b2d9f91cfbd0ec62b:
On 6 August the sculptor Tamara Ditman was sent on her final journey from Alexander Nevsky Cathedral. She was buried at Alexander Nevsky Cemetery.

Tamara Ditman was born in Russia, in Habarovsk, into a military family on 9 August 1945. Her childhood was spent in Tallinn. After graduating from ERKI she worked as an art teacher at Tallinn Secondary School No. 52 and as an artist at the sports society Kalev, and from 1985 she was a freelance artist.

In her last years the artist suffered from serious health problems, she gave up work as a practising artist and devoted herself to religious life in the Orthodox church.
2986cde646f7a3a923497b686540ef2022e193f2: In the middle ground Joachim and Anna bow to the right and point with their hands to the small Mary standing before them. To the right of Mary, Zacharias stands on a pedestal and blesses Mary. On the left, somewhat behind Mary's parents, a crowd of people in greenish garments with red outer mantles. The leftmost of them holds a burning candle. In the background architectural elements and, on the left, a taller tower-like house. In the upper right corner Mary enthroned with an angel. The tonality of the icon is greenish-brown, the decorations of the garments, the halos of the saints and the angel wings are golden.
fffd11ad5bf97b41bbd01e2f7aec7f4130e2b7b7: In the foreground, against a background of a flat greenish-blue field with green shades, at the lower right the head of a brown horse, and to the right of it, closer to the viewer, the head of a red horse with yellow harness, both in profile facing left. In the middle ground on the left, in profile facing right, a maiden standing in a red combination. In the background an undulating landscape with deciduous trees and bushes, in the middle two low grey buildings in simple geometric forms. Above the horizon, slightly to the left of the central axis, two life-size lilies of the valley float. Above the horizon the sky is white, becoming creamy as it approaches the horizon.
05b2acc1410f847ef930b8515a57b4e7325070d3: A multi-figure composition in pastel tones with diffused contour lines. In the foreground a bespectacled woman in a colourful blouse, a grey coat, hat and shoes, next to her a woman seen frontally in a grey coat and hat, with long brown trousers, her hand on the shoulder of the child standing beside her. To the right of the child, a traffic light and a girl sitting in a dark red dress. Besides the four figures in the foreground, there are children's figures of various ages, executed with varying degrees of detail, on both sides and above. Amid the pastel transparency some individual details are emphasised. In places the paint is applied pastosely.
1da1d3f8dbebffabe041910bcadc71298e2dac4d: A captivating park view in diffused light: in the foreground on the left and right, tall yellow garden posts with knobs, with a forged garden fence between the posts. Behind the fence, lush greenery of trees and bushes, confined to green islands by white stone borders. Between the green islands, smooth grey park paths. Straight ahead, through the open gate, the view opening into the park is closed off by a large grey house, of which only a part of the wall, a bright white-framed window and a gable are visible. In the middle a man stands on the park path with his back to the viewer, hands in pockets, above at the upper left a patch of blue sky.
961bc720a53426b90303c9e1e79e530ec8b39f87: A four-part painting. A gigantic reclining female nude extends across the picture plane. The profile head is located in the upper right corner. The arm stretched over the head is not visible in the picture. The composition is arched, somewhat U-shaped. The nude's right leg is bent at the knee, upright in a triangular shape. The left leg lies bent horizontally. The foot of the right leg is obscured by the head located in the left corner of the painting, which is placed in a sideways view, slightly diagonally upward. The head is in greenish-grey tones. The background is a soiled brown - in red, grey, black tones. The frame is in the upper part of the painting.
7152d74496fc996af157cd20b796d2b4322f4113: A bust portrait of a young woman composed within an oval, the head turned to the right, the gaze directed slightly to the side and down, over the shoulder. The woman has soft facial features, dark eyes, a straight nose, an eyebrow line. Long curly reddish-blond hair, parted in the middle, falls onto her bared shoulders; in her hair, on the right, brightly coloured flowers: edelweiss, poppy, cornflower with a green twig. A light transparent scarf-garment is wrapped around her shoulders. Muted brownish, silvery tones, a soft academic manner of depiction. The figure blends into the background, the light directed onto the face and shoulder. Carved oval wooden frame.
88782208414c47328b46f76c791817a3ce25d8e4: Under the window, in the room, a table with a striped tablecloth is piled high with all kinds of garden produce, vessels, flower vases on the floor, fruits and containers on the windowsill and on stands in front of the window. In front, in the middle, a large table on which, from the left, two plates with apples, a halved green squash, a plate with fruits. On the tablecloth beans, apples, beets, an aubergine, in the middle pears on a footed dish. On the right leaves, branches with fruits. On the floor on the left a vase of red gladioli, in front a colourful bouquet. In the upper part of the painting, sunny greenery is visible through the window. A free impressionistic manner, conditionally marking forms.
5c356bc24eb86ff71a3a69a4c5de5c6b367adb43: The sculpture collection of the Art Museum of Estonia contains some of his realistic genre sculptures, portraits and small ceramic plastic works from the post-war years. Of his numerous garden sculptures the best known is "Thoughts from Pandivere" in the garden of the Kristjan Raud House Museum in Nõmme. Signe Mölder has also created public sculptures and monumental plastic works. The monument to V. I. Lenin in Jõhvi, created together with Arseni Mölder and Enn Roos, has by now been removed from the town. In 1999 a monument created by her to Estonian soldiers who took part in World War II was erected in Jüriöö Park in Tallinn.
eae11cbb18a69ea5c2fa1f0366eb75dbdb3e569c: In the foreground a small table of dark wood with carved legs. On the table a beige-brown striped tablecloth. On the table an arrangement: at the front edge two books placed one on top of the other, the top one with a green cover. On the books a dark, greyish-green bowl narrowing at the bottom, with two dark stripes at its upper edge. Behind the books, on the right, a dark blue vase with a narrow neck at the top, in which a large yellow rose. To the left of the vase with the rose, a slender brown ceramic vase with a handle, narrowing at the top. The background is in old rose and greenish-blue tones, with slightly imitated drapery at the edges.
1d98facf17f6f7de6f8f5c21763c88110ac90106: In the foreground three pedestals of grey stone with cartouches, ornaments and bas-reliefs. On the left pedestal a tower narrowing gradually from top (green at the bottom, pink at the top), with a small red rod at its tip. To the left of the tip of the tower an indeterminately shaped blue patch. From the middle pedestal grows a light pink form resembling an atomic cloud. On the right pedestal a piece of landscape with a green tree, a lamp post and grass, above, against a dark blue sky background, a crescent moon. The background is light grey. The pedestals are painted in a sandy-coloured mixed technique, with a very pastose effect.
65532d28f7841094880db078c3de755bcf458573: A late-autumn cityscape, in the background on the right a tall modern complex with a four-lane road, in the foreground on the left part of a building with a balcony on which two people stand, in the background a pyramid-shaped parking complex, on the horizontal surfaces of which smaller buildings, bare trees and people. The colour scheme is whitish-grey, in the background a light sky with grey shreds of cloud. The work belongs to the series "Aidu Pyramids", in which Kadarik-Tüür Arhitektid sketch a future use for the deposit area of the Aidu oil shale quarry in the form of a parking complex made of pyramids built from stone waste.
6ffed4ad22423e296b368b55579c2f9717bc2322:
Born in Tallinn into an engineer's family. In 1948 she graduated, together with her future husband Albert Eskel and several other well-known artists of her generation, from the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, but was not given a diploma for political reasons. Her father Raiu Mullari was a prominent Estonian War of Independence veteran, and her brother Rünno Mullari, a talented mathematician, was sent to a prison camp by the occupying authorities.

In 1948-1952 Juta Eskel worked as a drawing teacher in several schools in Tallinn, in 1952-1957 she found work as an artist at the Art Products Combine.
3ca199e6d8a962625bda3334f4ae0b5c1e3f4aa6: Siiri Jüris is an artist living and working in Tartu. She graduated from the Tartu Art School in the specialty of decorator-stylist (2012) and obtained both a bachelor's and a master's degree from the Painting Department of the University of Tartu (2015 and 2017 respectively). Since her bachelor's thesis, Jüris has repeatedly turned to portrait painting, being interested in the possibilities and possibility of depicting the individual and their states, while consistently questioning the conventions and traditions of this painting genre. Jüris's paintings are held in several private collections.
97a28f04486acc4e704bbbdb9dbafaf569b8626b: Moona Saul (b. 1992) studied fashion design and technology at TEKO in Denmark and at the Amsterdam Fashion Institute. She then moved on into the world of illustration and painting. She held her first (group) exhibition in Amsterdam (2020). From there the winds carried her instead into the art of tattooing, and in parallel Moona found the technique of yarn tufting as a means of self-expression. Painting and illustration have always accompanied these pursuits at the same time. Moona's painting style is figurative art in a vivid, psychedelic and slightly ironic key.
96ecf7698ba1fb3ce670f1c20737901bfcd2e9d6: At the centre of the painting stands a three-quarter figure of a female nude in yellow tones. Around her upward-looking head is an aura marked by a thin yellow line. The breasts are slightly relief-like. From the upper right corner to the lower left corner runs an irregular diagonal area of colour modulated in yellow tones. On the right in the middle is a rectangle in a black colour scheme with red accents, from which flows a waterfall in blue and green tones. In the upper part of the painting, on the left, on a blue background, is a rectangle marked in yellow. The overall effect of the painting is somewhat abstractionist and in places painted pastosely.
fe356ac9762d435b9a2f1482cc472fa200760f4d: View of the building of the former Tallinn Emperor Nicholas Men's Gymnasium on Suur-Kloostri Street near the Nunna Gate. In the foreground a street with stone paving and a sidewalk of stone slabs. To the right a man and a woman are driving in a ladder-wagon. Groups of gymnasium students in uniform stand on the street. The gymnasium plot is separated from the street by a stone fence with stone posts. On the left the city wall with three towers and buildings along the wall. On the right a two-storey stone classicist gymnasium building. The tower of the Church of the Transfiguration of the Lord, located next to the school, is also visible.
3e4797beaa39fa605267c60c126f7cac1dcd5ec8: Mari Prekup (1984) has in recent years focused on the layers of traditional culture and their contemporary interpretations, moving from everyday rituals and the field of meaning of sacred groves toward the worldview of the Finno-Ugric and related peoples. Her works do not offer ready-made answers, but open up a space where remembering is at once both a sacred and a fragile act. Prekup holds a master's degree in printmaking from the Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA) (2015); she has been active in art life both as an exhibiting artist, performance artist and organiser, and has received, among other awards, the Eduard Wiiralt Young Author's Award.
44f39cf7a029374d0f899c370fa3dd3f05d9bfc4: Annabel Janke (b. 1994) is a painter who lives and works in Tallinn. After graduating from the Tallinn Art School, she began studies in graphic design at the Estonian Academy of Arts, but is currently completing her studies in the Painting Department. In her paintings she is primarily interested in depicting the human being, capturing character, as well as abstraction. Lately she has become more interested in op-art, while her style has always tended toward pop-art-like poster-like quality. In addition, the artist also draws caricatures.
c9b4e4ed848a11ef749350d2c5cf82be70b9bd13: In the foreground on the left an easel with an unfinished canvas, a faceless man in a blue jacket stepping out of the picture. On the left the bust portrait of a woman in a brown dress strongly gathered at the shoulders. Above her, on a white wall, a portrait of a woman in grey tones. To the right of the picture in the foreground is a multi-square composition (group portrait), in which especially striking are a female nude with upswept hair, to her right a woman with long black hair and glasses, and at the bottom edge a woman with a pageboy hairstyle in a black dress. Very painterly, in places pastose.
ef13d9441f7391a3a1116742b3f72f8127355ac2: Her earlier free creative work focuses mainly on portraits of children and adolescents and on nude figures. Compositions made in the late 1930s and during the war years have a very delicate and poetic effect due to their fragile, expressive treatment of the figure. Lydia Laas's figurative works of the Soviet period acquired the simple, ascetic culture of form characteristic of the 1960s. From 1945 she worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn, being the only one of Estonia's first women sculptors who adapted to Soviet art life in the postwar decades.
f49ff8e9b16b073e9a86d96898da9ad3a2734db9: In the foreground four male figures: the middle one, a grey-haired man in a fur coat and papakha, holds a piece of paper in his hand as if showing something to the young dark-haired man in a peaked cap standing beside him. On the right a young man, in a fur coat and forage cap, cartridge belts over his shoulder, hand grenades attached to his belt, in profile facing left. Behind the men standing in the middle a young man, a red ribbon around his left arm, his head turned to the left. Further back on the left men pulling a heavy machine gun, on the horizon a building in flames. On the right, in front of a railway carriage, a group of men in military uniform busy at work.
b9939d2fef372f5dc1291379c71b989bd674a257: In the foreground, in three-quarter profile facing left, a dark-haired seated man in a white shirt, his right arm bent at the elbow and stretched forward, palm toward the viewer, his left arm bent at the elbow with the hand hanging freely. In front of him a fragment of Palladio's facade drawings, on which lies a golden metal plate in the shape of a heraldic rose, with a pink dahlia flower resting on it. Behind the figure, in reddish shades, a semicircular colonnade with paired columns; on the right edge of the painting, behind the colonnade, young men and women dance in colourful chitons.
7522d7fcfc79ca3a43466902909fe6d8317a2ddf: Timur Husainov is an artist from Narva who combines various art forms in his work, including traditional painting, graphic design, and digital art. He is an active participant in art life and has taken part in local exhibitions, such as those organised by the "Vesterwalli" association. In addition, his work can be seen on the streets of Narva in the form of graffiti, which bring freshness and creativity to the city. Husainov draws inspiration from the urban environment and architecture, bringing a unique dynamism and vitality to his works.
950d10720fde140e6c738f3f51dd993481725206: Above the midline, out of a blackish-brown background, a glowing red draped relief-like form emerges smoothly, thickly covered with paint. Between the folds of the form, one drop-shaped sea-blue area and another yellowish area. The lower half of the form narrows and becomes flat toward the midline. Three semicircles of metal rivets at the bottom centre, a smaller one on the left edge and on the right on the plywood form.
b1c17a682b3c219e3175d576e3e7b6e67df5d57e: In the foreground, Christ sunk down under the weight of the cross, supporting himself on the ground with both hands and raising his head crowned with thorns, his face bearing a pained expression. In the background a man with a turban, another with a ladder, one Roman soldier on horseback, another with a shield and spear.
cbedb25151daf7a9e42e63a0d0ca4e476c77c133: On the left side two sculptural putti. The fresco depicts the mythological scene of the Rape of the Sabine Women. In the curved back wall round arcades. 882d84bd8daed16c036a498187638077d1b3180d: Virge Jõekalda (1963) uses techniques such as drypoint and etching, which connect her to the traditions of printmaking, but the isolation of a meaningful fragment and its processing into an image, a forceful line and a sensitive treatment of the coloured surface reveal a path uniquely her own. Jõekalda graduated from ERKI in printmaking (1988) and has participated in numerous exhibitions in Estonia and abroad. Her works can be found in many (private) collections and she has received several accolades. Jõekalda is a member of the Estonian Association of Free Graphic Artists and the Estonian Artists' Association.
87d1e8c8d0328de27b56181c78476b78875ba862: In the upper right part of the picture an irregular, arcaded white stone house, above whose door a canopy rests on forged supports. The stone wall continues from the house with a brown roof, through whose high arched gate greenish-blue trees and bushes are visible. cec92800a9f88f2996769222143e559a76182326: The work consists of four parts. 1. 46331f5c6843fb1586764e1fa265d030757904b9: View of a green meadow in Kadriorg. In the foreground a grassy field with a haystack. A road runs from the right corner to the left with a rider and a dog. On the right an unpaved street (Leineri tn) runs into the depth of the picture, bordered on the meadow side by young trees, and on the right by small wooden houses.
5b03c4a2a132aac348a26bc44cd26b6e01c8f845: Buildings and ships in dark tones with cubist forms. In front, in the centre, a harbour crane with a wagon, of which only the rear part is visible. The smoke coming from the funnels resembles dark-coloured discs. Dirty blue, grey and purple tones dominate the painting's colour range.
bf97e711a14c334ec52ea84ede712d0771aa1442: In a dark brownish-red wall, a sheet-metal radiator, red at the top and green at the bottom, with a white lace handkerchief with monograms "K" in the corners in its middle. In the centre a bluish-reddish, green-edged round clump, with small trimmed bushes and a park path running through it. In the centre a tall, lush exotic plant. Behind the fence a wooded meadow in reddish and brownish-green tones.
99ee3c2f30c0245469dff36a0825321f38b24705: Mila Balti is a painter who has flown into the art scene like a comet, one who is not afraid of gigantic formats, themes requiring skill and technical proficiency, nor shies away from the desire hidden in painting for a total, all-encompassing visual mystery. A pop-like image is combined with baroque pomposity. The story presented in one painting contrasts with or comments on what is contained in another. These are not simply Mila Balti's personal stories, but precisely what matters to everyone. At the same time, when she says one thing, she may mean something else.
8753cb8b24444bb295be226b986c008bcbba2bf5: Studied at the art specialisation school of Pelgulinna Gümnaasium 1992 - 2006 and performing arts at the Estonian Academy of Arts (unfinished) 2008 - ... Has completed the bachelor's programme in full, and in addition, for the purpose of self-development, has participated extensively in the study programmes of other universities. Two-year study at the Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre as a guest student. Two-year full-time study in directing at the Baltic Film and Media School as a guest student. One-semester study at Central Saint Martins London art university as an exchange student.
b26612409b5ab8920d3778c4c116e1f7731bd54f: Liisamari Viik is a video and performance artist. She has completed master's studies in scenography at the Estonian Academy of Arts and furthered her studies in video at the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts (2025). Viik has received the Young Artist Prize (2026), the Eduard Wiiralt Scholarship (2024) and the Helju Rossmann-Schneider Scholarship (2025). As an artist she has worked on various projects in exhibitions, theatre and film. Recently Liisamari has mainly been engaged in exploring, rhythmising and practising inhuman precision.
32132f1658304683a848d77e20ae7557b4a6e0e9: Piret Jürgenson (born 1970) is an Estonian artist who began her art studies in 2007 at the Tartu Rahvaülikool under the guidance of Priit Pajos, and continued her studies from 2008 under Robert Suvi. She has participated in numerous exhibitions since 2008, including the Tartu art annual exhibitions in 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022 at the Tartu Kunstimaja. Her works have also been exhibited at the E-kunstisalong. Jürgenson's work focuses mainly on landscape paintings reminiscent of the South Estonian nature views of the former Pallas artists.
6e85d7773f69762921239d5a9743ad51361b732c: A double portrait of a milkmaid in horizontal format. Composition: The painting is divided into three parts. 2/3 of the picture surface depicts, in profile, a milkmaid crouching (in the centre of the picture) in a white smock and cap, setting a milking machine on a cow. On the left side of the picture, in front of the milkmaid, a cow, seen from behind. 1/3 of the painting is divided in half by a light green frame. Above, a semi-profile face portrait of L. Peips. Below, the year 1976 and the numbers 5323 511 T. Painted in a realistic manner, in brown and green tones. The central part of the painting (the milkmaid) in white, light pinkish, bluish-grey tones.
7ed40ca345c7b5bc334d392fdeb1f299d1d6e71b: Three-part work. On the wider central panel, against an orange background, outlined by wide coloured brush strokes, the shape of a heart, within which is a seemingly old naivist landscape image of a nocturnal river valley with a huntsman galloping on a white horse chasing a hare. In the picture, on both sides, between the tree wings, hunting lodges, moonlight falling on the water. The narrow side panels are both orange pastose surfaces in the upper part, and in the lower parts plastic anatomical models of human internal organs, painted over in a garishly abstract manner. On the left-hand panel the heart model is tinted pink.
16fcc1831d34fa6faadd51c57601c019bd4c64ca: Daria Titova is a Ukrainian artist who began her studies at the Kharkiv Art School and is currently continuing them at the Estonian Academy of Arts. Her work focuses on themes of colonialism and national identity, weaving together personal memories and sensitive experiences. Embroidery serves as a poetic tool for expressing intimate stories and collective memory. In her practice, print, text, video, embroidery, and moving image converge, as she explores the experience of presence and embodiment through materiality.
96becf85de13f10ac50579d9d2878442ec1b7b20: View of the ruins of Pirita Convent from the southern, town-side bank of the river. In the foreground a hilly pasture with sheep and a sitting shepherd. On the left the seashore is visible. Across the river, to the left of the road running from the middle of the picture into the depth, is a low stone dwelling with a row of tiny windows and several farm buildings, enclosed by a low wooden fence. To the right of the road, near the eastern end of the convent, is the area of the convent ruins and cemetery with a group of farm buildings. The walls of the convent church, with the high gable of the façade, rise above the surrounding landscape. The western gable, with its Gothic decoration, is intact.
a084db437341091c7466ff6ccc131e8ae6405944: In 1912 he entered the drawing courses of the Estonian Art Society in Tallinn, which in 1914 were renamed the Tallinn School of Applied Art, and also studied at Nikolai Triik's studio school until 1917, when he was mobilised into the army. In 1916 he became a member of the Estonian Art Society, and in 1917 a member of the art group Vikerla. In 1918–1921 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Paldiski Realgymnasium. In 1920 Haavamägi settled in Haapsalu, where he worked as a teacher of drawing and art history at the Läänemaa joint gymnasium, and thereafter as a freelance artist.
1de9af786abab5ee1ac5eb04f5f9b46ca830d9c3: Andrei Jegorov lived in St. Petersburg from 1887 to 1921. Having lost his hearing in childhood, he studied from 1887 to 1896 at the St. Petersburg school for the deaf and mute. In 1898 he entered the drawing school of the St. Petersburg Society for the Encouragement of the Arts. From 1901 to 1909 he studied as an auditor at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts under Ilya Repin. He furthered his training in Munich at Dmitri Kardovski's studio. He then began working as a freelance artist. In 1919–1920 he was an artist with Semyon Budyonny's 1st Cavalry Army in the tsarist army. Having opted for Estonian citizenship, he worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn. During the Second World War he was evacuated to the rear of the USSR.
703ff91d8d8a181c8cbbf25529ff3f398c5ddcc0: Anu Muiste (b. 1984) holds a master's degree in design from the Estonian Academy of Arts and a master's degree in social sciences from Tallinn University. She is an active member of the Estonian Painters' Association. Her background in psychology, design and the social sciences is also reflected in her work, in which she examines the relationships between the individual and society and the various levels of existence. Muiste's works are introspective, visually ambiguous and conceptually layered, inviting the viewer to perceive the world through organic forms and surrealism.
d5259a1c9ec5533b733e9e8e4dc0bc33b8e1249b: Aksel Haagensen (b. 1993) is a Tallinn-based artist. He completed his bachelor's studies in installation and sculpture at the Estonian Academy of Arts. In his art he engages with questions of photography and documentation theory. He is not so much interested in the content of photographs as in what remains outside the frame or the shot, both physically and theoretically. With the series of light boxes presented at the fair, he explores the capriciousness of the attention directed at photographs and the fragility of the connections between photographs and accompanying texts. The work invites the viewer to take part in the process of viewing.
d12a132ac3b9029dc2073277fc7486ea1b598a5a: In the doorway of a blue room a young, slightly smiling woman is entering, depicted as a three-quarter figure, in a red dress with abundant folds, her head in semi-profile turned and tilted to the right. Her left hand is hidden in the folds at her chest, under her left arm a large green tablet. In the lower left corner on the floor a red-and-yellow drapery form. Through the doorway opens a view onto a bare, desert-like plain in reddish and yellowish tones. Intense colours, with shadows rendered in colours contrasting with the primary tones (light blue, yellow, green).
4ffaa16f0f713e512d30f61c4040de84ad256da3: In a luxurious interior sits a man in a dark suit with a short dark beard and moustache. To the right is a round table covered with a patterned cloth, on which stands a closed bottle of sparkling wine and a tall glass vase with a single rose. The man's right hand rests on the table, his left on his knee. Under his jacket is a light shirt and a dark tie with a tie pin. Behind the man stands a large pendulum clock. Two large mirrors are on the right and left, in which the rest of the room can be dimly seen. In front of the right-hand mirror a small white table lamp is burning.
e1b010eaf76f13659e746c4d8d091cd26fa2de32: The sheet depicts a section of the wall surface of a baroque palace with numerous architectural details. On the left a rectangular two-part window with small panes. On the right, viewed from behind, an atlas supports the console of a supporting beam and is surrounded by two young fauns and two putti. Between the window and the sculptures a fresco, in the foreground of which a group of men - the first young man blowing a horn, followed by a bearded man and another group of men. In the background, in front of columns, an altar with a lit fire, surrounded by men. In the distance a view of a landscape opens up.
52e4bb2421273dde16e8b0b2e050ad70425b908d: A three-dimensional object with figures arranged on two planes on its front side. In the middle, lower, on a light green background, a chamomile-like flower with a long green stem, the bloom with white-painted metal petals at the top of the base, below on either side of the stem variously shaped green leaves (ready-made). On either side of the flower higher semicircular blue planes, to each of which a black-painted oak leaf is attached (ready-made). The object is surrounded by a three-colour frame, the front side blue, the inner edge yellow, the outer part green.
a775e44d2ec9b8aa4641a70dee0de0c7c4fdcd81: Jaan Paavle was an Estonian writer and artist. Paavle published six poetry collections, the first of which, "Vabaarmastus", appeared in 1972. At the age of 35 he entered the Tallinn Art Institute to study ceramics. In the 1990s Paavle became interested in performance art. He taught performance to children at the Tallinn Art School and worked as a guard at the Estonian Museum of Applied Art and Design. Jaan Paavle created ceramics, painted, wrote poems, plays, film and theatre criticism, made a few films himself and appeared in mass scenes of several films
ddf35f0606a5fd872f5d9e8b502c4eed43d9cafd: In the middle panel of the three-part composition a greyish-blue screen with a small yellow circle and yellow-green lines. Behind the screen a brown wooden plank fence, behind which, above, interwoven geometric shapes appear. The brown fence and the pale blue sky continue also on the left and right panels. Behind the fence part of each wing, geometric constructions in grey and yellowish-brown tones appear. Along the outer edges of both the left and right wings, green thread and bushes in the background.
dad27be79817ebd46078a943ff2dd8427f352201: View through open doors into three rooms. In the foreground on the right the corner of a table with a stack of magazines. In the middle, opening towards the viewer, a white two-leaf panel door, through which a view opens into the next rooms. In the middle room on the left, under the window, a table covered with a white cloth, with a bouquet of lilac, three high-backed chairs around it. On the right part of a white tiled stove is visible. Through the open doorway a cabinet corner and a mirror on the wall are visible in the next room. Through the windows located on the left side patches of sunlight fall on the floor. Detailed, smooth painting style.
122e32d853d671a8d45a2f96243f55e6c15bbebe: A conventionally two-part composition. On the left, from the left golden section, a group of green Soviet army soldiers in frontal view, with red five-pointed stars on their helmets up to the horizon with bright stripes of colour, and above the horizon against a background of brown industrial formations. On the composition's right, larger part, among abstract blue-green streamlined shapes, in gold-framed broken circles and gold picture frames, reddish-pink hands with revolvers, a soldier's head in a helmet with a swastika, a woman's head, legs.
c35ab9e36fb9ba8b9da6b0f39d13c084d18b39e6:

eb76fbfc42e56b2e9b297c7c36167b05ba20f8f2: In a dim interior, in front of Ancient Egyptian pharaoh sculptures, two middle-aged men standing and conversing. 01263e793569671f5fe9adfc26f19fab16b5adab: In the right golden section, the half-figure of a bespectacled young man in blue jeans and a yellow striped open-collared shirt, en face, hands in trouser pockets, reaching with the crown of his head to the perspective line. d4e9d97f33968143f8346614ed8156adb7629cfc: In an interior, around a table covered with a patterned cloth, four men are sitting. On the table lie books, papers and an hourglass. 68d534f0d31f87ecb8b2665aaad02fe678e70c57: View from a terrace with a white barrier with a beige, red handrail on the left, to the seashore. 357de9e6f66d6fd47e090d5502d2b2902af5d789: On the right edge of the picture part of a two-storey light-coloured building with a red gable roof, from which a brownish-yellow path leads, surrounded on the left by lush flowering bushes and on the right by a colourful flower bed. Further away, in general vivid greenery, solitary trees, on the right a discernible patch of water. On the horizon, under a pale blue sky covered with scattered cumulus clouds, low houses with red roofs sheltered by gardens.
a8f55e048ebf6d243d5543b4d06fd060e603efce: A figural composition of people pressed tightly against one another, whose main point of gravity falls slightly to the right of the horizontal centre line, since the main part of the mass of people is gathered there. 68e74a19914fef9d6c54a7c8c6abe2e4e8a88077: A man and a woman on a river bridge. 89c20775c927762c646b772c8f284b462d77a94d: Alissa Nirgi (b. 1993) is a photo and video artist who lives and works in Tallinn, currently studying in the final year of the bachelor's programme in photography at the Faculty of Fine Arts of the Estonian Academy of Arts. This project participates in the Riga Photography Biennial in April 2016. Nirgi was awarded the Eduard Wiiralt scholarship in 2015. She is currently preparing for a joint exhibition at the Haapsalu Linnagalerii.
9e277b8b2c4e7b09943dc351bb5460233a2a4641: A confessional dialogue between mother and son, in which the latter, as if forcing himself, tries to say something very important to his mother. In the main part of the video, shot in black and white with a rough, documentary-emphasizing style – presented in an elongated cinematic format, which in turn adds an alienation effect to the source material – the son's dramatic effort at self-disclosure dominates, along with the prolonged expectation of the mother, and also the viewer, that this something will finally be said. This is framed by a more everyday, colour, standard-format segment showing the setting up of the camera, lighting and "performers".
d2d9968a356268b3b49cf8f1206e996c07b7e440: A composition combined mosaic-like from geometric shapes of varying size, at the centre of which lies a female nude, viewed straight on, knees drawn up beneath her. The woman's left arm is stretched out, slightly raised; the hand of her right arm (bent at the elbow) supports her head, which has short straight hair. In the thigh area of the figure, three crosses. To the left of the outstretched arm, a crescent moon. Above the figure, in the background, are other details referring to a landscape (a star, a roof of a house). e2cecbae1b1ddc2f3d43754e4476e8f29fb777d8: Naima Neidre (1943) is a graphic artist, illustrator and watercolourist who has long worked at a high level, whose works, marked by an extremely sensitive visual style, weave together stories of nature, the sea and people. Her works can be found in many (private) collections, and she has received several honours, including the Kristjan Raud Prize (2004). Neidre is a member of the Estonian Association of Free Graphic Artists and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
bd6869646b4a4388898c0bf5e0dcea808504d000: A symmetrical composition, at the centre of which is a stepped, pyramid-like structure topped with a sphere. Inside the lowest step of the pyramid is a coffee grinder with the horns of a gramophone; on the upper steps, orphans in bowler hats and helmets with human heads. In the middle of the sphere, two egg-shaped motifs stacked with a pair of wings; around the sphere a wreath of lions and half pocket watches. On both sides, electric light bulbs, below them fragments of telephones. In the lower part of the image, alternating heads in bowler hats, helmets and bandages, above them a row of oval tree crowns.
92ea4ef66eaeb063d14ece3454ec7f333910356e: The painting consists of a rectangular canvas in the central part and wooden wings of various sizes and shapes attached with hinges at the top of both sides. fe0fd9596804a76d0c7f0230aae66137e3350225: A landscape painted pastosely, with broad, thick brushstrokes in bright colour tones. b85633842b5cc09f4c3876ae863219ed96761007: Video installation for 6 monitors. f29180d7f748d1b4720b595685c2c7185fe963fd: Against a golden-yellow sky, a lakeside landscape where a folk festival is taking place. 7968c0ce04973341f429776b17d5229801b478ff: View of the former Rotermann building in Tallinn. On the right, a corner view of the building - the side and façade facing Narva Road are visible. 63ed36886321c2a652757f4377bfbc502d803a83: The exhibition series "Drama is in your head I-III" (2012-2013) reflected on people's (and the artist's) personal doubts about their surroundings. 14e2d32bfdd5f0933e9e85cd18035895649de4c1: In her practice, Inessa Saarits seeks common ground between art and biology. She is interested in natural and time-changing materials and, in her works, explores the relationship between man and nature, using as elements, for example, tree bark swollen with bark beetle galleries and microorganisms filmed under a microscope. Saarits has graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in installation and sculpture and has furthered her studies at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna. She is a member of ENKKL and a founding member of the young art event "Kunstikompott".
ded5a010644bd109ca46d6dcc6d2e6d068f3146a: Evelyn Müürsepp (eku) is an artist and cultural coordinator living in South-East Estonia. 67109709c53abdaeaf932be866d948097774ba88: Jaanika Peerna (1971) is an artist born in Tallinn who has lived and worked in New York since 1998. Peerna's works can be found in hundreds of private and public collections, and she is represented in the USA by JHB Fine Art and ARC Fine Art. 00ed583af2152b43a2ee3d3c36fa210022ff3ddc: In the foreground on the left, a dense group of demonstrators with a red flag and slogans; in their front ranks, a number of fallen lying on the stone pavement. Kai Kaljos's photo installation concentrates on the working life of the artist, surfacing the paradox of an artist giving away money rather than bringing it in while working, thus questioning the well-known phrase "Time is money". The work was first shown at

The piece features random images from five workdays in the life of an artist, bringing in a total loss of 246 euros. The photos were taken between November 2005 and Februray 2006, with the help from graphic designer Tiina Sildre who added the texts.
4fefae51ee9f8a225a7ab97b08b4e7bdf62aec70: Brightly coloured decorative composition of various figures and shapes. ad26fa53c705062e8324e5dab7fbb70ca4f01921: A late-autumn cityscape with tall white panel apartment buildings in the background, a pyramid-shaped car park at the front left with bare trees and groups of people on its various horizontal surfaces, and at the front right a winding motorway bridge with an interchange running between the panel buildings. 8f27f519693c96ebd10056fa5518c97ceb6d5757: Laurentsius (Lauri Sillak; b. 1969 in Kohtla-Järve) has been called a fetishistic aesthete in his work: he approaches his subject with extreme dedication. Laurentsius's works combine academic painting with pop art. While valuing, on the one hand, the classical still life in the manner of the 17th-century Low Countries school of painting, his oeuvre has also often been associated with kitsch and camp. By skilfully employing the lexicon of kitsch, Laurentsius's works are at the same time a parody of kitsch, joyfully amplifying the elements of kitsch to the maximum.
818249cf314f2f479a67a21e4e73f464b472b844: Natalia Kondratenko is a visual artist. She was born in 1989 (Russia) but now she's based in Tallinn, Estonia. be37877aa1afb41f76d3d071b4a5625672747f84: A metal artist, graduated from ERKI in 1986. Worked as a lecturer from 1991 to 2015, of which 18 years in the position of Associate Professor. He has exhibited relatively rarely, the main emphasis having been on commissioned works, both in historical settings and in connection with contemporary architecture. In the last few years sculpture has interested him more than before, but as a sculptor too he is more material-focused than concerned with organising space or searching for form.
7081d58d23ffbd180ba11b4ae5b987b4e6f684cf: A documentary film of Cubus Larvik's performance at the Vatiteater [Cotton Wool Theatre] located in the small town of Soodevahe in the autumn of 2011. From the tall grass surrounding the building emerges Cubus Larvik, entirely wrapped in cotton wool with his face painted brown, who throws large plastic bundles ahead of himself and enters the building, where he improvises with various objects found there. Camera operator Sergei Trofimov. Editing by Timo Toots and Marika Agu. Sound by Karl Saks.
02abf154af92731104e7660b016aab0fe88318a9: A bust portrait, en face, of a man modelled in yellowish and brownish tones against a dark neutral background, with ascetically sharp, characterful facial features, slightly wavy light-brown hair, wearing a dark green blouse and a dark blue bow tie with red stripes, in a slight turn to the left, with greenish eyes and a probing, sharp gaze directed at the viewer from under his brows. 3dae346cbb772576dc9b00643ba364efd8c858fe: During the eight years spent in Italy, the artist developed his distinctive style. Rubens's versatility as an artist became apparent: altarpieces, portraits, paintings with mythological and allegorical content, and religious compositions. The young Rubens's works were of superb technical execution. By around 1620 his painting style had fully developed. Its characteristics were figures of lush, vigorous forms, passionate movements and brilliant colours. He is characterised by the depiction of plump nude women.
18c54ea9509b760a05311a535e17aaada306c7d3: He was born as the son of a district doctor in Rakvere, and was the stepson of Count Rehbinder, the owner of Udriku manor. In 1814 he went on a study trip to Berlin, then in 1815-1816 to Vienna, and lived in 1817-1820 in Italy, Germany, Switzerland, England and France. b2670ec1fa104fea7df32508dd368cf1b7354d36: Marje Taska was born in 1955 in Tallinn, graduated from the Tallinn Music High School in piano, and studied German philology at the University of Tartu. 19883f5c672f03e4757ff3fa50bbb12405c3a2a0: Andrei Maksimjuk is an Estonian artist. He was born in Tallinn and has lived for years in Milan. 112604e292eafc8a613328ca037c11bf43d82c39: Born (1951) in Jõgeva County, grew up in Ida-Viru County. In 1980 he began studying fine art at the Moscow Art University and graduated with honours in 1985. 9f3df8ab19066822248cba388e4c7c0243853714: Studied at the Estonian Academy of Arts and the Oslo Academy of Arts. Creative director of the publishing house Näo Kirik and design studio AKT7. In the lower right corner, a young man sits on a rock smoking a pipe; beside him part of a standing male figure is visible. In the distance, a grey sea with a boat, above it a pink sky.

At the left edge of the picture, among the trees, a straw-roofed building surrounded by a fence. Compared to J. Köler's watercolour on the same theme, the differences are only in very few details.
b0cc2abf297235a22769b189b576899ce8a460c4: A group of six people in a bluish-green landscape. On the left, in front of a flowering bush, stands a young woman turned three-quarters to the left, wearing a bluish skirt-blouse with a pink jacket around her shoulders. A dog beside her. In the centre, two people sitting on a bench, a girl with braid ends on the left and an older woman glancing over her shoulder. On the right of the picture a young man stands facing forward, hand in pocket. Behind him on the right a young man and a girl in a light blue summer dress leaning against him. The figures are painted with great generalisation, in places emphasising forms with a contour line.
2e58982cc6a6ad9dafd5c02e823c9857682ebf9e: A colourful composition in a naive-caricature style of stylised female body forms and geometric decorative shapes arranged across the picture plane in an arc from the upper left to the lower right. Below, a doll-like torso lying on its side with striped thighs. Lower right, a smaller figure with a mask and female breasts. Upper left, an eye-opening shape and breasts as cones pointing to the right. Individual shapes-forms floating in the upper right in a lilac-brown expanse. Sharply delineated forms, mostly depicted with volume.
f79ae5f373a25ed48211679acc60de97cd8235ac: Ivan Zubaka was born in Western Ukraine and has lived and worked in Estonia since 1982. He has been a member of the Estonian Sculptors' Association since 1993 and a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1997. Zubaka has created several public space works, including the gravestone of Igor Severyanin, the "Men of Vanishing" ("Kaduviku mehed") near the Rakvere Theatre, and carried out the restoration of the Tondipoisid Memorial. Zubaka has received several awards, including art prizes from the cities of Tallinn and Rakvere and the Viljandi city medal of merit.
939344012d7efac705999e98e007ba7047a3dcf4: Tjurina obtained her education in textile design at the Moscow Textile Academy from 1985 to 1990, and subsequently worked as a fabric designer at the Kreenholm Manufaktuur from 1990 to 1993. Since 1994 she has been a teacher at the Narva Art School, consistently contributing to the development of young artists. Continuing her education, she completed the correspondence department of art teacher studies at Tallinn University (2008–2013). She has actively participated in artistic life since 1990, being a member of the Narva artists' association "Vestervalli".
682d9ca50a14f70fe2a20e637c9a1297a1b7279b: Erki Kannus graduated from ERKI in 1981 in the field of glass art. He has been exhibiting since 1976. He has created several works of monumental art for public spaces. From 1989 to 2000 he resided in Germany, the USA and Sweden. Since 2000 he has actively participated in Estonian art, both in solo and group exhibitions, as well as exhibitions in Latvia, Lithuania, Sweden, Poland, Ukraine, France and Bulgaria. In his work he combines various techniques (painting, printmaking, sculpture) and materials (glass, wood, metal) with sound and video.
09ea8035a4645724f573f6f423e44f97c2aa9f0e: Figure of a young woman on skates, resting on one leg, the other leg stretched back, arms stretched back at the sides of the body, in a "swallow" position. Wearing boots with figure skates. Face with strong eyebrows, modelled eyelids, a straight nose and full lips, a graceful long neck. A short skirt and a fitted buttoned cardigan, fastened at the throat, a low round cap on curly hair. The upper body together with the leg stretched back is cast as a separate part, which is attached to the leg resting on the lower oval base with a metal dowel.
62d23a0798aa78729c6131be7e9e71098e01ea2b: born in Dresden as the son of a craftsman, studied at the Dresden Academy of Arts. The writer August von Kotzebue invited him to Estonia as a home tutor for his children; Walther worked at Vardi manor and at the Hageri parsonage in the service of Provost Ignatius, who was a relative of Kotzebue. In 1812 Walther moved to Tallinn and in 1815 became the art teacher at Tallinn Cathedral School. In Tallinn he was the first to work as a lithographer, painted portraits and paintings for church altarpieces. In 1835 Walther received the title of free artist from the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts.
49027d66b10620a7c7727695fb30f89fde6c99af: Lemme Haldre (1955) is a recognised psychologist, family therapist and artist. She acquired her artistic skills at the Konrad Mägi Studio, in various courses and privately under the artist Silvia Jõgever. Haldre's work deals with deeply personal and socially important themes, combining aesthetic pursuits with psychological depth. Her works reflect interpersonal relationships, emotional layers and reflections of the inner world of a person. Haldre is a member of the Tartu Artists' Association.
27853399b4fdd2b00e659a8473445516f3c910a9: On a table with a high horizon and no perspective diminution, covered with a checked tablecloth of crossing straight black and grey lines, there stands in front on the right a metal coffee pot with a large spout and handle, behind it on the left a 3-litre glass jar and on the right a mug. In the left part of the composition, further back, a bottle with a label next to a tall brown paper package opened at the top, and in front of them a small-patterned red headscarf. The background is a brown drapery with reddish-brown and bluish-black shadows.
6ecdacbd8e174fb4d0450baff006cddf5c5473f1: Part of the castle's vertical log wall has been torn away, creating a wide gate-like opening. Crusader knights are rushing towards the opening over logs lying on the ground. In front, fallen knights lie on the ground. The opening is defended by Estonians, who have round shields and weapons — swords, battle-axes, bows and clubs. Above, Estonians can be seen defending the fortress. On the left a log is falling onto the necks of the invaders. Further back on the right, a ladder is placed against the log wall. Germans are climbing up the ladder, arrows flying towards them.
ffa7f1992e508de96fb3834028338161eaf72594: The artist is a saviour, a comforter. When no one needs saving, the saviour must somehow manage — staging situations for himself in which he is needed and gathering around him young disciples who might carry forward his ideas. Those who need saving search among false rescue possibilities. Both are in an awkward situation, where one must advertise himself to the other through a performance. The slides do not actually offer ready-made solutions, but hint at the beginning of the rescue process, its possibility.
f87094a7f5e12fd1e1119e69a2d977da7f72bb61: Lotte Jürjendal is an Estonian multidisciplinary artist whose work combines painting, sound art, textile, installation and sculpture. Selected solo exhibitions: 2022 – "Baroque in Metaverse", Solaris Gallery, Tallinn. The exhibition combined hand-embroidered haute couture, sound and textile painting. 2022 – "Avatars", OKAPI Gallery, Tallinn. An installation exhibition exploring virtual identity, cosmos and embodiment through painting, sound art, embroidered sculptures and light installations.
7b0b1c9f02c8fc2ae974a73b1a56c4f3694460c8: Grisli Soppe-Kahar (b. 1990) is an artist who lives and works in Tallinn. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts' department of fine arts in painting with a BA (2014) and MA (2016). Her first solo exhibition took place in 2015 at Draakoni Gallery; in 2017 she had a large-scale exhibition together with Danel Kahar in the large hall of the Tartu Art House. In the summer of 2018 she was in residence together with Danel Kahar in Italy (Mazzano Romano). Her most recent solo exhibition took place in 2021 at the Tallinn Portrait Gallery ("Someone Else").
259beba674ec63a4c58d1850e02fc621f0820b3f: A large figural composition. In the foreground, women in headscarves standing by grain sacks, one of them holding a notebook and a red pencil. In the middle ground on the right a threshing machine, at which three people are handing sheaves of grain to a man from a horse-drawn load. Two men are collecting grain into sacks. In the middle ground on the left a woman in a blue dress and headscarf, with her back to the viewer, leaning on a pitchfork. To her left a scale with grain sacks and men loading grain sacks onto a truck. In the background a haystack, landscape to the left and right.
1f5448989b6eef528dc0fe56cb2ebb4f2d793744: In the foreground two men in black boxing gloves: the one on the left in a khaki green suit with a wide red stripe on the sleeves and trousers, left hand extended for a punch and touching the opponent's head, a yellow dot under the right boxing glove. The man on the right has green trousers (red stripe on the side), bare upper body, pinkish-red hair. A red line running across the back of the right-hand man continues on the white cords encircling the men behind them. Upper left a fragment of a building. Background green, bright blue sky above.
34f424ffbeadf9fb4cd962db8a8a6a2eb2b84957: Behind a long table covered with books, in the foreground sits a young woman with slightly curly hair parted in the middle, on a reddish-brown chair covered with patterned fabric. In her right hand she holds a black pen holder, with which she rests on white paper, her left hand holds the back of the chair. Her body is turned slightly to the right, right leg raised over the left knee. She is wearing a dark skirt and a blouse with a slightly higher collar. Behind the table on the left, in frontal view, a man with a red cap and in dark clothing, leaning on the table with his elbows. Background dark red.
57f19f85fbd0a830791c892d75315ef827d96ef3: On the left side of the picture the foot of a high hill above large bushes, two small deciduous trees and a sandstone boulder. In the background two deciduous trees and a grove of trees on the horizon to the right. Light blue sky with white and grey cumulus clouds. The foot of the hill extends as a steep, almost vertical wall to a low stony stream flowing diagonally in the foreground, which disappears between shaded trees and bushes in the foreground on the right side of the painting. At the stream, in profile facing the viewer, a girl in a white blouse and red vest, holding a vessel.
d485b12225817d48b9a8115216c4b58637b070d7: In an interior sits a man with glasses. In the background on the right a curtain with a wavy pattern, on the left a wall completely covered with paintings. In the centre of the photo sits a grey-haired man in an armchair, wearing a light shirt and dark waistcoat, his head turned to the right. His right hand supports his chin, left hand on his knee. On the floor of the room two striped rag rugs, on which scattered crumpled and straight sheets of paper are lying. On the right edge a serving table with papers, a cup, a glass bowl and other objects. To the left of the man, on a small stool, a large black typewriter.
b6a358c5ad1f410ecbb9f006522f7296aae9c4a3: Side by side sit a woman with Native American facial features and, behind her left shoulder, an animal of the same size as the woman, with pricked-up ears and black smooth fur. Both gazes are directed at the viewer. The woman is wearing a purple sweater with white trim, her hands in her lap, a striped blanket on her knees. In the centre in large white letters: Ellinor Crimson. Below, smaller: They like nuts for better for worse. Below that: A Trinidad & Tobago Film. At the very bottom in yellow lettering: Carbonary Pictures Presents. In the lower right corner a logo and text: While Away Films
627e5420b6b224a2bc40dc053a42cfcefd019622: Ivika Luisk (b.1969) is a painter and puppet-film artist who lives and works in Tallinn. She completed her bachelor's studies in painting and monumental painting at the Estonian Academy of Arts in 1995 and her master's studies in 1998. Luisk is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Painters' Association. The artist has so far had 15 solo exhibitions, has participated in several group exhibitions and has worked as an artist on 15 puppet films. In her work, an important place is occupied by the human being and nature, their relationship and mutual influence.
79191f810dd77f3d21d9387d2c73927eaa8f9f1f: Hedi Jaansoo (1989) mostly works with small and delicate things, flowers, uncertainties, feelings and sensitivities. In her practice Jaansoo combines photography and installative details. Recurring threads running through her work are women, grandmothers, gentle resistances and less noticeable details. In 2023 Jaansoo took part in a 6-month artist residency at the WIELS contemporary art centre in Brussels. Since 2024 she has been project manager of the Estonian Society of Photographic Art (FOKU) and head of the FOKU gallery.
7200afd82ec49d14eb792fecc66da54c21014075: View of Kadriorg Palace from the avenue leading to the sea. A large footpath runs from the centre towards the background, on which several groups of walkers: in the foreground a gentleman with a top hat and a dog, a lady with a child, a group of three people including one officer. On the left side of the path a fortified slope with grass and a sparse grove of trees, through which the palace's wing building can be seen. In the centre, in an angled view, the main facade of the palace with a balcony. On the right, opposite the wing building, a gazebo, and further along the path on a fortified slope deciduous trees. A sparse tree fence borders the palace grounds.
6f4fbd5bfe74cfe32400185ff53675152d2d723d: Karin Kalman (1962) uses various types of clay in her work – from porcelain to coarse chamotte clay – and fires her works in both electric and wood-burning kilns. Alongside her exhibition activity she works as a lecturer in ceramics at the Estonian Academy of Arts and works in her own Studio Ceramics workshop. Kalman graduated from the ceramics department of ERKI (1986) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad. Her works can be found in several (private) collections. Kalman is a member of the Estonian Ceramists' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
0b4037cf0e57b42f74b760399befdf749133a5a9: Five human figures on roller skates. On the left, in a long dress with a large shawl on her shoulders, a slender young girl standing in profile facing left. In the foreground, in the centre, a girl in profile skating to the right, her head turned towards the viewer, both hands near her ears. On the right, in profile skating to the left, a fair-haired young man in a dark suit. On the right edge, in profile standing facing right, a man in dark clothing with a wide-brimmed hat, his left hand stretched forward as if to cover the figure skating in profile to the left, whose head is not visible.
95918e8796555ff077447edea224e5d1b1bbf47d: A standing, straddle-legged, deformed – especially the head and legs – nude female figure in frontal view among decorative trees, in front of a peach-toned screen covered with light blue clouds. The nude has one hand on her hip, the other at the back of her neck, on the base beneath her feet a bright yellow square, on which stands, to the right, a stool with curved legs, a pot with a handle on a plate with a single red flower. Clear shadows of the figure and objects fall onto the base. The subject is set against a uniform bright orange background. An even, thin orange contour line surrounds the plastically shaped figure and forms.
b3782ebcaaf36bb90fd343b1ef33e29100fb3261: Ulvi Haagensen (b.1964, Sydney, Australia) is an artist, researcher and educator who has worked for years in Tallinn, Estonia. She currently resides in Sydney, Australia. Her artistic practice combines installation, sculpture, drawing and performance with everyday practices, exploring the blurred boundaries between art and everyday life. In 2024 she defended (cum laude) her doctoral thesis at the Estonian Academy of Arts, „In-Betweenness. Studies on the Line Between Art and Everyday Life Through the Eyes of a Visual Artist“.
dfd3595a91274a87d63cb0e0b40a05d09dd18151: Eleriin Ello (1984) is a freelance painter who lives and works in Tallinn. After brief studies in the painting department of the University of Tartu, she earned a bachelor's degree in graphic art at the Estonian Academy of Arts (2007) and a master's degree in painting (2010). During her master's studies she furthered her education at the painting department of the University of Porto in Portugal. Eleriin Ello's work has been recognised with third place in the Baltic Young Painter Prize in 2012 and the Sadolin Art Prize in 2016.
09e27ee60869759522eb293aa87e3a07bf6d2894: Leho Rubis completed his bachelor's studies in painting at the University of Tartu in 2001 and his master's studies in art history in 2010. In his work Rubis delves into the relationships between consciousness, text and fields of perception. Rubis's solo exhibitions have taken place in Estonia, India and Egypt. In 2010 he curated the joint exhibition of Estonian artists „A Gift to Arvo Pärt“. From 2005 to 2023 he was the artistic director of the cultural festivals „Kolmkõla“ and „PaIDA“. Since 2021 he has been the author of the Estonian Classical Radio programme series „Raaga aeg“.
de763b82d077e8fadde0cd55b07a05898f541ca8: Against a dark green background, on the right edge of the work, a life-size knee-length portrait of a young woman. The woman, with light-coloured medium-length hair and a straight nose, is wearing a half-length coat of brown fur, from the collar of which a yellow blouse can be seen. On the skirt large colourful fruits: two yellow lemons, two green greengages and two red apples together with three pale winter lilies of the valley. In the background, as if floating in the depths, two red mugs and one beige mug, on one of which is the sitter's wedding photo, on another a family photo with her son.
1a4aa9b719b48d3d4caecb57048d83eb73c20068: Elo Tamul (portrait painting), undated. The portrait of Vanemuine Theatre actress, opera and operetta soloist Elo Tamul (1913–1994) depicts the actress preparing herself for a performance in front of a mirror in her boudoir. Tamul stands supplely in a feminine pose, her gaze directed into the distance, her hand resting on the dressing table. The soft light and the four red roses visible in a vase on the dressing table, which has carved legs and an old-fashioned close-up lighting lamp, give the overall impression of the portrait a gentle and romantic quality. /text by Liisi Aibel/
c24f8c503dfd4a9a58b480412ad1861436a87766: The surface of the painting is divided into six vertically oriented rectangles of different colours. In the upper row: greenish-yellow, red, dark blue; below: ochre, purple, green. On the coloured surfaces small cut-out spots reveal the lower layers of paint, at the same time forming a certain rhythmic pattern. On the two outermost colour panels in the upper row and on the middle one below, the cut spots are arranged symmetrically in rows. On the opposite rectangles the small holes are concentrated in the centre, forming a small cluster.
81777034489ac411719145b82d8d168ee732040d: A figural composition in pinkish-red and greenish tones: in the centre, an alasti [nude] female figure with closed eyes, Berenice; lower left, a man's figure in ecstasy holds the woman's hand. Both central figures are surrounded mainly by nude figures given as mythological creatures or clusters of human limbs. Above Berenice, a man in a mask, dressed in green, on whose neck rides a nude female figure. In the lower part on the right, three graces holding a veil, on the left a nude man holds a veil, his back to the viewer.
9f009a55ae186f25d99fde5de13942dfd2fa8947: In the centre of the painting, under a large tree, sits a man with white hair and beard, in a long red robe. His right hand is stretched upward, his left holds a kannel [Estonian zither]. To his right, a crowd of people standing and sitting, on the left, on the riverbank, a group of four people. To the left of this group, beside a boat, a single person sitting. In the foreground in the centre, seen frontally, a girl sitting on the grass, on the right stands a mother with a child. Above the mother, in profile, leaning forward, her face turned to the left. Her gaze is directed at the child clinging to her.
66d3e139bdf2651cf003aeacac13b5a2a35d2305: Eve Kask (b 1958) is an Estonian artist who works mainly in the following fields: print, artist's book and photography. Her works have been described in terms of the subconscious, mythicalness, symbolism, expressionism, feminism and anthropological documentalism. In recent decades she has worked mainly on photo projects – "Käsmu inimesed" ["People of Käsmu"] 1999–2004, "Kärberi 37" 2004, "Bussiputkad" ["Bus Shelters"] 2004–2008, "Mida inimesed tahavad" ["What People Want"] 2007–2010. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Print Artists' Association.
c789a8a5a3fe70bd0fd1e0a59127959f083cacad: A figural composition as if drenched in cold blue light: on a seaside rocky plateau covered with stones, tufts of grass and solitary bushes, on the left a bright pink-bodied nude woman, long red hair fluttering in the wind, gaze over her shoulder toward the viewer, a white cloth between her hands. On the right, a muscular man painted in grey tones hurries toward the woman with great strides, his hair fluttering in the wind. In the background a bay inlet with dark blue water, above a sky sparsely covered with clouds. In the lower centre of the picture, a seal's skull.
c45bb25d503bfea70e90d4060338d054a2ae9210: In the foreground on the left, a two-tiered wooden pier bridge, on the lower tier of which men are stacking piles of fish crates being handed over from boats standing by the bridge. On the railings of the higher tier of the same bridge, nets are drying. Lighter, a flat-roofed harbour service building. In the foreground on the right, a rippling water surface, further away a row of schooners at anchor with sails lowered. In the background, against a clouded sky, the silhouette of Tallinn, with the tower of Oleviste [St. Olaf's Church] in the middle section and several smoking factory chimneys on the left.
1b584e50e6585af11d2217087cce3e179ea08ea4: In the right corner an armchair, to the left of it a writing desk, on which lie, on the right side, an ashtray with a pipe, a book and a telephone apparatus; on the left side a vase with brushes, a statuette, a small bottle and a palette on a blue drapery. The drapery reaches to the floor. On the windowsill a ship model. Behind the desk a radio apparatus is visible, on which stands a candlestick. Behind that a bookcase, on which stands a globe. On the left wall hang two gilt-framed paintings, of which the upper depicts a portrait of comrade Lenin; the lower one the artist's self-portrait.
323c126a0a4c319b1e28af3f9ec711e4a50c02c2: In the foreground a wasteland overpiled with pipes, jars, vases, old furniture etc. On the left a hillock on which grows a tree painted in yellow-green. Another, taller tree is placed at the right edge. Under the tree on the right an old milk can. The discarded objects in greyish-blue and red tones, in their depiction fabric has been used in places. Behind the hillock, horizontally across the picture surface, the sea; to the right of the hillock an island covered with trees. Above, in heavy yellow, red and blue tones, a striped sky.
eb1ee55012d035f414ca9fba6d90f4ac2feb0304: In the foreground, five figures given at angles, sitting on a parapet: the first from the left is a man playing a flute, in blue trousers and a blouse, the second a woman in a long green dress with shoulder-length dark hair and a halo around her head, the third a woman in a long greenish-blue dress sitting on a white cloth, with a white blossom in her lap, the fourth a woman in a blue dress and a white kerchief is given in profile, the fifth woman is in a short blue dress and kerchief, playing a double-piped whistle. In the background narrow bay inlets and bluish-pink mountains.
d024170678c99b65f1570291215fe229431463ad: Piret Rohusaar (1961) focuses in her painting practice on music, especially jazz, through which she explores rhythm, presence, and the invisible field of tension between music and the depicted subject. In Rohusaar's portraits, a recognisable image is combined with a musical, fluidly painterly treatment, in which figure and atmosphere merge. Rohusaar graduated from ERKI in painting (1988) and has participated in art life with numerous solo and group exhibitions. She is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.
b032934a3d3dd8a5ed5925c0557f8291f604441f: In front of a beige house stand two elderly women. The one on the left stands in the doorway, a red kerchief on her head, wearing a yellowish blouse, a blue vest and a bluish-toned chintz skirt; black socks and green shoes on her feet. The woman's arm is raised at the elbow and her hand holds a long, pencil-like object. The other woman stands in the centre of the painting. Her hands are on her stomach, palms together. She wears a light blue blouse, a red vest, a blue skirt and a greenish apron. Blue shoes on her feet. Painted in a naive-realist style.
de7a59feb001792bab8d4248c712f59b7054bebb: Kalli Kalde (b. 1967) is a painter and printmaker who graduated from the Tartu Art School in artistic design (1986), then obtained the qualification of a teacher of art education and handicraft from the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute (1991), and has worked since 1991 at the Tartu Art School as a teacher of drawing and print (in the years 2001–2010 also as a lecturer in the print speciality). Kalli Kalde has participated in exhibitions since 1988. She is a member of the Estonian Print Artists' Association and the Tartu Artists' Association.
ec16f584d7ace8582a1abc50707dd40f0c156ca1: A composition of two full and two half figures on a white background. In the centre, a nude figure of Christ (with a blue-yellow striped loincloth around the hips) in a three-quarter turn to the right, hands folded in prayer on the chest. To his right, in side view, a saint holds the orb of dominion above Christ's head. Above in the centre, two blessing hands and the image of a dove. In the lower left quarter of the painting, two half figures, above them the image of a palm. Above the heads of all the figures depicted are faint nimbuses. The painting is executed in the manner of a negative photograph, marked in grey-black.
14b878ccf7014bb3d9b2dc7a6fabb99690c2e4b2: He studied in 1909–1911 in St. Petersburg at the Higher Courses of Commerce and Industry, in 1911–1912 in Munich at A. Ažbe's art school, in 1912–1913 in Paris at private academies. In 1916–1918 he worked as a prisoner of war in Germany in the stone-carving workshops of Rathen and Dresden, in 1917 in F. Metzner's studio in Berlin. In 1919 he took part in the founding of the Pallas art school in Tartu and was a lecturer at the school in 1919–1940, as well as director in 1929–1940. After that he took part in the activities of the "post-Pallas", in 1950 he moved to Moscow. From 1954 until his death he was a freelance artist in Tartu.
9e5d630effbd78b5de2829b916fae3684e34a6b2: Olesya Münd's education and creative work are continuously connected with interdisciplinary pursuits. She has educational and work experience in the fields of fine arts, museum pedagogy and conservation. This has given the artist the opportunity to know the presence of art. Münd holds a bachelor's degree in fine arts from the University of Tartu and a master's degree in art pedagogy from the Estonian Academy of Arts. She is currently studying conservation and restoration in St. Petersburg at the Repin State Academy of Arts.
74ce2e338383f8cc91ed888b4eb7844ca3b9e4bd: A village landscape by a body of water, painted in broken greyish and greenish tones and, in a few places, in harmonising pinkish-violet tones. In the foreground and middle ground, a silver-grey pond with a mirror-smooth water surface. In the foreground, on the left, in the golden section, a small strip of land with a tree with sparse foliage growing on it, which branches from the ground into many long, thin, fragile trunks. In the background, on the shore of the body of water, three single-storey buildings, of which the one on the right is partially shaded by a grove of deciduous trees. A light bluish-grey sky.
dff081ad470dd6eb867abe1bf40a9a5a0ec11b38: A biblical scene of the Crowning of Christ with a crown of thorns. In a vaulted room, in the foreground of the picture, Christ sits in a long robe, his wrists bound together with a rope. A young barefoot man standing on the right presses the crown of thorns onto Christ's head. His movement expresses force and expressiveness such that Jesus is leaning to the right under the pressure. In the background stand a man with a turban and an old Jew, who is saying something to the former, pointing at Christ with his hand. In front, on the ground, lie the broken pieces of a staff.
00ae4ca0f008a92eddf2fbb4c523b81907932851: Loit Jõekalda (b. 1951) graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in photography and print (1986). He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and chairman of the Estonian Print Artists' Association, a member of the Estonian Ancient Art Society (1987), the Estonian Sami Association (1988), the Finnish Ancient Art Society (1990) and the artists' association YDI (1998). Jõekalda has participated in art exhibitions since 1979, has organised solo exhibitions at home and abroad, and has curated numerous exhibitions and events related to print and ancient art.
131137eaabe929e87bbd69b5836db0bd6e814c24: Elina Vitola (b. 1986) is a young Latvian artist who introduces herself as follows: "I have been joyfully learning to paint for almost my entire life, and in 2018 I will complete my master's studies at the Art Academy of Latvia. The exhibitions I have had the greatest pleasure of taking part in are, for example, "Children of the New East" at the Tallinn Art Hall and "Viewing and Reading Room" at Kogo Gallery in Tartu. Recently I have made several abstract paintings, but in the near future I am planning to paint pasta."
545b5e4d7890bef49d663be2c94c1c4b82e710fd: Nils Hint (1986) is an iron artist who uses this material as a means of expression for conveying thoughts and states that are difficult to put into words or imagine without physical presence. Hint graduated from the EKA master's programme in jewellery and blacksmithing (2013) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally. His works belong to several (private) collections. In addition to his artistic practice, he works as an associate professor of jewellery and blacksmithing at EKA. Hint is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.
dc55c02e40f0ada43d04426742c99b4b24c16872: A painting in a realistic style. In the foreground on the right, a young woman with a small girl. The woman has a red kerchief on her head and shoulders, and holds a basket. In the middle of the painting, a girl in a light-coloured dress is walking, with a few twigs in the crook of her arm, a light-coloured kerchief on her head. The woman's head is tilted slightly to the left, the child in a slight turn to the right. To the left of the girl, a fragment of a garden, further back on the left a man standing with his back turned, working the fields with two horses. The colouring of the painting is pastel, in brownish tones. The sky is bluish, the ground brownish-greenish.
8733cd0a276f5645e1da2852d9e746bfc85ffe65: A silicone mask (head) of a man of indeterminate age, with hair. The face is tinted with ready-made cosmetic powder cream, in front of the eyes ready-made plastic sunglasses with reddish frames. Hair: natural human hair on a nylon net, with dog hair added. White plaster teeth partially visible between slightly parted lips. The silicone mask hollow form rests on a balustrade-shaped white ceramic vase, filled with sand for weight. The base of the ceramic form is covered with coloured paper
23b0e7b9b45fffb6b63e9a33a44000439ed260fa: Hannah Harkes (1989) is a Scottish artist and printmaker who has lived and worked in Tallinn since 2012. She graduated (BA) from Aberdeen Art School in Scotland, in the fine art printmaking department (2011), and obtained a master's degree at the University of Winchester in England in the field of death, religion and culture (2019). She has had solo exhibitions in Estonia, Finland, Sweden and the United Kingdom, and has participated in group exhibitions from Xi'an to New York. In 2020 she had the solo exhibition "As long as we make it"
c762ba4c77651649bca11850ea469bd61a114d88: A photo installation on a tall four-wheeled structure made of light-coloured wood. The photo shows a workroom with greenish-yellowish walls and a barred window, in which a pile resembling a steam locomotive is composed of various objects, plastic tanks stacked on top of each other, and folded cardboard boxes.
