The drawing may depict the sauna that stood in the Varangu manor park.
B) In the foreground a river, by which, on the right, a barefoot boy with a fishing rod sits, a hat next to him on the ground. In the middle a group of trees, under which a dog is sniffing a food bag. In the background a house among trees.
f1130b952cc626428644a25ceaa21bbd69e6eec8: The dish is entirely covered with repoussé ornament: on the rim, twisted acanthus leaves, fruits and men's busts with flags. In the central section one can see the goddess Athena with a flag and a shield, a helmet on her head, an owl and a book at her feet. On one side of her is an architectural motif, on the other a battle scene (4 fighting horsemen, a foot soldier and a fallen man). The repoussé work of the dish has been left unfinished in the central section: both scenes are sketched with engraved lines. Alur Reinans surmised that the reason was the death of the goldsmith Holst from the plague in 1710.
acd0c86038ba46307a33f4053e29bebc2792db37: The outline of the geographical map of Estonia with images of coats of arms, portraits, monuments and other depictions. Upper left the coat of arms of the ESSR, the title of the map and the names of the authors. Lower left Tallinn's Old Town as seen from a bird's-eye view, along the bottom edge figures in national costume against the background of farms, above them depictions of the Russalka, Kadriorg Palace, the Song Festival stage, the gable of the Pirita Convent, portraits, etc. Lower right an inscription: EESTI RAAMAT 1525-1975 [ESTONIAN BOOK 1525-1975] together with an image of the emblem and a list of the authors. At the bottom, in a narrow strip, printed from a separate plate, explanations to the map
28386c52f02551eb768b34367c052fb8261fc23b: In the foreground, in a top view, half of a round table, on which, on the left, a jug with roses and, in the middle, in profile facing right, head bowed to the chest, with long wavy hair, a dancing barefoot female figure in a tunic (an antique bacchante). Behind the table on the right, in a full front view, a chair with a backrest. Lower right an outstretched left palm, on which an (Athenian) owl is perched. In the upper half of the sheet a windowsill, on which, on the left, two fighting Ancient Greek warriors, and on the upper right the figure of a flying deity. Between the window panes, on a zigzag spring, a lampshade
38e63723a43f62d943f342abeabedbe06fdffa05: Peeter Sink, who studied at the Tallinn School of Applied Art, gave up the artist's profession as a result of what he experienced in the War of Independence and devoted himself in his subsequent life to the clergy. From then on Sink engaged with art in his free time, creating portraits and landscape views in the family's summer places and in locations to which his service duties brought him. In Sink's work one can sense a resonance with the Estonian modernists of the early 20th century, above all Nikolai Triik and Roman Nyman. The works were donated to the Art Museum of Estonia by Peeter Sink's family.
a1bf4fa05cfc9dcaeb822a9cf7c46fe4cbe347db: Tõnu Tamm (1971-2023) was a self-taught Tartu photographer, inventor, experimenter, rangefinder camera enthusiast, promoter of pinhole photography, and lecturer at the Tartu Art College Pallas, where he gave courses on camera construction and pinhole photography. In addition to building cameras, his passion was colour analogue photography. A substantial part of his legacy consists of shots depicting friends, Tartu's social and night life, and street scenes, characterised by a distinctive viewpoint, warmth and humour.
2ad5753a7e881cce51992bc9ae2d82e8ade96f11: In the foreground on the left a small hovel, on its threshold a mother with a child in her arms and a small boy playing with a tank, inside the hovel, behind a table, a man sitting with his hand on his cheek, in the centre foreground a standing madonna figure, at her feet, on boxes, a small child sitting, a little further away, on the right, a hovel, in front of it an older woman holding a bowl, diagonally to the left a clothesline with white sheets hanging on it separating the life amid the ruins from the round-domed church nearby, a taller building, and a column with a figural composition widening from above.
2d15e2d74342a4679365daba51d00fb02cba9848: At the top of the sheet a ship and radio waves radiating from it, in the middle of which a red stamp with a portrait of Marconi. The image is supplemented by text in red: "In 1902 the "Cardo Alberto" went to sea with a new Marconi antenna. This antenna made it possible to carry out long-distance radio transmissions. In July of the same year the "Cardo Alberto" made a stopover in Kronstadt, Russia. Senator Marconi's later radio experimental yacht "Electra" also went down in history, from whose onboard radio laboratory Marconi attempted to capture radio waves from the planet Mars"
fa3d842b95af7f762cf2a5c94c1664baaa5f938b: Martin Järv, born in 1853, received his art education in watercolour at the Art School of the Petersburg Society for the Encouragement of the Arts. Although he worked in the field of engineering his whole life, he still managed to engage in artistic creation on the side. The watercolours by Martin Järv held in the Art Museum of Estonia, which are mainly landscape or interior views, are interestingly complemented by a self-portrait in pastel technique from 1905, which excellently conveys both the spirit of the era and knowledge of the artist himself.
b0e47cadd09c5953f45d03f8197fa0364d62c2ba: The caricatures of book illustrator and caricaturist Elle Tikerpää complement well the collection representing this field in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. As a conceptual continuation of the tradition of satirical images formed in the early years of the Republic of Estonia (Gori, Otto Krusten and others), these (e.g. alongside Heinz Valk's caricatures) dissect the topical social problems of their era – moving toward the context of the Soviet period and the time of Estonia's restoration of independence, where witty collages hold a separate place.
6c454d2e472721c2e928e7b8f22c807f45f3953a: A café scene: in the foreground on the right a table covered with a white cloth, on which a man in a black jacket, grey trousers and a bow tie leans with his right hand holding a cigarette. In front of the man a half-finished glass of beer. Behind the table stands a waiter in a black suit, a white towel over his right arm, writing down the order. On the left edge sits a lady in a mustard-yellow dress and a hat of the same colour, a reddish-brown scarf on the armrest of the chair. In the background isolated figures of guests and waiters. The background is bluish-green, reddish-brown from the upper right.
897f3ddbbf276c1f0a4b03014bdf3efefcad1419:
Anna Triik-Põllusaar (1902-1999), born Anja Põllusaar, later Anna Kompus, was one of the first Estonian female artists. She graduated from the Art College Pallas in 1926 as a painter. In 1944 she fled to Germany, in 1949 she moved to Australia.
As the student and wife of Nikolai Triik, influences of Triik's work can be seen in her, but her works, especially portraits, are characterised by a particular sensitivity.
Anna Triik-Põllusaar's drawings and watercolours from various stages of her creative work are a valuable addition to the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.
49b38016ab480916ac4608cb8bae6a9a66b99df1:
A) A composition of six standing male figures. In the foreground at the sides two nude figures, the rest in short skirts, round-crowned hats or horned caps. The print still lacks the sword in the middle figure's left hand and the ring on the head of the second figure from the left.
B) At the top, within a curved frame, the inscription: КАЛЬМА.ЗНАКОМЫЕ. Below it, in the centre, a standing boy in frontal view, in knee-breeches, a cap on his head, a bag over his shoulder, an apple in his left hand. Around him animals: an owl, a cockatoo, a roe deer, a monkey and others.
4879053003861c581f21cecafb9197b046339d4a: Keiu Maasik, who works mainly in the photography and video medium, has chosen memory, identity and interpersonal relationships as the focus of her work, which reveal the contemporary Estonian person on both a personal and a societal level. She often approaches these themes through personal experiences and memories. In the work "Kolm venda" [Three Brothers] the theme of weapons is raised. Keiu Maasik's camera focus remains firmly on her close circle, whose portrayal leads to eloquent generalisations characterising the spirit of the times.
ca18a09cd6bb8ad752eb891a8283c5b7077fb3e9: The most radical work of the female artists of the Tartu circle of friends was created in the second half of the 1950s, when Valve Janov, Silvia Jõgever and Kaja Kärner experimented with abstract compositions and explored the limits of collage technique. Kaja Kärner is known in Estonian art history primarily as a painter of period genre scenes, whose main interest was not modernist formal experiments. "Nofretete" [Nefertiti] shows a lesser-known side of Kärner as a master of collage who playfully distorts Soviet reality.
0337d6094ec0b95f69f5665ffd2c67bdcc55cd24: A fragment of a teahouse interior with three tables, seen from above. At the table in the foreground, the man on the left is peeling a potato, the middle one is holding a bottle, and the one on the right is drinking tea from a saucer. In the back on the left – an old woman and a bearded old man behind a samovar, in the back on the right two men, one of whom is pouring a glass of vodka. At the top centre a window with the inscription: ЧАЙ. Company trademarks in metal have also been used as decorative elements (bottom centre 1 II 14 Н.ЖАРОВЪ С.П.Б. and top centre ВАГНЕРЪ И СЫНОВЬЯ НОССЕНЪ)
4dd1037528f4b6e468155403f3bce73bbe5437a8:
Nikolai Kummits (1897-1944) was one of the important artists of the Pallas school, who often used the monotype technique. Kummits preferred human themes such as poverty, loneliness, modesty, etc., which he depicted very suggestively.
The monotypes "Pliidi ees" [In Front of the Stove] (1938) and "Rändaja" [The Wanderer] (1935), part of the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia, show the warm colouring characteristic of Nikolai Kummits. They are also typical of him thematically: an old woman and a child warming themselves, and a lone traveller in a landscape.
b7b08cf33841909a8ac69d832f633727854cc724:
An older man standing in high boots and jodhpurs, under the smiling man's feet a map of Estonia full of footprints. A composition in a rectangle, below which the author's text:
An attack on Naan is truly baseless, for just think, how can
a being with cosmological and global interests, who since
1956 has been tormented by large-scale lacunae, notice
unportrayable non-existent parish-sized patches at his feet,
therefore let us protect Naan! Three freight trains full of
Eilarts are fair exchange for one Naan!
6dc1ab3d17b05dda82802047332b952c29366aab:
1) In the foreground three bare-chested men, the one on the right bent over. Behind, an industrial enterprise with chimneys, towers and outbuildings.

Signature on the plate at the top right (monogram): EW.

There are no inscriptions on the verso or recto.

2) An old man's seated full figure, half-turned to the right, hands together above the knees. On the man's head a felt hat, behind, on the left wall, a four-paned window, on the right a devotional picture, on the floor a mouse.

Signature on the plate at the bottom left: Mar↑ Konk 1928
At the bottom right (monogram): EW MCMXX

There are no inscriptions on the verso or recto.
efb21157765a74550d85024d7c3a1e0902a56153: On the street, on the left, behind a low table with fish in a box on it, sits a bearded man in a felt hat, in half-profile to the right. Facing him, in full view, a standing woman in a checkered skirt. In the centre, a basket in her right hand, a standing woman in half-profile to the right, where, in half-frontal view, bent forward, to the right, a woman, her hands in an elongated vessel. Facing her stand a woman with a white apron on the right and a man leaning forward in half-profile to the left. In the back on the left, standing by the wall of a house, a man facing forward and a woman in profile to the right.
03052368bfc98a3a5b5b5250043b45573a8c5c56:
The small drawing has been attributed to Eduard Wiiralt by analogy. The EKM collection contains 36 sketches by E. Wiiralt on the lid or bottom of a matchbox from 1944-1945.
That Wiiralt also engaged in this kind of overdrawing during the first Soviet year is confirmed by a drawing of political content on a 1941 wall calendar (EKM G 28175). On the latter is Wiiralt's signature E.Viiralt. On the verso of the matchbox label "Naine rätikus" [Woman in a Headscarf] there is a pencil inscription Viiralt 1940. Thus this small found object can be attributed to Wiiralt.
ea7f69022da74db2a2dc0ccf033876907e8fdc1c:
A) A weeping mother with a child in her lap, both slightly turned to the right. At the top left a man's head in frontal view. All in a vigorous line.
At the bottom of the image, printed horizontally, a small female figure – walking from left to right, in a costume and high shoes.
B) An old man's head, slightly turned to the right, lowered.
Crossing the image, two trial proofs: a skiing Santa Claus with a tree and a bag, a Santa Claus listening to a rhyme from children. The tree and bag on the ground on the right. In the upper right corner of both proofs: RÕÕMSAID JÕULU PÜHI! [Merry Christmas!]
6d93596a09cdcae32d20971f2fbcef6b11dcba1e: Diana Tamane's main medium of expression is photography. Since 2008, when her half-sister Elina was born, Tamane has been photographing the time they spend together. The project uses one particular place as the setting for the action, which makes the passing of time perceptible in the works both visually and metaphorically, and certain recurring motifs come to the fore. The greenhouse serves the role of a studio, and it is there that the traditional annual portrait is taken, forming a timeline of Elina growing up.
eb8f4a9e3dc643dfed0c0670d4f00449ecd9a745: A composition printed from a two-part plate. In the upper part, a map of the Baltic Sea and the surrounding lands. Along the upper edge, depictions of the oldest Estonian sailing ships, on the left in the middle a coat-of-arms-shaped title, on the right in the middle an excerpt from the "Estonian Sailing Sport Yearbook". Below on the left, the emblem of the Moscow Olympic Games, the silhouette of Pirita Convent and a row of yachts. Below on the right, a panorama of Tallinn with sailing ships in the harbour. The lower part of the work presents the history of sailing in Estonia with pictures illustrating the text (building of a sailboat, etc.)
de0faf26c890700a6aa228ff5fe06c1f8cd28845: Colour digital print on Kapa board. A stone ball stands on a stone base. A girl in an old-fashioned white underskirt rests her right foot on it. She wears old-fashioned black lace-up boots, old-fashioned white gloves on her hands, and on her head a bonnet tied under the chin with ribbons. Her right hand rests on the raised leg on the ball and holds a black bag. Her left hand at the hip below holds a bunch of gladioli. The background is a bright pink fabric drawn taut. Above, a blue sky is visible. View to the left.
6c4a52838af1dd9cc92693f8980312d6f8fbf257:
The object consists of two parts made at different times. The miniature composition "Knight in the Fence" decorating the upper part of the bell is particularly valuable and rare, dating from the Gothic period (2nd half of the 15th century). In one hand the knight holds a flag, in the other a shield with Tallinn's coat of arms. This is the oldest secular-purpose silver vessel in the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.
The lower part, i.e. the table bell, was made for the Kanuti Guild in 1799 by the goldsmith J. J. Öhrmann, who also mounted the "Knight in the Fence" onto it.
f734cc0daca10204890f9822402c29a90bf0e4fe: On a plate shaped like a postage stamp, a dark oval, surrounded by a background filled with bubbles and pebbles, in the corners of which, on the right, winged letters И and Э, in the left corner a light curved band with the date "25•XII•83" and in the upper left corner a tiny winged horseman. Below the oval, biomorphic shapes, on top of which a goblet, in the middle an image resembling two heads on long necks. Above, a U-shaped opening in which there are two goblets, on either side of it inverted-U-shaped objects, inside the left one a bell on a cord
e665a9f2fec3da6f756acf2081249639e3ad7e8d: A group of people walking to the right in darkness, at the very front a woman with fluttering coat flaps, a large portfolio under her left arm, a smaller portfolio and a purse in her right hand. Behind her an older woman, a child in her arms and a tied bundle in her right hand, further back the dark half-figure of a man, a man with a hat, a large bag on his back, a suitcase in his right hand, and a woman with a bundle under her right arm. On the left, in the lower corner, a bearded old man as a three-quarter figure in half-profile to the left, crouching forward, holding a large bundle. In the distance, a burning house
6374bda80430e3b75c3ab8e62afa27422126840d:
Agathe Veeber's 1974 engraving "Two Women", acquired for the museum from an art collection belonging to an exiled Estonian in Canada, complements the museum's overview of this recognised Pallas artist's work.
The work depicts two women side by side and is connected with Veeber's pre-war drypoint prints, but even more so with drawings made in America in the 1950s–1960s. The artist may have dedicated all these compositions to her sister, who lived in Latvia and with whom she maintained correspondence for decades.
b6dcb2758383302157a3d492d74d933b31b7e502: Inge Kudisiim is a painter, graphic artist and illustrator active in Tartu, who made her public debut with her work in 1974. Kudisiim's creative model has been considered to be the Far Eastern art tradition, more precisely Zen Buddhist ink painting. We often encounter Japanese-style figures, and the works are accompanied by haiku by Matsuo Bashō. But we also see more universal moments and characters, very fragile and emotional. Among the creators of the haiku featured in her works is also the poet Lembit Karu,
a8681c31cbb3b3b62b2edd4a8ff67e1338f72765: Six heads across the sheet. Upper left, the head of a woman with loose hair in a frontal view, her right hand raised in front of her left shoulder. Upper right, the head of a short-haired woman in a slight turn to the left. Middle left, the head of a woman in a half-turn to the left. Lower left, the head of a child in a frontal view. Lower middle, the head of a woman in a slight turn to the right. Middle right, the head of a child in a slight turn to the right. The lower right area of the sheet is left untouched. All faces have a tense expression, except for the last-mentioned child, who is smiling.
d40127b714cec178b32ce28f9ac23120157ed728: Ada Otema's work brings to the Art Museum of Estonia's graphic art collection an example of the work of an author not previously represented there, and is also a good addition to the collection of works by Estonian émigré women graphic artists. Ada Otema, a poet, writer and graphic artist who studied at the State School of Applied Art, created this intaglio-technique composition, in which one can find references both to the pre-Second World War Estonian tradition of graphic art and to the life and artistic experience in Sweden, which became the author's new homeland after the war.
f79c580ffdf170811d03348f4e2ee3a217ded7b5: Drawing played an important role in Sooster's art, functioning as a creative laboratory for experimenting with very different methods, ideas and images. This work is a vivid example of one of the author's favourite devices, in which fantastical and surrealistic characters are created by swapping the places of parts of the human face. Paraphrasing Leonardo da Vinci's iconic work, Sooster moves from the modernist discourse based on originality into the postmodernist world of playful quotations.
025d9d19b8beb1f462b94e27f08db888419b3a37: On a black background, three slender young women standing in long white dresses, and a boy. The left-hand one in profile to the right, breasts bare; the middle one in half-profile to the left with four bare breasts; the right-hand one almost in profile to the left, belly bare, an envelope in her left hand. In front of them, on the right, a boy in a white costume in a frontal view, in front of his thighs a disc with a dark core, to the right of which a bird with a snake's head positioned vertically. In the background, rectangles, corners, circles and crosses drawn with red lines
442ba71129f70c2498a3ba1fa7033151262c6af3: Both the cup and the saucer are engraved with views of Tartu: the cup is dominated by the town hall together with the buildings of Town Hall Square, and the rim of the plate by the Inglisild (English Bridge). In addition to the views of Tartu, the rim of the plate is decorated with an engraved ribbon ornament and two floral motifs. A three-line text has been rubbed off from the underside of the plate, of which only individual letters are visible. Interestingly, Nagel has used differently designed maker's marks on the cup and the plate: on the plate Gothic letters, on the cup antiqua letters.
55a11ab61aaa799e90cb136e746f89a22a68ea60: This is a work representing a notable creative stage in Elmar Kits's oeuvre, marking the experiments with abstraction of imagery that took place from the end of the 1950s onward, alongside realistic commissioned works. This composition testifies to the beginning of Kits's abstract explorations, and the Art Museum of Estonia's graphic art collection previously had no similar works; the examples in the painting collection currently belong to a later period, the 1960s and 1970s.
81ba9bf5fb1f1e400f9c84ee5c14f68124a18a49:
A portrait figure of a young man with dark hair and a moustache. A stout lady holds onto his right arm. Behind his left shoulder, the half-figure of a clinging woman. The composition is in a rectangle, below which is the author's text:
To love means to choose.
As Estonia's most popular film actor Lembit Ulfsak stated, for him
choosing between cinema and theatre was just as inexplicable a process
as choice in love. And although Lembit loves theatre terribly,
he went into film anyway.
d1826e0800cabb4fe90f6f66ee039eabcb2d4f83: A rare example of the early work of Natalie Mei, one of Estonia's first modernist artists, which nicely complements the paintings, watercolours, costume designs, etc. by her already held in the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. The work was apparently inspired by the surroundings of the Tallinn Mine Harbour, where the Mei family lived at the time, and is connected both in content and style to another early watercolour depicting a sailor in the EAM collection (G 28066). It is also a rare example of a paper-cut from the 1920s in Estonia.
40a94516ab2c159333f59149e49217e3f2af6f9f: Vello Vinna's works are a remarkable example of the creative output of the generation of Estonian graphic artists that emerged in the late 1960s – early 1970s, whose distinguishing feature is a coherent and emphatically individual pictorial system. Vello Vinna's etchings, photo-etchings and collages from the 1970s–1980s, which give recognition to the formation and development of his system based on symmetry and play on images and words, are an important addition to the Art Museum of Estonia's graphic art collection.
17918979052a182e060fab65b489ffc270bcb674:
A linocut on both sides of the sheet, together forming two pages of a portfolio. Unfolded size 39.2x65.9 cm

1) In the background a factory and towers, against which three working figures. The work is in an expressionistically angular form.

Signature on the plate, lower right (monogram): EW 1920.

There are no inscriptions on the verso or recto.

2) A path running between trees from the lower left to the upper right, on which a couple of human figures.

Signature on the plate, lower right (monogram): EW.

There are no inscriptions on the verso or recto.
2e805a63d687c7447f4c49eead9dc2f7a4df8b83:
Maara Vind's (b. 1955) work has largely developed within the sphere of influence of her artist brothers Tõnis and Toomas Vind and sisters-in-law Mare and Aili Vind. Her pictorial world is recognisably individual.
Clearly legible, linear drawings express an aesthetic and elitist attitude towards the surroundings. Maara Vind's drawings are hermetic, full of various symbols and mythological motifs from nature, Christian religion, freemasonry, etc.
1e0e4361b247031a1d1f5a986675a97374dd2f97:
An older man sitting in half-profile to the right, with dark hair combed over his head, tousled eyebrows and long drooping moustache shaped like a lady's legs. In his left hand an open book, in his right a pencil. His right leg is over his invisible left leg. Below, the author's text:
And here, dear Estonian women, you see this unworthy man,
who has been loved by a Japanese woman. At the same time, the
creator of the picture grants, with copyright permission, the right
to print this portrait of Heino Kiik on your pillowcase.
bd5445867b6b8a30b982e484c05286feb4746f62: A woman's act with long hair, seated lower right, leaning on her left hand, right hand on her thigh. Beside her stylised sculptures. In the middle a little man standing on his knees, head in profile to the left, pointing left with his right hand. On the left two little men: one holding a book, the other's quarter figure partly visible, both holding a white chess piece in front of them with both hands. Upper right an elk's head, in the centre a little man looking out of a window opening, and on the left stairs ending in an arched doorway.
96a2d6a4df5775bcedeb5b7ffe740b4c846ecc68: Composition of three standing female figures, the left one in a slight turn to the right, leaning on her left leg, arms bent at the elbow brought up to the chest, thin cloth around the hips, the right female figure in a slight turn to the left, holding with her left hand a cloth thrown over her right shoulder, exposing her right breast, the hand of the rear woman at the right shoulder of the left figure, the gaze of the rear and right women directed towards the left figure.
cae621000248295cbf904af9293c7bc70900728d: Anna Elisabeth von Maydell (1861-1944) was a Baltic German painter and applied artist, from whose oeuvre two furniture designs from the early 20th century belong to the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia (EKM). The present work is likewise connected with Anna von Maydell's interest in applied art and stands out among the other sheets in the EKM collection for its degree of elaboration, thus complementing both the artist's own oeuvre and, more broadly, the work of Baltic German women artists in the EKM collection.
3784c5baf0cd10e22221c0b8133de2ba59b77ca6: In the foreground lower right, on a footpath by the river, a man standing in profile to the right, a woman with a basket in frontal view, and a boy in profile to the left. In the middle, diagonally, across the river a massive bridge built of stones on two thick semi-cylindrical pillars with two supporting arches. On the bridge two three-bayed triumphal arches. On the left edge, in the middle on a rise, a human figure inside a small garden under a tree, looking towards the bridge. In the background multi-storey town houses. Along the upper edge branches of a deciduous tree.
c47a946f4466c05b87d2a26a4bfc40a5dac451be: The artist stands against the background of a large white stretcher frame and speaks in English. At first she smiles, in the middle she is serious, at the end she starts to laugh. "Hello! My name is Kai Kaljo. I am an Estonian artist. I weigh 92 kg. I am 37 years old, but I still live with my mother. I am not married. I work at the Estonian Academy of Arts as a teacher for 90 dollars a month. I think the most important thing about being an artist is freedom. I am very happy." Her text is answered by mocking laughter.
e224a056f95ae213ba15cf526d067203db698d82: The work belongs to a folder of sketches (6 notebooks) arranged by Märt Laarman. The drawings and engravings are preliminary works for Fr. Tuglas's "Väike Illimar" ("Little Illimar"). The notebook contains 50 different designs, of which 5 photographs have been uploaded to Muis. The designs and proof prints depict a rooster 3 times, a crow 2 times, a sleeping child 8 times, an apple tree 4 times, a woman winding yarn 8 times, a frog 2 times, rain 7 times, masks 4 times, a building with two chimneys 4 times, two seated figures 2 times, in a sauna 3 times, a winter road 2 times, a spruce branch with candles 4 times.
0f6f739b1306f6b746d414bd70fb920a0c099be9: A map of Estonia depicting sacral buildings. Upper left, a plan of Tallinn Old Town, lower left a plan of Tartu city centre. Along the left and bottom edge 13 sacral buildings of republic-wide importance. Along the right edge 6 sacral buildings of all-Union importance. Above, depictions of Pirita and Padise monastery and imprints of the seals of monasteries, castles and churches. In the lower part an additional list of monuments and title with a depiction of an angel bearing a church model, lower right.
ae319eda01921b1d7f49370a0949b3fd704ce094: Popov's first wireless receiver, below a red stamp with Popov's portrait. The depiction is complemented by a red-coloured diagram of the receiver and inscriptions, above "With Popov's first wireless receiver it was possible in 1895 to register natural electrical discharges from a distance of up to 20 km. Ten months later (1896), the first wireless telegram in Morse code was sent by means of Popov's device, its content being "Heinrich Hertz"" and below, lower right, "Electrical diagram of Popov's first receiver, 1895"
81b7886054fbb1f88f88d323b03ea7f147691a98:
A frontal portrait of four men, in the background a tall column with plants, the whole composition within a rectangle, below which the author's text:

exhibition of four painters (from the centre: Olev Subbi, Andres Tolts, Tiit Pääsuke and Ando Keskküla), which also allows one to read out their kindred
spirit in the future. Leaving aside the conditional mood, one can
afterwards boldly say: "These boys have become painters! They are
painters!"
a2ad7c11178afe33345d5853bcaf075e7e817381: In a richly decorated interior, in the middle a woman seated in an armchair with carved legs, in profile to the left, left knee over the right, wearing a festive headdress, gloves and a short dress. 8ce8a0f54f98f76f00fb587465910979005131f0: Comic-like pictures of art politicians (Union of Artists - Heinz Valk, Jaan Elken, Anu Kalm), with Russian-language text inside speech bubbles. Translation of the text: I do not remember such a middle period of modernism - a flourishing socialism! Now unworthy of art and dilettantism (love of the thing)... Does the candidate have sufficient toughening? Full of a sense of responsibility I declare before you: Ando's mistakes will not be repeated, I am a man! And so that nothing would spoil his reputation, he carried out castration with his own hand.
a483628b65d384fb7677fe0a8e395b2b92b524db: The Atelier for Applied Art (Atelier für Kunstgewerbe), founded in Tallinn in 1904, was an innovative undertaking of its time and an important step towards the professionalisation of local applied art, but its activity has been little studied and documented. Of the atelier's furniture designs, mainly works with Anna von Maydell's signature have survived, which is why the design created by Lilly Walther, a woman artist connected with the other atelier, is an important addition to what has so far been known.
4d1f8e7181e280044881333b92cf33b399862649: A woman sitting on a wooden chair (diagonally to the left), pensive eyes lowered down to the left, in her lap, between her hands, (diagonally to the right) a small child sitting, gaze directed at the viewer, mouth slightly smiling, left hand placed on the mother's left wrist, the woman wearing a round medallion around her neck, dressed in a knee-length striped skirt and a short-sleeved blouse with a diamond pattern, over it an apron, the child wearing woollen socks, dressed in a short dress, the background dark.
832d0e9688bedbd293c21d63fa6de15188548774: Gunnar Neeme's multi-part oil painting "Tartu" arrived at the Tartu City Museum through the mediation of Marin Laak, an employee of the Estonian Literary Museum. Gunnar Neeme's archive and paintings arrived in Estonia from Australia with the support of the "Compatriots Programme" project. This work is a fine addition to the already existing collection of Gunnar Neeme's works at the Tartu City Museum. This painting is important for expressing the feelings and memories connected with Tartu of an artist living in exile.
bab473ae00afbcdd959b97a11f3a6a04b07b355e: Painted in oil on cardboard, depicting a stylised human head figure in brown tones against a dark background, with a black crown on its head, the painting is attached to a wooden frame painted in dark brown-golden tones, on the reverse kraft paper is glued to the edges of the painting to attach it to the frame, and two metal loops are attached to the frame, through which wire is passed for hanging, in the lower corner of the painting on the left the artist's signature together with the year
c95a9fdf4e1216b07233ee62259f8c8b5e347a2c: In fifteen colour photographs Linnap himself poses at the foot of the crumbling Nikonov monument in Kadriorg, Tallinn. His comic gestures range from a merciless caricature of the heroic tradition of depiction to playfully undignified poses that show the effort of climbing the monument. "After-monuments" aggressively mock the missing monument, as if trying to cleanse national consciousness of the burdensome layers of memory gathered there.
51de94ab7821d9c5e764408ee1b61fee0277f847: Evi Tihemets is one of the outstanding figures in Estonian post-World War II printmaking, who had to prove herself as a strong independent graphic artist in the male-centred art world of the late 1950s and early 1960s. From Tihemets's period of formation as an artist comes a notable collection of self-portrait sketches, which bears witness to the young woman artist's search for identity and self-assertion, and to a persistent self-observation and analysis.
73c2b46db154480ea88394e23e260cb0899678df: Above in the centre an ornament and text: KANNU KÕRVAD (JUG HANDLES). On the right the lower part of a handle and fastening hoops (three above, two below), below the text: KAILDA-KÜLA SAAREMAA 5. (3243). 3fb1cbb1648d626487b898c0879625c78ff0a5c9: A grassy clearing by the river filled with a celebrating crowd of people. In the foreground a body of water in a narrow horizontal strip, on the left below a boat with three people, a fourth holding on to the edge of the boat in the water. By the shore in the water three people, on the right on a small piece of board two boys fishing. On the opposite bank, on an open ground, many people sitting, drinking, dancing, playing ball, on a swing. In the background on the right under a large tree two trucks, on the left-hand one people on top.
0429fe69d80cfa90989cb3f31ff17206778fafe9: Peeter Alliku's drawings and print graphics are a remarkable example of the developments in Estonian print art after the restoration of independence, and are thus a fine addition to the graphic art collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. Based on high technical mastery, Alliku's linocuts combine a dialogue with (print)(art) history with a witty treatment of the new social situation and changes in the art world, which often take the form of absurdist allegorical images.
574e12c0b8d168e0cae039c50437777345544b97: On the left in the foreground two men wearing hats stand facing each other, hands in pockets, the one on the right holding a walking stick in his left hand. Their conversation is observed by two hatted men standing in the background. On the right a trio: behind, a woman standing with hands on hips, and in the foreground a shouting boy holding a stick in his left hand and a man standing in waistcoat and slippers, onto whose head a riding boot (as a horse's head) has been pulled, with a string hanging from it held in the boy's fist.
a08cf8b9cd5c0c7bfdd7c1af6e2e162a0a5257b3: Kadri Toom has focused on experimental contemporary print art. From nature motifs and architectonic forms — in this series also images of Buckminster Fuller's domes and historical greenhouses — she creates mystical, silence-filled coloured spaces. The artist uses very different techniques: cyanotype, relief printing, screen printing, intaglio printing; she prints her plates herself, all works are unique, each with only one impression.
79e3ce3dff0628c1058095c01cd3edf73db919f2: A landscape view in impressionist style. In front on the left a tall tree crown in green tones with red blossoms. In the foreground below a fjord. In the middle part of the painting a green headland, partly covered with trees and bushes, which does not reach the right edge of the painting. In the background bluish-green mountains, with dark green forest at their base. In the upper part of the painting the sky, greenish in tone lower down with whitish clouds, and higher up light blue with pinkish-bluish clouds.

b044f3fb95fe6c5f45f9311b9fa2bf4c83ea993e: The works of Agathe Veeber (1901-1988), a printmaker who graduated from the Pallas art school in Tartu in 1939, left Estonia in 1944, and later gained recognition in American art life, are a valuable addition to the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. Veeber's estampes (some of which are unique copies within the EKM collection), a monotype and 12 original drawings make it possible to further supplement the comprehensive body of her works in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.

89d7c885551834c689abb5484428fceb5cf7b790: The portrait of Kristjan Teder is a somewhat exceptional work in Richard Kaljo's graphic oeuvre. Differing from the direct and vivid treatment of character typical of the author's rather dry manner, it reflects the artist's somewhat awkward attempt to adapt to the imposed depiction methods of socialist realism. The portrait, depicting the painter Kristjan Teder a few years before his expulsion from the Estonian SSR Artists' Union, is also of interest from a cultural-historical viewpoint.
92fae54402f85a30601bca5235e9781dc95a73b8: This is a strong example of the work of one of the most notable and distinctive Estonian printmakers of the 1970s, which is a good addition to Marju Mutsu's collection in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia. Like the etchings "Mets" [Forest], "Suvi" [Summer], "Suvi on punane" [Summer is Red], "Kaev" [Well] and others, the composition in question represents an approach typical of Mutsu's graphic art of the 1970s, in which natural phenomena and seasons are presented as an allegory combining human figures and nature motifs.
f6e89e4ee34b1188328bb70764adb7446ae71f1a:

a sea of suffering: we have desires, but they do not
come true, everything is often the opposite of expectations, and
what finally comes out of it is also
complete nonsense."
9d20dca58f42bad55cc10a36affad01f072ef53b: the image consists of three separately printed surfaces — above a horizontal, bluish-green surface with red magical signs, below a dark-red strip of uneven width. 0175009aeb425b8e0d2ce11f16b53787449710c5: Erna Josephine von Deeters (1876-1961) was a Baltic German artist born in Latvia, who in the 1920s-30s was closely connected with Estonian art life, working as an art teacher in Tallinn and exhibiting at exhibitions. In Estonia she is known primarily as a creator of townscapes. Her legacy preserved in museum collections is scant, which is why this sketch-like female portrait is also an addition to her and, more broadly, to the work of Baltic German women artists in the EKM collection.

377b9da476610ceef995728b38d7d4235e75465b: Ede Raadik represents the younger generation of Estonian printmakers, who in her work has moved from traditional print techniques to digital printing, while retaining a certain graphic quality. Notable in Raadik's works is the presentation of situations related to the artist's personal life and work through complex algorithm-based yet elegant diagrams, which also grow into a treatment of broader current issues.

9cb8d9c04749b969b6e60d3873457782bba3d19a: A significant place in the oeuvre of the versatile artist Leonhard Lapin is occupied by a series of drawings made in the early 1970s, which deconstructs phenomena and signs of Western and (Soviet) Estonian culture. In its ironic, pop-like surrealist treatment, the drawing "Naer" ["Laughter"] (1972) complements well the works represented in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, such as "Linda leekides" ["Linda in Flames"], "Avatud Lee'd" ["Open Lee's"], "Pessaari universum" ["The Universe of the Pessary"], "MMM" (all 1972) and others.

ee914c4c502a255971f6810c9c7bcaa2d9895b9a: On the lid of an oval vessel is a fully modelled mythological creature – a hippocampus, a sea-horse with a horse's head and a fish's tail. d8e4c5e6da4e7d07dab670b04efd9328d6de55c9: The sketch is a preliminary work for Vive Tolli's 1960 print "Võrguparandajad eided" ["Old Women Mending Nets"]. According to the artist, the sketch was made on the beach at Toila; the quickly sketched, striking drawings characterise the artist's working style. The sketch also contains elements not found in the final work (a dog, men). The aquatint print "Võrguparandajad eided", created on the theme of the work of coastal dwellers, is an excellent example of Vive Tolli's early style of her time.

cc05b7f5e71250ab2f8f0c076886685dd83d3398: A complete portfolio acquired from the estate of the well-known Estonian graphic artist Berta Mäger (1918-1999), containing twenty-four caricatures from the years 1946-1968, includes witty portraits of the author's contemporaries, among them notable sculptors, painters, graphic artists and others. As such, Berta Mäger's series is a fine addition to the corresponding genre collection at the Art Museum of Estonia and will certainly find use, above all, in illustrating texts on cultural history.

fca651a75c5ac8e566b3c09451bc33df99ab6af7: "Milvi" – The work is an exceptional silkscreen portrait by Malle Leis. At the same time, the work also contains the interpretation of plant motifs characteristic of Malle Leis's silkscreen oeuvre, which links it to works already belonging to the EAM's graphic art collection.

d6f472c44e3fb5933ea9afb1d2a6628ec47c5532: Kaljo Põllu (1934-2010) was one of the legendary figures of Estonian culture. In this work the artist thinks in even larger categories than in the "Kodalased" series, which is devoted mainly to Finno-Ugric mythology.

468f4338e1623a532cb7e6f9c3472760863eb6ed: The lower part of the box is surrounded by a basket of relief oak leaves; the upper part is engraved with an ornamental band with ribbons and stylised plant decoration. The upper ends of the tall handles are formed as a relief fish tail. The lower edge of the oval foot is likewise surrounded by relief oak leaves. The foot rests on a rhombus-shaped base, which in turn rests on four hoofed legs. On the edge of the box a segment-shaped opening for a spoon.
c1c0b3c98458bc9572805058ffddd7f6e6a0e00a: Kristjan Raud's competition designs for the 1918 Estonian postage stamp competition complement well the artist's legacy in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, highlighting the versatility of his interests. Besides fine art, Kristjan Raud also worked in applied graphics, producing coat-of-arms, currency and stamp designs in his characteristic archaising style, thereby contributing to the shaping of the visual culture and identity of the young Republic of Estonia
040eb15e2d981837b16eada4c66d2e28b6e1f3b6: Around a table set parallel to the picture plane, thirteen men: in the foreground, four apostles with their backs to the viewer, two middle apostles facing the viewer, in the background on the other side of the table Christ and three apostles on either side of him. The apostles gesture wretchedly or are theatrically sunk in thought. The dim room is lit by four candles standing on the table, the figures cast shadows on the back wall.
9f97a0fda17f7ab2fb01e585670895464b5a37c1:

72f63e1c98432d0d62c7271ecef886faee50274e: Ado Vabbe (1892-1961), a developer of Estonian modernist art, head of the Pallas art school and its long-time lecturer, created the 1924 work "Tänavastseen, Pariis" ["Street Scene, Paris"], which belongs to the futurist period of his oeuvre. The watercolour's pair is the known work "Seine´i jõgi" ["The Seine River"]. "Tänavastseen, Pariis" is (evidently deliberately) unfinished, signed and dated, and a very valuable addition to the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.
a4eda362dc539c3e357a85f87b0c1542712e70c9: On the sheet, on the left and right, three rectangles, between them vertically three narrower rectangles, in which the depiction of a fountain repeats - in the upper rectangle against a black background, in the middle one against a light background, in the lower one in a black frame. The side rectangles are bordered with black and red contour lines, in the upper right rectangle a black diagonal stripe and below it, in the middle rectangle, a similar red one.

3b4be767ca8ccc8fa8addab471c3a71d210462fa: Kristjan Raud's oeuvre, inspired by folklore and ethnographic heritage, is one of the most important and distinctive phenomena of Estonian symbolist art. His works on the theme of Kalevipoeg belong among the seminal texts of Estonian art and national culture. The motif depicting the felling of the great oak is based on the sixth song of the epic "Kalevipoeg" and, as a finished composition, is rare among Raud's surviving works.
10ecde61660a4b5fe4d21960b06f596d1ca09241:
The artwork consists of three dialogues: the first video depicts
the artist, who has become alienated from the world as a result of several suicide attempts.
The second video shows the artist as an exchange student in England
doing dirty work. The third video shows a clockmaker who takes care
of large clock mechanisms. All three characters seek happiness
and identity, just as previous generations have done.
b1f41f30dca197ce8c2d02c87daf0fddb4bd0991:
On one sheet three drafts-studies:
at the top of the sheet on the right, in a square frame, a picture of the sea, in the foreground a man's head seen frontally, behind on the left a shore visible.
At the top of the sheet on the left a standing female figure dressed in brightly coloured clothing, on her head a hat with feathers, hands in a muff. Below the depiction of the woman: 1911 and a sketch of a hand.
At the bottom of the sheet, across the sheet, a lake, by which three male nudes stand talking to one another, all holding a stone
e63bd58020dc02903d5c5d23bbc9f59e8a4539ac:
A seated man with square-framed glasses, a house in his lap, a book in his hand, an angel figurine beside him. Below the depiction, text:
Art historian V.Raam has just announced a sensational find. At the Pirita convent, where student work-brigade volunteers, romping about, pried loose the piscina from its original position in the nuns' bricked-up wall niche, on the underside of which was carved an especially rare composition, the so-called Villem ise esimene, a fragment of which you see here.
f5e73b4ccc2a961a54699fb748a44cde3d94ca74:
A) A composition draft with a stage, at the edge of which sits a woman in black boots, hands behind her neck, in a half-turn to the left. On the left, in a half-turn facing back to the right, a woman sitting on a Vienna chair, feet raised onto the edge of the stage.
B) In a room, in whose back wall there are windows on the left and right, two seated nudes in a half-turn to the right, right leg crossed over the knee (in front a man, behind a woman). Behind, in the middle, a woman's torso seen frontally and a vase.
188ddf3f84bb08ffd7d045f697b7fc2da1777f81: Anu Kalm's works are a weighty contribution to the conceptualising of the mother's role in Estonian graphic art and in visual art more broadly. Expressive, sensitive and poetic drypoints testify to the liberation of Estonian graphic art during the period striving towards the restoration of independence. By emphasising humanity, empathy and tactility, these works acquire new significance from the viewpoint of today's so-called new materialism.
f3dcd900d58a76d3d160d1702067a0ee5a8ce6d8: A fragment of an interior filled with figures, with a window at the top left. In the foreground, a large depiction of a group at table, cut off by the picture edges so that only the head is visible of the man on the left, slurping soup, and of the man on the right, holding his hand in front of his mouth and wearing a top hat. Between them a third man sleeps face-down on the table, next to snuff. Further back another group of men at table, snuffing and wearing peaked caps, the head of a waitress.
9c02ad2e78abd99297d834f5519243de7be2e2b7: A tureen, its low foot and lid are decorated with winding vertical grooves. At the top of the lid a decorative, roundly modelled rosebud, at the lower part of whose stem relief leaves attach to the lid. At the joining point with the tureen of the heart-shaped handles, formed as plant stems, there are likewise relief plant leaves. The oval serving plate has a wavy, profiled edge, the heart-shaped handles imitate a plant stem.
dc5e5c8f83da5e43d05c4ab0c3fb1d87ae413aa2: On the left a man standing slightly bent forward, in profile facing right, in his right hand a pan with two flaming rolled pancakes, which he holds above the table. On the right a man and a woman sitting in a half-turn to the left, the man's head in profile facing left. The standing figure is shown as a half-figure, the seated ones as quarter-figures, partly left undepicted. In the background, over low wood panelling, the heads of more people are visible in profile facing left.
879571ed0424220e5da1dc9d920575d4f3ab39e5: A massive table, on which a decanter, a book, drawings and Popov's radio system. At the table, on a chair, left leg crossed over the right, sits an admiral thoughtfully looking at the radio system, to whose left stands Popov pointing with his left hand at his radio system. At the lower edge of the sheet a red stamp with a portrait of Popov. The depiction is supplemented by text in red: "Aleksander Popov tutvustab oma raadisüsteemi admiral Makarovile" ["Aleksander Popov presents his radio system to Admiral Makarov"]
7769ff269ddf1d0cb2dffe3c9aa8f3f04b0b178d: A street corner in Montparnasse. In the foreground a two-storey red corner house, in whose doorway a female figure stands. In the right part of the house a street café with a couple sitting at a table. In the middle ground taller buildings, on whose end walls advertisements: "Pâtes alimentaires" (with a moon peeking at a plate) and "Cinzano" (with a horseman). The backgrounds of the advertisements are blue. Over everything a yellow sky. At top right an airplane, at bottom left a car.
ee1a8ea36d3547efef38dbd204a9baa5d73458c1:
A man in a hat behind a table, behind him a female figure. On the table a globe, radishes and a rabbit figure and a sign: Radishes grown by K.Jermakoff. Below the depiction, text:
Mihkel Mutt, junior researcher of the Kalle Jermakoff Writing-Desk Museum, is moved by a rare exhibit, a globe with which K.J. was struck on the head, and which was now donated to the museum by Lucrezia Wörtzjerv, an internationally known researcher of K.J.'s oeuvre.
40d2c6a42d3502ec035f8002a955963f8f8030d5: Assessment by Kaisa Puustak (pre-registration no. 2024:0101): The work was created based on the author's travel impressions from Canada and complements well the small but distinctive and expressive, technically masterful examples of Kaisa Puustak's oeuvre in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, which convincingly renders Soviet everyday reality through hyperrealism and visual estrangement. The EKM collection also includes the work's pair, "Kõrghoone II" ["High-Rise II"].
ccf2e16284e8cddcfdbc6f8f2bce3d3c21e00b19: A bust portrait of Kaljula Aru painted in oil colours on Finnish cardboard, the background of the painting is in green tones. Kaljula Aru is depicted wearing glasses, dressed in white and green tones, with a red and black tie, with a cigarette in his right hand. Nails have been driven into the back of the wooden frame, painted white, between which the painting is fastened. In the upper left corner of the painting the artist's signature and the year.
1b9eb27d09904961ad2c1b72da47caa0c99ee6cc: Against a turquoise-blue background, a young woman seated in frontal view behind a raspberry-red tabletop, her right hand resting on a support in front, her left under her chin. The woman has dark hair combed back in a bun at the nape, she is wearing a rust-brown, long-sleeved closed garment, on her shoulders a light-based crinkled shawl or vest. The contour lines of the hair and hand, and the cross hanging on her neck, are scratched into the paint surface. The paper surface is partly left uncovered.
aba31f5aae232e9b10e69e60bd82bba8cd72ad1a: The basis of the installation is M. Laarman's original painting "Laud" ["Table"] (1928, TKM 48). The author has digitally processed the image of the original, changing the anonymous boxes on the table into a Marlboro cigarette pack and a Kalev eagle matchbox. The composition of the painting is unchanged. The resulting slide has been reduced in size, fixed with adhesive film onto acrylic glass. In the light box there are 2 bulbs, the wire lacks a plug/socket. (Liina Tiitsmaa 10.01.1997)
3b396bfaa8cefb88635364ea8c27b70ffe8e4cf6: In an interior, in front on the left, a three-quarter figure of a man sitting in front of an easel, a palette in his lap, brushes in his left fist. 0889ede3b4e0f80f8cded319851b0952b36b7171: Maara Vint (b. 1955) has developed within the sphere of influence of her artist brothers Tõnis and Toomas Vint and sisters-in-law Mare and Aili Vint. Her pictorial world is recognisably individual; clearly legible, linear works express an aesthetic worldview. Maara Vint's drawings are hermetic, filled with various symbols and mythological motifs from nature, Buddhist religion, etc.

75161934a9cbb4bf085a629b2de5bd378265ebcd: The watercolour attests to the excellent drawing talent and individual style of the then only 17-year-old Natalie Mei, showing her already at that time as a mature artist. The lights reflecting on the water surface have an era-typical metropolitan and modern effect. For Natalie Mei, born into a high-ranking naval officer's family and having lived for years in Tallinn's Miinisadam, harbour views certainly had a personal meaning.

733e26947959d5ef52b188b7e18230df39757b99: The geometrically pure minimalism of Leonhard Lapin's graphic art refers to Lapin's experience as an architect. The work "Machine-Architecture IX" reflects the author's relationship to the innovative architectural thought and heritage of the 20th century - connecting both with the radical aesthetics of constructivism and with Le Corbusier's concept of the "house-machine", this composition generalises the phenomenon of the building as a graphic sign or formula.

a9862ac3e4ca99cf31af23699d35a8d885305fb9: The woodcuts and linocuts of the 1930s, primarily known through the works of Eduard Wiiralt, Arkadio Laigo, Hando Mugasto and Paul Liivak, were joined in the latter half of the decade by the work of Richard Sagrits, with its distinctive and painterly treatment. Since the artist made few prints from his plates, his graphic legacy from this period is very modestly represented in Estonian museums.
934f108f363736dae99377c2349f12c30529d64a: Aino Bach's (1901-1980) monotype from 1938 is a good addition to the collection of works from the high period of this Pallas school graphic artist's oeuvre in the Art Museum of Estonia. In her graphic work, mainly in aquatint technique, the author often dealt with depicting groups of women and young girls. Such is also this exceptionally black-and-white monotype, showing a nocturnal or evening interior with two people.

The man stands, lighting a pipe, the woman sits, holding in her raised right hand a beer tankard. On the road five figures. Behind on the left a rising sun disc, on which the number 3. 8a119d88df7147f15d425b00747d9c70c20b12a7:

6f86a359c007c2d1b79f588883f35d0e916b641d: Salome Trei, born in Kuressaare, studied graphic art in Tallinn at the State School of Applied Arts from 1929-1934 and completed the school's 6-year course cum laude, then continued her studies in Tartu at Pallas, which she completed in the 1939 graduating class. These watercolours belong to the early period of Trei's oeuvre, being, in the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia, among the few examples of Trei's studies at the State School of Applied Arts.
0d27643488b679ec40bc8cea9ee302eb325028ee: At the representative exhibition of Estonian exile art held in 2010-2011 at the Art Museum of Estonia and the Tartu Art Museum, both museums received a substantial addition to their collections of Estonian art abroad, mostly in the form of gifts. Nine paintings and two collages by Ville Tops acquired from this exhibition supplement the rather sparse collection of Estonian art abroad, both of the artist's and of the Art Museum of Estonia's.

60f05407e9953544395fd1aa943196b7d72bea25: Leonhard Lapin's graphic series "Processes" ["Protsessid"], created in the years 1980-1993, consists of at least 35 different sheets. The prints in lithography technique were preceded by drawings, prototypes. One of these is "Process III" ["Protsess III"]. The series' geometrically pure minimalism refers to the author's architectural thinking and experience, but also to L. Lapin's deep attachment to the problematics of emptiness and space.

Väino Tõnisson's (1925-1991) free graphic prints characterise the artist quite well, serving as a supplement to the overview of his work in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.
Themes of the sea, harbour, island dwellers etc. are typical of Soviet-era Estonian graphic art, as is the generalising, angular and black-and-white treatment. Väino Tõnisson was also known as an exlibris artist and illustrator.
6ec637ff411e3ee4d932eddf7fa7650589b30a34: The sheet depicts six workmen having their lunch break amid various construction materials. 0c4bb591fea0c06a96e0a94a21c90d8370db49c4: Henno Arrak's etching "Uudised punastest lippudest" ["News of Red Flags"] is rather an exception in the artist's work. It treats the theme of revolution, favoured in Soviet art, in a rather timeless and detached manner, bringing a moment of estrangement to the treatment of the historical event. With its unusual interpretation this work is a good addition to the so-called history-painting genre in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia.

a002fa9480be347b087c66fe6a3aef12c2ebd2df: A legendary series on the theme of the forest, an important Estonian symbol and resource, which Leonhard Lapin has been working on since 1994. In 1994 he presented the first work of the series, "Eesti mets I" ["Estonian Forest I"], at the São Paulo Biennial, being together with Jaan Toomik the first Estonians to take part in this exhibition. The latest, "Eesti mets VI" ["Estonian Forest VI"], was exhibited in August 2017 at the Tartu Art House.
de88f5ae38b509df9dd98e126868b0092c9d8f85:
Illustration for the book "Les procédés originaux d'illustration. La gravure sur cuivre et l'impression en tailledouce.", published in Paris in 1951.
On a table covered with a checked cloth, on the left a vase with a handle containing dahlias, around it various fruits. Behind on the right a goblet filled with wine and the edge of a striped curtain. Below on the right, as a separate element, a hand with an apple.
ce4a5190dbe7b9a627a35383487655508592381b: The work belongs to a folder of sketches arranged by Märt Laarmann (6 notebooks). The drawings and engravings are preparatory works for Fr. Tuglas's "Väike Illimar" ["Little Illimar"]. One notebook contains 46 different sketches, of which 5 photographs have been uploaded to Muis. Depicted are: lamp 4, masks 3, geese 6, house 3, spruces 8, fish 5, sap birch 3, bridge 2, funeral 1, church 2, sailboats 5, Tartu Stone Bridge on 4 sketches
b7e89dd5c366c7ae11dd6702903e6114fa54dc80: In the middle, large, two dancing figures facing each other, both with open mouths, arms raised. On the left a standing figure with an open mouth and raised arms. Above, against a white background, a reclining figure in a purple tone.
377d0ecb457243e15d2161c3a0aa21f1b2231331: In the middle of a stylised flower-shaped bowl a relief palmette, at the junction of the bowl and the stem cast plant leaves are attached. At the end of the wooden stem a bone knob. The stem of one spoon has been repaired. The exact purpose of the spoons is not clear, but the thin wooden stem suggests that they were used for lifting something hot yet relatively light (e.g. sauce, broth or dessert).

Publisher - "Amis de la Tradityion", authors: Paul Durupt and Robert Failliot. Printed by Priester Frères. Print run 1100, this copy no. 2.
81ecaef629e32628e3535aedfc942be6e005c77e: Drawing played a very important role in Sooster's art, functioning as a creative laboratory for experimenting with various methods, ideas and imagery. In doing so he used his experience of illustrating scientific literature to enrich the language of his creative works, where non-artistic imagery - models of substances and space, graphs and diagrams - inspired conceptual artistic discoveries.
cf44a26697a731abcd1336bfde3869ebadd01b73:

To the right of the tree, behind, a male figure playing the cello, a view of a castle wall, and above the heads a fantastic armoured creature, on whose back a skeleton rider

e50370be0dc6f1721d31e0467d5161423edcedeb: The paintings and graphic works added to the museum collection come from the art collection of the former Forekspank, established in 1998, immediately after the completion of the bank building on Narva maantee. The architects of the building, Jüri Okas and Marika Lõoke, whose modern bank building interior was awarded the Cultural Endowment's architecture prize, played a leading role in the selection of the works exhibited there.
1f3e5650a2b606c7cb2ba0aaf2a944ab33067cd8: In the left part of the sheet a man in bast shoes, leaning slightly forward, facing left, arms spread, with a bushel measure on his left hip. 34564599f953599865bb9c5b988b85d66b041497: Marje Taska's early ink drawings are exciting evidence of the formation of the artist's distinctive style at the beginning of her creative career. In the works "Mürgimaod" ["Poisonous Snakes"] and "Must bassein" ["Black Pool"], which seemingly deal with purely aesthetic and philosophical problems, a closer look reveals a sense of oppression running through totalitarian society, even sharp criticism of Soviet power.
29b430f10990708aa28adab498c630f56a006c4a: Two parts of the work attached to the base sheet: above, a rectangle in the printed section and a woodcut on Japanese paper with an ornamental strip (49.8x49.5 cm). Above, a pale blue rectangle with flowing contours, below it a dark green and blue band with a floral ornament. Below, a small print (18.6x15.4 cm, plate mark 14.9x12.4 cm), in the centre of which a lattice-like figure, upper right and lower left a unicorn.
807d49d645c3fc1a84e1fa778a9ac2780809a809:
A woman with a hat stepping to the right, wearing heeled shoes and a dress, in her left hand, in front, a cat held by the tail. Behind the woman a sad-looking creature. Composition in a rectangle, below which the author's text:
This dynamic lady in this picture is, according to B. Bernstein's studies, the most feminine Estonian female graphic artist Silvi Liiva, whom you see walking on the ethereally thin thread of the real and the unreal.
844c630d7e78909668cbadc4f32e62449db38a32:
1. Nature. North-Estonian coast. On the left some trees, a bay inlet and boulders, a high cliff coast, a farmhouse and some trees.

3. History. On the left an Estonian horseman charging with a raised sword against a knight.
4. Two cavalry forces fighting, horsemen with lowered lances rushing at one another.

A) In the lower part of the sheet a sketch of four female nudes in a landscape, between two groups of trees. Upper left two seated female nudes under a tree, to the right of them a paler sketch of a standing female nude.
B) Sketch of a female nude (knee-length figure, seated) holding a child in her lap. The latter typical of Viiralt's work of this period - large-eyed, chubby-cheeked, one hand on the mother's left hand, the other on the mother's breast.
c0f9991085dfdf858a43239b3f2f6c400cccf4a3: The ceramic portrait head of Konstantin Päts is a copy, rendered in ceramic material, of Ferdi Sannamees's portrait of Päts created in the 1930s, one of the variants of which was indeed a bronze head cut off below the neck on a granite base. The ceramic version is considerably cheaper in price and evidently also, being mountable on a more modest base, a so-called budget variant of the head of state's portrait bust.
f9c94a1055acc382b5d9a31f680b41bd30a77d51:
A) Two standing female nudes, the left one sketched in outline, the right one worked out more with coloured pencils. The left nude in a half-turn to the right, hands crossed on the chest. The right one frontal, arms raised.
B) Seated female nude in profile to the right, head slightly turned to the right, resting on the right hand. Left leg drawn under, right leg stretched forward.

across the sheet various scenes and figures: upper left a man kneeling by a female sculpture, on the right a standing man with a torch and a sword, towards whom a crowd is moving.

5e90327b163148468f9f012566a26be33b83e0b1: Leonhard Lapin's reaction to the action - Tartu as the new capital of Estonia - at the turn of the millennium. The artist has printed approximately 300 identical cards with Tartu motifs. 154 of them belong to the installation held at the Tartu Art Museum. According to Lapin, the cards can be displayed in different ways. Presumably because every sign can indeed be presented in different ways.
e4bce404d78f7b737d2dde6ce9b159992ee68719:
A man with a bow tie putting a ring on a girl's finger, with the text:
Those are mistaken who consider this Hollywood-like scene to have been slyly slipped into "Sirp" by H. Valk in order to lull the editorial board's vigilance. No! The drawing has a deeply scientific value and in it we see our most famous naiadologist com. E. Vetemaa ringing a water-sprite, "the courting warbler," in the reeds of Lake Endla.
3f426060990d7a1750f335340af8f9fb2ae4713e: A tall cylindrical jug is covered with hemispherical bosses, with birds engraved on the flat surfaces between them. In the centre of the convex lid is a coin dating from 1629 - a thaler of the Elector of Saxony Johann Georg I (1611-1656). The jug's handle is adorned with a row of little balls, at the lower part of the handle there is a shield left blank. The base is articulated with oval cartouches bordered by acanthus leaves.
819b7bb06fb49135fca7f26c5003e60fbd4c67b7: Tõnis Laanemaa (1937), who belonged to the group ANK' 64 active in Tallinn 1964-1969, remains an active artist to this day. The three early etchings are typical examples of Laanemaa's style, based on associations, emotionally readable. Among the graphic artists of his generation, Laanemaa stands out for turning to social themes, which relate to the upheavals in society.
facc4cba4f836a70e13c61862be792d1ba53f2db: A black screen, the rumble of a train. Gradually a window opens, then a quickly passing landscape is shown. Finally the sea - this image is no longer through the window. The roar of the sea, sunset. Then the image turns white and it ends.

4bb199a0139ca4f6a7d10dc423691fdbfd2062ed: Terje Ojaver (b. 1955) is an artist and art pedagogue. In 1985 she graduated from the Sculpture Department of the Estonian SSR State Art Institute, after which she actively joined the local art scene. She has a firm place among the strongest Estonian female artists, and a characteristic feature of her work is a relief-like female position and environmental awareness in a distinctive humorous manner.

The strikingly large and effective pattern of the background creates a strong decorative effect. The tablecloth and background are painted with long, dabbing brushstrokes.

A diligent researcher of the cradle days of Estonian art, Mr Voldemar Erm, at his

d144b02c22f8cd3aa055e1fcc310170fafeabd96: Tõnis Vind's large-scale gouache composition is the only known surviving example of the artist's experiments in this format, which at the same time continues the author's characteristic visual system. It relates to the lithographs from the series "Q" and "White Houses" held in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia, with one of which it forms a larger inter-medial whole.
a0e7ad76f61771a491ab6de79a501ef04f2323dd:
The interior of the Rosen Chapel in St. Nicholas' Church, in the middle of the room a monument with a glass sarcophagus.
The doors of the chapel were the decorative wall of the Rosen Chapel, which is currently located in the tower room of St. Nicholas' Church. The chapel has not survived, it was a small room located at the site of the current staircase in the eastern part of the North Sacristy. The windows in the background have survived and are the same. 
Data by Merike Kurisoo

f1516fdab02c2e071272d436d9a6a81f75776013: Karl von Kügelgen's 15-sheet series of views of Finland, executed in a novel lithographic technique, represented the first published voyage pittoresque of views of Finland. The series is very rare in Estonia and examples of it have so far been absent from EAM's print collection, which is why this sheet is a relevant addition to the other works by Kügelgen in the existing collection.
5bf44df0dccaa1b149e76eac3884bad5fad50dad: In the interior, in the foreground at the bottom left a female nude sitting on the floor and drawing, seen in profile, legs to the right; behind on the right a female nude leaning on a carpet and cushions, seen frontally, upper body tilted to the right, in the raised left hand a goblet. c64ba551a0f3b7ec7a7ee331ab858551da5189c8: Raul Meel's serigraph series "Windows and Landscapes", created in the second half of the 1980s, is a notable reflection by the author on the closedness of the Soviet Union and the limitation of artistic freedom. The two sheets in question from the monumental series are so far, as far as is known, unrepresented in Estonian museums, which is why they are a good addition to the existing set.

560aa7efea0088c248163a87371413ef2efc3650: The present work is remarkable both for its interesting technical execution and its witty treatment of the motif, which is psychologically expressive and reflects, among other things, the post-World War II situation in Western society. 0ce6918aaf4f9581de00c9cb8b8ed34737f5983e: Paul Saar (1946-2007) was a painter active in Tartu. He studied at the Tartu Art School under the guidance of Pallas-graduate Alfred Kongo. Alongside his creative work he worked for 27 years as a pedagogue at the Tartu Children's Art School.

Loit Jõekalda is a notable Estonian graphic artist and organiser of graphic-art life, whose work is characterised by explorations of imagery and often also experiments with little-used graphic techniques.
His prints based on photographic images are an expressive example of the rivalry of the photography and graphic art of his time, but also of the dialogue between the two artistic media.

3e7bc277c09ce852dc1ed720a23c0ecacb049aa8: Kristjan Raud's work, inspired by folklore and ethnographic heritage, is one of the most important and distinctive phenomena of Estonian symbolist art. 4bbe55706c5bd87532f21f7432907de49372341a:
A man dressed in black with a hat behind a seated blonde woman. Text below the image:
Using demonic methods, Mati Unt staged a lunar eclipse in Kalamaja to illuminate the inner life of a certain woman. According to Unt, he does such work "simply by living". However, it should be checked what kind of living that is.
be59b90d223822d4016bc6094712bd34911ab900:
A small man in a dark suit pushing a colossal seated man in an armchair. Text on the image:
The swivel chair of Eugen Jannsen, set spinning on the stage of the Drama Theatre by Mikk Mikiver, has now, together with Heino Mandre, spun on several continents and for so long that it raises suspicions of circumventing the laws of setting things in motion.
e84b0acf3a82effb5ba70f40f531a2b240006ef6:
A) On an irregular surface, at the top right, the head of a long-haired, bearded old man in a half-turn to the left. A smoking pipe in his mouth, gaze lowered. 65689a2feacc0113b1c6729949c4ebca046769c0:
A jug with a lid "Bear in the Beehive".

Vermäcktniss von Fr. Siefarth 19 27/IV 07.
On the lower rim of the jug and to the left of the handle a high-relief plant ornament.
On the bottom a maker's mark KA.
869c40eae37a9e1d2f10aa011e195d3b5b7a0f75: Half-portrait of a little girl, the girl's head turned slightly towards the right shoulder, gaze to the left side, wearing a blouse with a round collar and long sleeves, on her head a simple cap with a turned-up brim, hands placed crossed, a bracelet on the wrist of the right hand. Inscriptions at the lower left in black pencil. EK 42/170.
958c163917d033656164fa2d6289f00dcb6dbc5a: In a garden, in the center a round table, whose leg is formed of a vertically winding snake and plants. On the table a small vase with flowers, a pen and an envelope. Behind the table on the left, on a chair, a young reading woman in profile to the right, on her head a small human figure. The chair legs are of winding snake and plants. Behind, plants.
faab37fd1ac673912c5e49c1c872d0d4d518ad33: In an interior, behind a small, round covered table, a grotesque man and woman facing each other, pushing against one another. The man has on his head a bird pierced with a nail through its wing, the woman has on her head a fish and in her raised right hand a hammer ready to strike. To her left the figure of a seated man, head slightly turned to the right. In the background six female nudes. At the bottom center of the sheet the head of a man slightly turned to the left.

A man with tousled hair and beard, a book under his arm. Behind him a reclining female nude. Text below the image:
Enn Põldroos hopes that good spirits will protect him from critics who seek symbols or parables in the depiction of the female figure in his works. So the maker of this picture will not go looking for them in Enn's works either.

9690f6c9a59618f27fb1cdac71c2b5155d55255a: The early watercolours of the well-known Estonian painter and theatre artist Roman Nyman (1881-1951) date from his period of study in St. Petersburg at the Stieglitz School of Art (1900-1906). In the collection of the Art Museum of Estonia, Nyman's school works supplement the overview of the lesser-known early stage and formative years of the artist's oeuvre.
d9791618d954ef1cd853c098d61d9b83b2783db4: In the upper half of the sheet a female figure sitting on the ground in half-profile to the left, hands crossed in the lap, legs bent at the knees parallel to the left, below a female figure lying on her back with head to the left, right hand raised holding an elongated object in the palm, legs bent and slightly raised, right hand on the ground, against the side
4bd226081ff66808bbd7066816aef61600015aed: In the foreground center left a female figure with a headscarf and a long skirt in profile to the right, pouring water from a bucket hanging from a well-sweep into a barrel, from which a horse is drinking. 58a65bf34eeea7896f8cf7dd04cf091ef560a5e1: The work of Visvaldis Ziedinš (1942-2007), which has become known to a wider public only in recent years, is a rare example of Baltic Soviet-period nonconformist art. The works belonging to the EKM collection date from the 1960s, one of the most fruitful periods in the artist's oeuvre.
240ab965c318c7abb913b1fffb93046fff52af0d: The "Tallinn Declaration", made in intaglio printing technique, i.e. as an original print, is as important a document in the history of Estonian environmental protection as it is a recognition of the cooperation between conservationists and artists in this field, and it is also an interesting example of Urmas Ploomipuu's activity in the field of applied graphic art.
bceadabef4726fbc9041fb2dd7ff9db9656ee158: In the foreground on the left a bust of a dictator wearing a uniform, the man's screaming face turned towards the viewer, gaze directed somewhere into the distance, in front of the dictator three soldiers' heads are visible, surrounded by a crowd, human faces expressing various emotions. Ott Ojamaa vahendusel meieni jõudnud lugu
kaitstud meestest tugevdas eesti naiste kartusi

df204a59daa8ad3716e90ae83a9bf9a06bef260d: In the foreground on the left a small body of water, which a rider on a black horse is crossing towards the viewer, on the right a white horse behind them, a crow on the bank. 9117b75dc9aa663f44bffcd94f206f776e077fcc: Tea service: teapot, sugar bowl, sweets basket. The wavy body of the pot is divided by vertical ridges into eight oval fields. The handle and the lid knob are of bone.

In the foreground on the right a table, on which a knobbed vase with flowers.
d3dd12e979f71560963544d60b57037b14e3cc21: "A Short Emblematic History" is a series of pictorial emblems marking long historical periods. These are signs, already imprinted in the memory of every Estonian from primary school textbooks, of the Estonians' history and identity, which the artist presents as an assembled puzzle from which some pieces have gone missing.
3b211f19b98f7a90b72ec780bbf58d8e395c07aa: Illustration for the second scene of the second act. On the left a young man in a monk's robe, in his left hand pressed to his chest a cross, his right hand outstretched to take a dagger. Beside him a priest-monk with a cruel expression (Alobrand), who with his right hand embraces the young man's shoulders and, looking him in the eye, hands him a dagger with his left hand.
94c5fb774332d7a5bc37b942db193ecb66bda623: In reddish tones a wide landscape with isolated dark grey, red and white spruce silhouettes. Below, on a separate narrow, horizontal plate, greenish-blue, flat mountains.

On the right edge a rectangular stove, almost reaching the ceiling, with two doors. Through the doorway another room is visible.

6d0b8da3bdb535598aed5bae963ac1435a508528: The jug stands on three gilded balls held between eagle's claws. On the lid the coat of arms of the Burchart Belavary de Sycava family. de449c67566ea7bc0abb102a23aa752548b5651d: Marje Üksi's early graphic series differs in its visual language from the artist's works of later creative periods, representing a unique artistic experiment. Its value also lies in its coherent treatment of imagery and themes, which continue in the graphic art of both Üksi and her like-minded contemporaries later on.

Above, text: TAARIKANN TAMMUNA k. SAAREMAALT IAMMALT. KANNUKÕRV do.
b775e71672cf1a441bf88b9d2f36d3ae877b61cb: Kalli Kalde's print series "Cosmic maze" is inspired by Estonia's first satellite, ESTCube. The artist is fascinated by the aesthetics of the device's technical schemes, as well as by the associations they evoke with traditional sign systems, such as those woven into our delicate mitten patterns.
